# DataWorks User Guide 20260629

## What is DataWorks?

DataWorks, formerly known as Big Data Development Suite, is a one-stop platform for intelligent big data development and governance. It is built on compute engines such as MaxCompute and E-MapReduce (EMR). DataWorks provides a comprehensive suite of tools for data integration, development, governance, services, quality control, and security. DataWorks provides a one-stop solution for the entire data lifecycle, from data collection and presentation to analysis and application development. It supports offline processing, analysis, and data mining of massive amounts of data. DataWorks also integrates core data processes, such as data integration, data development, production operations and maintenance (O&M), real-time analysis, asset management, data quality, data security, and data sharing. Additionally, DataWorks provides DataService Studio and an online development platform for Machine Learning Platform for Artificial Intelligence (PAI). In 2018, the analytics firm Forrester ranked the DataWorks and MaxCompute solution second in the world among cloud data warehouses. It was the only Chinese product to be included in the evaluation. DataWorks V2.0 builds on V1.0 by adding business flows and components. This version improves the data development system by supporting dual-project development, isolating development and production environments, enforcing development standards, and reducing code errors. map Data Asset discovery/Asset Metadata parsing/Data Resource optimization

### Create a workspace

A workspace is the basic unit in DataWorks for managing tasks, members, roles, and permissions. All development work is performed in a workspace. Therefore, you must create a workspace before you can develop tasks. A MaxCompute project has been created.

**Note**

You must create a compute engine to initialize the MaxCompute project. You can then bind this compute engine when you create the workspace. When you create a workspace, you can use preset templates provided by DataWorks to create one or more environments, such as development, testing, staging, and production. DataWorks can also automatically create associations between workspaces, which establishes a one-to-many relationship between a department and its workspaces. DataWorks workspaces are available in simple mode and standard mode:
**Simple mode**: This mode has only a production environment and corresponds to a single
project. It does not provide data permission isolation or separate development and production environments.
**Standard mode**: This mode includes both development and production environments.
These environments can correspond to two separate projects for better isolation and data security.

**Note**

Standard mode is recommended for task development.

**Procedure**

1. As a tenant administrator, log on to the DataWorks console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > More >**
**Organization Management** to navigate to the **Workspace List** page.
3. On the Workspace list page, click **Create a workspace** in the upper-right corner.
4. In the **Create Workspace** dialog box, configure the basic information.

| Administrator | Select an administrator from the drop-down list. You can filter by username or UID. |
|---|---|
| Mode | The following modes are supported: Simple mode (single environment) Standard mode (development and production environment isolation) If you set Mode to Standard mode, you must associate the workspace with two MaxCompute projects. |
| Description | Enter a brief description of the workspace for easy identification. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Start scheduling cycle | You can enable and set scheduling cycles as needed. If this feature is disabled, auto triggered tasks in this workspace no longer automatically generate instances or run on a schedule. Existing instances are not affected and can run as normal. If this feature is enabled, the workspace automatically generates instances based on the node settings. |
| Allow download of SELECT results | You can download SELECT results and configure the corresponding settings. If this feature is disabled, you cannot download data from the results of SELECT queries. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| MaxCompute project name | From the drop-down list, select a MaxCompute project that you have created. |
| MaxCompute access identity | Alibaba Cloud account and Task owner are supported. As needed, select an account type to use for running task code in MaxCompute. |

5. Configure the **Advanced Settings**.
6. Configure the settings for MaxCompute.
7. Click **Confirm**.
After the workspace is created, you can refresh the workspace list to view the new workspace. You can also **Configure**, **Enter Workspace**, **Disable**, or **Delete** the workspace.

## Quick Start

### Overview

Quick Start guides you through a complete process of data analytics and O&M. Generally, you can complete the following data analytics and O&M operations in a workspace of DataWorks:
1. Create tables and import data.
2. Create a workflow.
3. Create a sync node.
4. Configure recurrence and dependencies for a node.
5. Run a node and troubleshoot errors.
The following figure shows the basic process of data analytics and O&M.

### Create tables and upload data

**Note**

The bank_data table stores business data, and the result_table table stores data analytics results. A workspace is created. For more information, see Create a workspace.

**Create the bank_data table**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > Data Development**
**and O&M > DataStudio**. The **DataStudio** page appears.

### Create a workflow

This topic describes how to create and configure a workflow in DataWorks, including how to create a workflow, add nodes, configure dependencies between nodes, and run and debug the nodes. After you create a workflow, you can use the DataStudio service to analyze and compute data in your workspace. The `bank_data` table for storing business data and the `result_table` table for storing data analytics results are created in the workspace. Data is imported to the bank_data table. For more information, see Create tables and upload data.

**Background information**

The DataStudio service of DataWorks allows you to visually configure node dependencies in a workflow by dragging and dropping nodes. You can process data and define dependencies by building and managing the workflow.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console. In the upper part of the page, go to the DataWorks
workspace that you want to manage.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click the
pointer over **Create** and select **Create Workflow**.
3. In the **Create Workflow** dialog box, configure the **Workflow Name** and **Description**
parameters.
4. Click **Create**.

**Create nodes and configure dependencies between nodes.**

**Note**

Take note of the following items when you use a zero load node: A zero load node is a control node that is used to maintain and control its descendant nodes in a workflow. A zero load node does not generate data. If other nodes depend on a zero load node and the zero load node is set to the Failed state by O&M engineers, the pending descendant nodes cannot run. During the O&M process, a zero load node can be disabled to prevent incorrect data of ancestor nodes from being obtained by their descendant nodes. In most cases, the root node of the workspace is used as the ancestor node of a zero load node in a workflow. The root node of a workspace is named in the format

```
of Workspace name_root .
```

When you design a workflow, we recommend that you create a zero load node as the root node of the workflow to control the entire workflow.
1. On the Scheduled Workflow pane, double-click the name of the workflow that you created
below Business Flow, and choose General > **Create Node**.
2. Click **Zero-Load Node**. You can also drag **Zero-Load Node** to the canvas on the right
side.
3. In the **Create Node** dialog box, set the **Node Name** parameter to `start` and click
**Confirm**.
4. Use the same method to create an **ODPS SQL** node named `insert_data` .
5. Drag a line from the start node to the insert_data node to configure the `start` node as
the ancestor node of the `insert_data` node.

**Configure the ancestor node of the zero load node**

In a workflow, a zero load node is often used to control the entire workflow and serves as the ancestor node of all nodes in the workflow. In most cases, the zero load node in a workflow depends on the root node of the workspace.
1. Double-click the `start` node. In the right-side navigation pane of the configuration tab,
click the **Properties** tab.
2. In the **Dependencies** section of the Properties tab, click **Add Root Node** to configure the
root node of the workspace as the ancestor node of the zero load node.

**Note**

In addition to the scheduling dependencies, you must also configure other required parameters, such as **Rerun** and **Resource Group**. icon in the top toolbar to save the node. This section describes how to use SQL code in the ODPS SQL node `insert_data` to query the number of singles who have different education levels and have mortgage loans and save the query result. The descendant nodes can use the query result to analyze or present data.
1. Double-click the workflow name to go to the canvas.
2. Double-click the ODPS SQL node `insert_data` to go to the editing page.
3. In this example, the following SQL statement is executed:

```
INSERT OVERWRITE TABLE result_table -- Insert data into the result_table table.
    , COUNT(marital) AS num
FROM bank_data WHERE housing = 'yes'
    AND marital = 'single'
```

4. Click the **Properties** tab in the right-side navigation pane. Configure the **Rerun** parameter
in the **Schedule** section and the **Resource Group** parameter in the Resource Group section.
5. In the top toolbar of the `insert_data` node, click the **Save** icon to save the code.
1. Double-click the workflow name to go to the canvas. Find the `insert_data` node and
double-click it to go to the editing page.
2. In the top toolbar of the `insert_data` node, click **Run**. After the node is run, you can view
the operation logs and results.

**Commit the workflow**

1. After you run and debug the ODPS SQL node `insert_data` , return to the workflow editing
page and click **Submit**.
2. In the **Commit** dialog box, select the nodes to be committed ( `start` and `insert_data` ),
enter a description in the **Change Description** field, and then select **Ignore I/O**
**Inconsistency Alerts**.
3. Click **Confirm**.

**What to do next**

You have learned how to create and commit a workflow. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In the next tutorial, you will learn how to create a synchronization node to export data to different types of data sources. For more information, see Create a synchronization node.

### Create a synchronization node

This topic describes how to create and configure a batch synchronization node in Data Integration to periodically synchronize data from MaxCompute to a MySQL database. You can add data sources, create destination tables, configure synchronization nodes, and commit synchronization nodes to migrate and synchronize data in an efficient and stable manner.

**Background information**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ) and must start with a letter. _ |
| Environment | The environment for which your workspace is used. This parameter appears only when you use a workspace in standard mode. You can select Development or Production. |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Configuratio n Mode | The mode in which the data source is added. Set this parameter to Connection String Mode. |
| Connection Address | Host IP Address: the host IP address of the destination MySQL database. Port Number: the port number of the MySQL database. |
| Database Name | The name of the MySQL database that you want to access. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |

You can use Data Integration to periodically synchronize the business data that is generated in a business system to a DataWorks workspace. You can create SQL nodes to compute the data and use Data Integration to periodically synchronize the computing results to your specified data source for further display or use. A workflow is created. For more information, see Create a workflow.

**Note**

Only the workspace administrator can add data sources. Members of other roles can only view data sources.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console, click the
icon in the upper-left corner, and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**. The **Data Integration** page
appears.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**. On the **Data Sources** page, click
**Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **MySQL**.
4. In the **Add MySQL Data Source** dialog box, configure the parameters. In this example, a
MySQL data source is added in **Connection String Mode**.

| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
|---|---|

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, find the resource group for Data Integration
that is associated with the workspace and click **Test Network Connectivity** in the
**Connection Status** column.
6. After you pass the connectivity test, click **Complete Creation**.

**Create a table in the destination MySQL database**

Create the **odps_result** table in the ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL database to which the data is synchronized. You can create the table by executing the following statement:

```
CREATE TABLE `ODPS_RESULT` ( `education` varchar(255) NULL , `num` int(10) NULL );
```

After the table is created, execute the DESC odps_result; statement to view the table details.

**Create and configure a batch synchronization node**

This section describes how to create and configure a batch synchronization node named `write_result` and use the node to synchronize data in the `result_table` table to a MySQL data source. Perform the following steps:
1. In the upper-left corner of the console, click the
icon and choose **All Products > Data**
**Development and O&M > DataStudio**. The **DataStudio** page appears.
2. In the top navigation bar, switch to your workspace. In the left-side navigation pane, click
the icon to go to the **DataStudio** page.
3. Double-click the workflow that you created to go to the editing page. Then, click Create
Node and select **Offline synchronization**. In the dialog box that appears, set the **Name** parameter to `write_result` .
4. Configure the `insert_data` node as the ancestor node of the `write_result` node.
5. Double-click the `write_result` node to go to the editing page. On the editing page, select
the MaxCompute data source that is created in the workspace as the source of data and the MySQL data source as the destination for data synchronization.
6. After the data sources pass the connectivity test, click **Next**.
7. Select the `result_table` table in the **source database** as the source of data.
8. Select the `odps_result` table in the **destination database** for data synchronization.
9. Configure field mappings between the tables in the source and destination databases.
The fields in the source on the left have a one-to-one mapping with the fields in the destination on the right. You can click **Add a row** to add a field. You can also click the icon to manually add or remove fields.
0. In the **Channel Control** section, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Task Expected Maximum Concurrency | The maximum number of parallel threads that the synchronization node can use to read data from the source or write data to the destination. You can configure the parallelism for the data synchronization node in the codeless UI. |
| Synchronizatio n rate | Specifies whether to enable throttling. You can enable throttling and specify a maximum synchronization rate to prevent heavy read workloads on the source. We recommend that you enable throttling and set the maximum synchronization rate to an appropriate value based on the configurations of the source. |
| Policy for Dirty Data Records | The policy used to process dirty data records. Valid values: Disallow Dirty Data Records Allow Limited Dirty Data Records Ignore Dirty Data Records |
| Distributed Execution | If you enable the distributed execution mode for the batch synchronization node, the system splits the node into slices and distributes them to multiple Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances for parallel running. In this case, the more ECS instances, the higher the data synchronization speed. If you have a high requirement for data synchronization performance, you can use the distributed execution mode to run your batch synchronization node. If you run the batch synchronization node in distributed execution mode, fragment resources of ECS instances can be utilized. This improves resource utilization. Limits: If you use a large number of concurrent threads to run your synchronization node in distributed execution mode, excessive access requests are sent to the data sources. Therefore, before you use the distributed execution mode, you must evaluate the access load on the data sources. Important If you do not enable the distributed execution mode for a data synchronization node, the configured number of parallel threads are used only for a single ECS instance. |

1. Save the configuration.
After the configuration is complete, you can scroll up and down to view the node icon in the top toolbar to save the configuration.

**Commit the synchronization node**

After you save the synchronization node, return to the configuration tab of the workflow to which the synchronization node belongs. Click the icon in the top toolbar of the configuration tab of the workflow to commit the synchronization node to the scheduling system. The scheduling system automatically and periodically runs the node from the next day based on the properties configured for the node.

**What to do next**

You have learned how to create a synchronization node to synchronize data to a specific data source. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In the next tutorial, you will learn how to configure properties and dependencies for a synchronization node. For more information, see Configure recurrence and dependencies for a node.

### Configure recurrence and

**dependencies for a node**

This topic describes how to configure the scheduling properties and set the recurrence and dependencies of a data synchronization node in DataWorks. This allows the node to run on a regular basis and rerun automatically. This ensures that the node can run reliably on demand. DataWorks has a powerful scheduling engine to trigger nodes based on the recurrence and dependencies of the nodes. DataWorks guarantees that tens of millions of nodes run accurately and punctually per day based on directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). In the DataWorks console, you can set the recurrence to minutely, hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly. A synchronization node is created. For more information, see Create a synchronization node.

**Note**

In this topic, the batch synchronization node `write_result` described in the "Create a synchronization node" topic is used, and the recurrence is set to weekly.

**Configure scheduling properties for the batch synchronization**

**node**

1. In the upper-left corner of the console, click the
icon and choose **All Products > Data**
**Development and O&M > DataStudio**. The **DataStudio** page appears.
2. In the top navigation bar, switch to your workspace. In the left-side navigation pane, click
the icon to go to the **DataStudio** page.
3. Find the workflow that you created and double-click the batch synchronization node
( `write_result` ) that you want to configure.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Instance Generation Mode | Next Day: Instances generated for a node are automatically scheduled on the next day after you deploy the node to the production environment. If you need to run this node on the current day, you can use the data backfill feature. Immediately After Deployment: Instances generated for a node are automatically scheduled on the current day after you deploy the node to the production environment. |
| Recurrence | The mode in which the node is run. Valid values: Normal, Skip Execution, and Dry Run. |
| Scheduling Calendar | The date and method for scheduling the node. Valid values: Default Calendar and Customize Calendar. |
| Scheduling Cycle | The recurrence of the node. Valid values: Minute, Hour, Day, Week, and Month. In this example, Week is selected. |
| Scheduled time and Run Every | The specific day and time when the node is run. For example, you can configure the node to run at 02:00 every Monday. |
| Cron Expression | The CRON expression of the time that you specified. The expression cannot be changed. |

4. On the configuration tab of the batch synchronization node, click **Properties** in the right-
side navigation pane and configure the parameters in the **Schedule** section.

| Timeout definition | By default, the system dynamically adjusts the timeout period for nodes based on the load. The timeout period ranges from 3 to 7, in days. If the running duration of a node exceeds the timeout period that you specify, the node is terminated and set to the Failed state. The timeout period for the node. Valid values: Default and Instances of Custom Nodes. |
|---|---|
| Rerun | Specifies whether the node can be rerun. Valid values: Allow Regardless of Running Status, Allow upon Failure Only, and Disallow Regardless of Running Status. |
| Auto Rerun upon Failure | Specifies whether to rerun the node upon an error. If you enable this feature, the scheduling system automatically reruns the related node based on the number of reruns and the rerun interval after the node fails. Take note that the scheduling system does not automatically rerun a node that you manually terminate. |
| Validity Period | The date from which the node is effective. |

**Configure dependencies for the batch synchronization node**

After you configure recurrence for the batch synchronization node write_result, you can configure dependencies for the node. You can configure the ancestor node on which the batch synchronization node depends. After that, the scheduling system triggers this node only after the instance of the ancestor node is run. For example, the instance of the batch synchronization node is not triggered until the instance of its ancestor node `insert_data` is run. By default, the scheduling system creates a node named in the format of `Workspace` `name_root` as the root node for each workspace. If no ancestor node is configured for the batch synchronization node, the node directly depends on the root node.

**Save and commit the node**

icon in the
1. Save the node. On the configuration tab of the `write_result` node, click the
top toolbar to save the node.
2. Commit the node. Click the
icon in the top toolbar to commit the node to the production environment.

**Important**

You must configure the **Rerun** and **Parent Nodes** parameters before you commit the node. A node must be committed to the scheduling system so that the scheduling system can automatically generate and run instances for the node. The scheduling system runs these instances at the specified time from the next day based on the recurrence settings.

**Note**

If you commit a node after 23:30, the scheduling system automatically generates and runs instances for the node from the third day.

**What to do next**

You have learned how to configure recurrence and dependencies for a synchronization node. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In the next tutorial, you will learn how to perform O&M operations on the committed node on a regular basis and troubleshoot errors that occur on the node based on operation logs. For more information, see Run a node and troubleshoot errors that occur on the node.

### Run a node and troubleshoot

**errors that occur on the node**

This topic describes three modes for you to run nodes: test run, data backfill, and periodic run. The information such as the scheduling settings, dependencies, and data output in logs helps efficient problem analysis and troubleshooting. In the "Configure recurrence and dependencies for a node" topic, you have configured the batch synchronization node write_result to run at 02:00 every Monday. After you commit this node, you have to wait until the next day to view the automatic scheduling result of this node. DataWorks allows you to run nodes in the following modes: test run, data backfill, and periodic run. This helps you confirm the scheduling time of each node instance, dependencies among node instances, and whether generated data meets your expectation.
**Test run**: The specific node is manually triggered. We recommend that you use this mode
if you need to check the scheduling time and running of a single node.
**Data backfill**: Nodes are manually triggered. We recommend that you use this mode if you
need to check the scheduling time of multiple nodes and scheduling dependencies among the nodes, or if you need to reperform data analysis and computing from a specific root node.
**Periodic run**: Nodes are automatically triggered. After you commit a node, the scheduling
system automatically runs instances for the node from 00:00 the next day. When the scheduling time of each instance arrives, the scheduling system checks whether the ancestor instances of the instance have been successfully run. If the scheduling time arrives and all the ancestor instances have been run, the scheduling system automatically triggers the instance without manual intervention.

**Note**

The scheduling system generates instances for manually triggered nodes and auto triggered nodes based on the same rules. The scheduling system generates an instance for each recurrence, which can occur by the day, hour, minute, month, or week. The scheduling system runs the instances generated for the specified dates only when the scheduling time arrives and generates operation logs for the instances. The scheduling system does not run the instances generated for other dates. Instead, it directly changes the states of the instances to Successful when the running conditions are met. In this case, the scheduling system does not generate operation logs.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Backfill Task Name | The name of the data backfill instance. |

**Test run**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the current page, click the
icon and choose **All Products >**
**Data Development and O&M > Operation Center**. The **Operation Center page**
appears.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Cycle Task Maintenance > Cycle Task**. On the
page that appears, find the node that you want to run and click **Test** in the **Actions** column.
4. In the **Test** dialog box, configure the **Test Name** and **Data Timestamp** parameters and
click **OK**.
5. On the **Test Instance** page, click the name of the generated instance. The directed acyclic
graph (DAG) of the instance appears on the right side. Right-click the instance in the DAG to view its details or manage this instance. For example, you can rerun this instance.

**Note**

In test run mode, a node is manually triggered. When the scheduling time arrives, the scheduling system immediately runs the instance that is generated for the node, regardless of whether the ancestor instances of the instance have been successfully run. The synchronization node `write_result` is configured to run at 02:00 every Monday. Based on the instance generation rules described earlier in this topic, if the data timestamp, which is one day earlier than the time at which the node is scheduled to run, is set to Sunday for a test run, the scheduling system runs the instance that is generated for the synchronization node at 02:00 on the following Monday. If the data timestamp is not set to Sunday for the test run, the scheduling system changes the state of the instance to Successful at 02:00 on the following Monday, and no operation logs are generated. We recommend that you backfill data for a node if you need to check the scheduling time of multiple nodes and scheduling dependencies among the nodes, or if you need to reperform data analysis and computing from a specific root node. To backfill data for a node, perform the following steps:
1. In the left-side navigation pane of the **Operation Center** page, choose **Cycle Task**
**Maintenance > Cycle Task**.
2. On the page that appears, find the node that you want to run and choose **Backfill Data >**
**Backfill Data for Current Node** in the **Actions** column.
3. In the **Backfill Data** pane, configure the parameters and click **Submit and Redirect**.
The following table describes the key parameters that you must configure. You can retain default values for other parameters.

| Current Task | The node for which you want to backfill data. By default, the current node is selected, which cannot be changed. |
|---|---|
| Data Timestamp | The data timestamp of the data backfill instance. The data backfill instance is run on the next day of the specified data timestamp. |
| Time Range | Specifies the time period during which the selected node needs to be run. Instances whose scheduling time is within the time period can be generated and run. You can configure this parameter to enable nodes that are scheduled by hour or minute to process only data in the specified time period. |
| Parallelism | Specifies whether to concurrently run the node with other nodes. Select No, or select Yes and specify several nodes to run concurrently. |
| Order | The order for the nodes to run. Valid values: Ascending by Business Date and Descending by Business Date. |

4. On the **Patch Data** page, click the name of the generated data backfill instance to view the
DAG of the instance. Right-click the instance in the DAG to view its details or manage this instance. For example, you can rerun this instance.

**Note**

In data backfill mode, the running of a data backfill instance on a day depends on the instance that is scheduled to run on the previous day. For example, in the scenario in which you backfill data in the period of time from September 15, 2017 to September 18, 2017 for a node, if the instance on September 15, 2017 fails to run, the instance on September 16, 2017 cannot be run. The batch synchronization node `write_result` is configured to run at 02:00 every Monday. Based on the instance generation rules described earlier in this topic, if the data timestamp, which is one day earlier than the time at which the node is scheduled to run, is set to Sunday for a data backfill operation, the scheduling system runs the instance that is generated for the synchronization node at 02:00 on the following Monday. If the data timestamp is not set to Sunday for the test run, the scheduling system changes the state of the instance to Successful at 02:00 on the following Monday, and no operation logs are generated.

**Periodic run**

In periodic run mode, the scheduling system automatically runs instances for all nodes based on the scheduling settings of the nodes. No menu item is provided for you to control the periodic run of nodes on the Operation Center page. You can view the instance information and operation logs of a node, such as the synchronization node write_result, by using one of the following methods: On the **Operation Center** page, choose **Cycle Task Maintenance > Cycle Instance** in the left-side navigation pane. On the page that appears, set parameters such as the data timestamp or run date to search for a specific instance of the node. Then, right-click the instance of the `write_result` node in the DAG to view the instance information and operation logs. On the **Cycle Instance** page, click an instance of the node. The DAG of the instance appears. Right-click the instance in the DAG to view its details or manage this instance. For example, you can rerun this instance.

**Note**

If an ancestor node has not been run, its descendant nodes are not run either. If the initial state of an instance is pending, the scheduling system checks whether all its ancestor instances have been run when the scheduling time arrives. The instance can be triggered and run only after all its ancestor instances have been run and when the scheduling time arrives. If an instance is pending, check whether all its ancestor instances have been run and whether the scheduling time arrives.

## Overview of the DataWorks

### Workspace management

#### Workspace modes

DataWorks provides basic and standard workspace modes, each providing a different level of security control. This topic describes the differences between the two workspace modes, their corresponding data access identities, and the required database table naming conventions.

**Workspaces in basic mode**

A DataWorks workspace in basic mode can be associated with only one project, instance, or database of each compute engine type. A workspace in basic mode does not isolate the development environment from the production environment. In such a workspace, you can perform only basic data development but cannot control the data development process and table permissions. A workspace in basic mode has the following benefits and risks: Benefits: This mode is easy to use. After you commit a node, the scheduling system immediately runs the node on a regular basis to produce data. In this case, you do not need to deploy the node. Risks: Developers can add, modify, or commit a node to the scheduling system without the need to obtain approval. This makes the production environment unstable. In addition, if this workspace is associated with a MaxCompute project, developers have the read and write permissions on all the tables of the MaxCompute project by default. Developers can create, delete, or modify tables. This puts data at risk. The following figure shows the data production process of a DataWorks workspace in basic mode. This workspace is associated with one MaxCompute compute engine instance.

**Workspaces in standard mode**

A DataWorks workspace in standard mode can be associated with two projects, instances, or databases of each compute engine type. A workspace in standard mode differs from a workspace in basic mode in the following aspects: You can modify code only in the development environment. After you commit a node, the scheduling system runs the node in the development environment only for smoke testing. The scheduling system does not automatically run this node in the development environment in the future. If you want the scheduling system to automatically run this node in the future, you must deploy it to the production environment. You can deploy a node only after you obtain approval from a workspace administrator or an O&M expert.

| Environment | Standard mode | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Development environment | Project name dev.Tabl _ e name | To create a development table named user info in the projectA _ project, the table name must be projectA dev.user info. _ _ |
| Production environment | Project name.Table name | To create a production table named user info in the projectA _ project, the table name must be projectA.user info. _ |

The following figure shows the data production process of a DataWorks workspace in standard mode. This workspace is associated with two MaxCompute compute engine instances.

**Database table naming conventions by workspace mode**

Basic mode does not separate development and production environments. Standard mode provides isolated development and production environments, and thus, database table naming conventions differ between them. If you need to access a production table from the development environment, strictly follow the naming conventions in the following table to prevent accidental operations in the production environment.

#### Manage workspace members and roles

DataWorks provides roles that can be granted different permissions. You can add users to your workspace and assign the required roles to the users. This way, you can implement the principle of least privilege and manage permissions in a finer-grained manner. You can also create custom roles and grant permissions to the roles based on your business requirements.

**Background information**

You can add multiple users to the same DataWorks workspace. In this case, if the users have excessive permissions on the workspace, the data security of the workspace may be affected by inappropriate permission use. However, if the users have insufficient permissions on the workspace, they may be unable to use the required features. To resolve this issue, DataWorks provides different identities, such as members and roles, at the workspace level. You can assign different roles to users based on the requirements of users for the workspace. If the built-in roles provided by DataWorks do not meet your business requirements, you can create custom roles and grant the required permissions to the roles. DataWorks provides the following identities:
**Member**: the Apsara Stack tenant accounts or Resource Access Management (RAM) users
added to a DataWorks workspace.
**Cloud account**: Apsara Stack tenant accounts or RAM users.
**Role**: the carriers that have operation permissions in a workspace and can be assumed by
the members of the workspace. DataWorks provides the following roles:
**Data analyst**: has the permissions on the DataAnalysis module.
**Project Owner**: has the highest level of permissions on a workspace.
**Project Manager**: has all the permissions on the features in a workspace. For example,
the Project Manager role can be used to assign a role to a RAM user and remove a member that is not the owner of a workspace from the workspace.
**Development**: has the permissions to develop and commit nodes.
**O&M**: has the permissions to allocate resources and deploy nodes.
**Deploy**: has the permissions to deploy nodes.
**Visitor**: has the read-only permissions on a DataWorks workspace.
**Safety Manager**: has the permissions to use Data Security Guard.
**Governance Administrator**: has the permissions to view and manage data governance
content of the workspace to which this role belongs in Data Governance Center.
**Model Developer**: has the permissions to use the data modeling feature.
For more information about the permissions of different roles, see View permissions.

**Limits**

You can use only the **Project Manager** and **Project Owner** roles to add users, change the roles that are assigned to members, remove **members**, and delete **custom roles**. You can use only a RAM user that is assigned the admin or super_administrator role of a MaxCompute project or an Apsara Stack tenant account to configure the mapping between a DataWorks custom workspace-level role and a role of a MaxCompute project.

DataWorks provides multiple roles such as Project Owner, Project Manager, Development, O&M, Deploy, Visitor, and Safety Manager. You cannot assign the Project Owner role to members. This topic describes the permissions of these roles. #### Manage data sources

Data sources are used to configure readers and writers during data integration. On the Data Source page of a workspace, you can view and add data sources.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
icon in the upper-right corner.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
On the **Data Sources** page, you can search for the desired data source based on **Data**

#### Manage clusters

DataWorks can be connected to Cloudera's Distribution Including Apache Hadoop (CDH) clusters. You can register a CDH cluster with DataWorks and perform data development and governance operations, such as task development, task scheduling, data map management (metadata management), and data quality management.

**Background information**

As an open source platform of Cloudera, CDH provides out-of-the-box features such as cluster management, cluster monitoring, and cluster diagnostics. CDH also supports a variety of components to help you run end-to-end big data workflows. Users assigned with any of the following permissions or role can register a CDH cluster in the current workspace: Apsara Stack tenant account DataWorks workspace member with the workspace administrator role A CDH cluster is deployed, and the required configuration of the cluster is available.

**Limits**

Only exclusive resource groups for scheduling can be used to run CDH tasks.

**Step 1: Go to the Cluster Management page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
icon in the upper-right corner.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cluster Management**.

**Step 2: Register a CDH cluster**

2. In the **Select Cluster Type** dialog box, click **CDH**.

The components required for the cluster vary based on the cluster version. You can view the components whose versions you must specify in the Cluster Connection Information section. |
| Cluster Name | The name of a cluster registered in another workspace or a custom cluster. You can select a cluster that is registered in another workspace to load its configurations, or customize a cluster name based on your business requirements to configure new settings. |

**Step 3: Configure a mapping between a tenant and the CDH**

**cluster account**

After the cluster is created, you can view the cluster card on the Cluster Management page. Click Account Mappings on the card, and then click Edit Account Mappings on the right to modify the account mappings.
1. Select a mapping type.
You can set the Mapping Type parameter to **No Authentication**, **Mapping to System**
**Account**, **Mapping to OpenLDAP Account**, or **Mapping to Kerberos Account** based on
your business requirements.
**No Authentication**: If you select this option, you do not need to configure a mapping.
By default, the cluster account that is configured when you register a CDH or CDP cluster is used to run CDH tasks.
**Mapping to System Account** : If you select this option, you can configure a mapping
between an Apsara Stack tenant account or a RAM user and a system account of a CDH cluster. Add the account information as prompted.
**Cluster Account Mapped to Alibaba Cloud Account** : Select an Apsara Stack tenant
account and configure a mapping between the Apsara Stack tenant account and a system account.
**Cluster Account Mapped to RAM User** : Select a RAM user and configure a mapping
between the RAM user and a system account. The following mappings are supported: Mapping between accounts with the same name (default): The CDH cluster account that has the same account name as the RAM user is mapped to the RAM user. For example: RAM user: **ram_user_1@xxx.onaliyun.com** CDH cluster account that has the same account name as the RAM user:

**ram_user_1**

If you use a RAM user named **ram_user_1@xxx.onaliyun.com** to run CDH tasks, the tasks are actually run by the CDH cluster account **ram_user_1**.

**Note**

If you use a RAM user to run CDH tasks in DataWorks, a CDH cluster account that has the same account name as the RAM user is actually used to run CDH tasks in the CDH cluster. You can also use a CDH cluster account that has a different account name from the RAM user to run CDH tasks. To prevent task execution failures, make sure that an account with the same name as the RAM user exists in the CDH cluster. To create such an account, choose **CDH Cluster Management > User Management**. Mapping between accounts with different names: A CDH cluster account that has a different account name from the RAM user is mapped to the RAM user. Configure a mapping as prompted.
**Mapping to OpenLDAP Account**: If you select this option, you can configure a mapping
between an Apsara Stack tenant account or a RAM user and an OpenLDAP account. Add the account information as prompted. If you select this option and use Presto at the same time, configure the `Config.Properties` and `Presto.Jks` files on the Basic Information tab of the CDH cluster. Make sure that the OpenLDAP service is enabled for the cluster.
**Mapping to Kerberos Account**: If you select this option, you can configure a mapping
between an Apsara Stack tenant or a RAM user and a Kerberos account of the CDH cluster. A Kerberos account is in the **Instance name@Domain name** format, such as cdn_test@HADOOP.COM. The **keytab authentication file** and **krb5.conf configuration file** are required for Kerberos authentication. The krb5.conf configuration file is used to store the configurations of the Key Distribution Center (KDC) server. The keytab authentication file is used to store the authentication credentials of the account that uses the resource. The file name must be in the **Kerberos**
**account.keytab** format.
Add the account information and upload the required files as prompted.

**Note**

You must select this option when Kerberos authentication is enabled for Hive Metastore of the CDH cluster. Otherwise, metadata collection is affected. If you select this option and use Presto at the same time, configure the `Config.Properties` and `Presto.Jks` files on the Basic Information tab of the CDH cluster. Make sure that the Kerberos service is enabled for the CDH cluster.
2. Configure a mapping.
Configure a mapping based on the selected mapping type.
3. After the configuration is complete, click Complete Modification.

**Step 4: Initialize a resource group**

You must initialize the resource group that you use when you associate with a cluster for the first time, change the service configurations of the cluster, or upgrade the component version. This ensures that the resource group can access the CDH cluster as expected, and CDH tasks can be run as expected by using the current environment configurations of the resource group. For example, if you modify the **core-site.xml** configuration file of your CDH cluster, you must initialize the resource group. To initialize the resource group that you use, go to the **Cluster Management** page, find the desired CDH cluster that is registered, and then click **Initialize Resource Group** in the upper-right corner.

DataWorks supports only MaxCompute as its compute engine. All workflows and nodes in a workspace are run on the MaxCompute compute engine associated with the workspace.

You can modify the following compute engine settings: description, whether to use the owner account of the MaxCompute project to run nodes, account that is used to run nodes, and AccessKey pair of the account. #### Resource group management

##### Create an exclusive resource group

DataWorks allows you to create exclusive resource groups to ensure fast and concurrent scheduling of a large number of nodes and stable data transmission. This topic describes how to create an exclusive resource group for scheduling and an exclusive resource group for Data Integration.

**Usage scenarios**

Create an exclusive resource group for scheduling If you need to run a large number of nodes in parallel, exclusive computing resources are required to ensure that the nodes can be run as scheduled. In this case, we recommend that you use an exclusive resource group for scheduling. Create an exclusive resource group for Data Integration If you need to run a large number of data synchronization nodes in parallel in Data Integration, exclusive computing resources are required to ensure fast and stable data transmission. In this case, we recommend that you use an exclusive resource group for Data Integration.

**Create an exclusive resource group for scheduling**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console as a tenant administrator.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
icon and choose **All Products > More > Tenant**
**Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Resource group Mgmt**.
4. On the **Exclusive Resource Group** tab, click **Create Resource Group for Scheduling**.
5. In the **Create Exclusive Resource Group** dialog box, configure the parameters as
required and click **Confirm**.

| Cluster | You can select Create Cluster. When you create a resource group, a cluster is created by default. |
|---|---|
| Slots | Optional. The number of slots. |

6. Find the exclusive resource group that you created and click **Bind Workspace** in the
**Actions** column.
7. In the **Bind Workspace** dialog box, click **Bind** in the Actions column to associate the
created exclusive resource group with the target workspace.

**Create an exclusive resource group for Data Integration**

The procedure of creating an exclusive resource group for Data Integration is similar to the procedure of creating an exclusive resource group for scheduling. The only difference is that you must set the **Resource Group Type** parameter to **Exclusive Resource Group for**
**Data Integration**.

**View the exclusive resource group information**

On the Exclusive Resource Group tab, find the exclusive resource group that you want to view and click **View Details** in the **Actions** column. In the Exclusive Resource Group message, view the details of the exclusive resource group.

**Change the number of slots**

On the Exclusive Resource Group tab, find the exclusive resource group that you want to manage and click **Slot Settings** in the **Actions** column. In the Slot Settings dialog box, change the number of slots based on your business requirements.

**Associate the resource group with a workspace**

On the Exclusive Resource Group tab, find the exclusive resource group that you want to manage and click **Bind Workspace** in the **Actions** column. You can associate the resource group with a specific workspace based on your business requirements. Then, you can select this resource group for Data Integration and scheduling tasks in the corresponding workspace.

## Data Integration

### Overview

Data Integration is a stable, efficient data synchronization platform that provides elastic scaling. It delivers high-speed, reliable data movement and synchronization between heterogeneous data sources in complex network environments. This topic describes the usage limitations, offline synchronization, development modes, and supported network types for Data Integration.

**Usage limitations**

Data Integration supports the synchronization of structured (for example, RDS and DRDS), semi-structured, and unstructured data (for example, data in OSS and TXT files). However, all data to be synchronized must be abstractable into a structured format. This means Data Integration only transfers data that can be abstracted as a logical two-dimensional table. It does not support synchronizing fully unstructured data, such as an MP3 file stored in OSS, to MaxCompute. Data Integration supports data synchronization for data stores within a single region and across some regions. Data can be transferred between some regions over the classic network, but connectivity is not guaranteed. If a connection test over the classic network fails, we recommend using the public network. Data Integration only synchronizes (transfers) data and does not provide a way to consume the resulting data stream.

**Offline (batch) synchronization**

Data Integration is primarily used for offline (batch) data synchronization. The offline data channel operates by defining the source and destination data sources and datasets. It uses an abstract framework of reader plug-ins and writer plug-ins with a simplified intermediate data format to enable data transfer between any structured and semi-structured data sources. For more information, see Supported data sources.

**Development modes**

You can configure data synchronization tasks in two modes:
**Wizard mode**: Provides a guided, step-by-step development experience for quickly
configuring data synchronization tasks. This mode is easy to learn but does not support some advanced features.
**Script mode**: Allows you to develop data synchronization tasks by writing a JSON script.
This mode is suitable for advanced users and provides greater flexibility for fine-grained configuration and management.

**Note**

Code generated in wizard mode can be converted to script mode. This is a one-way conversion. Before you write a script, you must configure the data source and create the target table.

**Network types**

Data Integration supports VPC connections. A VPC allows you to build an isolated network environment on Alibaba Cloud. You have full control over your virtual network, including selecting your own IP address ranges, dividing network segments, and configuring route tables and gateways. Data Integration provides an automatic reverse proxy detection feature for data sources such as RDS (MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server), PolarDB, DRDS, HybridDB for MySQL, AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, and AnalyticDB for MySQL 3.0. In a VPC, this feature lets you establish a network connection without purchasing an ECS instance in the same network. For other non-RDS Alibaba Cloud database services, such as PPAS, OceanBase, Redis, MongoDB, Memcache, Tablestore, and HBase, you must purchase an ECS instance in the same VPC. This instance provides network connectivity for the data synchronization task.

**Note**

Connections over the public network are also supported. However, due to bandwidth requirements and associated costs, we recommend using this option only when necessary.

**Concurrency**

The maximum number of parallel threads that a data synchronization task can use to read from the source or write to the destination.

**Rate limit**

The maximum data transfer speed that a Data Integration synchronization task can reach.

**Dirty data**

Data that is meaningless to the business or is in an invalid format. For example, if data from a source column of the VARCHAR type is written to a target column of the INT type, the write operation might fail because the type conversion is invalid. These failed records are considered dirty data. In DataWorks, a data source is the origin of the data to be processed, such as a database or a data warehouse. The service supports data transfer between various types of data sources.

#### Isolate data sources

Data source isolation ensures that data sources can be independently configured and used for the development and production environments. This feature applies only to workspaces in standard mode. This topic describes how to configure data source isolation and its impacts on a workspace. If a data source is configured in both the development and production environments, you can use the data source isolation feature to isolate the data source in the development environment from that in the production environment.

**Note**

Only workspaces in standard mode support the data source isolation feature. When you configure a synchronization node, the data source in the development environment is used. After you commit the synchronization node to the production environment for running, the data source in the production environment is used. To commit a synchronization node to the production environment for running, you must configure data sources with the same name in both the development and production environments. The data source isolation feature has the following impacts on workspaces: Workspaces in basic mode: The features and configuration dialog boxes of data sources are the same as those before the data source isolation feature is added. For more information, see Supported data sources. Workspaces in standard mode: The Environment parameter is added to the configuration dialog boxes of data sources. Workspaces upgraded from the basic mode to the standard mode: When you upgrade the mode, you are prompted to upgrade data sources. After you upgrade the mode, the data sources in the development environment are isolated from those in the production environment.

#### Manage permissions on data sources

DataWorks allows you to manage permissions on data sources to ensure data security. This topic describes how to configure and manage permissions on data sources in the DataWorks console.

**Background information**

The configurations of a data source include sensitive information such as the address, username, and password. Developers need to only reference the data source to access data in the data source. If sensitive information in a data source is leaked or the permissions to modify the data source configurations are not limited, security risks may occur. If multiple users modify the configurations of a data source, the data source may fail to be connected. As a result, the nodes that use the data source may fail. To prevent this issue, Data Integration allows only users who add data sources and workspace administrators to manage permissions on the data sources. They can grant permissions on data sources to a specific workspace or member.

**Manage permissions on a data source**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the page, click the
icon and choose **All Products > Data**
**Integration > Data Integration**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data source**.
4. On the **Data Sources** page, find the data source that you want to manage, and click the
icon in the Connection Information column.

**Note**

You cannot manage permissions on MaxCompute data sources.
5. In the **Manage Permissions on Data Source** dialog box, configure the parameters as
required.

| No. | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| (1) | Workspace | All workspaces to which the current user belongs and all members in each workspace. You can share the data source with a workspace or specific members in a workspace. If no permissions are configured for the data source, it inherits the permissions from the previous data source configuration. If you configure a permission on the data source for a workspace, the permission is granted to all members in the workspace. The permission is also automatically granted to the users who are added to the workspace as members after the permission is configured for the workspace. After you grant a permission on the data source to a workspace, you can still grant a different permission on the data source to a specific user in the workspace. For example, after you configure the No Permission permission on a data source for a workspace, you can still grant the Can be used permission on the data source to a specific member in the workspace. By default, only the user who added the data source can use the data source. Other users, including workspace administrators, cannot modify the data source. A workspace administrator can use the data source only after the workspace administrator is granted the required permissions. |
| (2) | Workspace Type | The type of each workspace. Valid values: Basic and Standard. |

| (3) | Permission | The type of the permission for managing the data source. No Permission: The workspace or member has no permission on the data source. Can be used: The workspace or member can use the data source but cannot modify or view the configurations of the data source. |
|---|---|---|
| (4) | Perform operations on multiple workflows at a time | The permission settings that you can configure for the selected workspaces or members at a time. You can configure the following permission settings for the selected workspaces or members at a time: Batch Usable and Batch No Permission. |

6. Click **OK**.
You can share data sources across workspaces based on the following rules: Share data sources between workspaces in basic mode: If the source workspace is upgraded to a workspace in standard mode, each shared data source in the production environment of the source workspace exists in the destination workspace. If the destination workspace is upgraded to a workspace in standard mode, each shared data source in the source workspace exists in both the development and production environments of the destination workspace. The data sources in the two environments are consistent. Share data sources from a workspace in basic mode to a workspace in standard mode: Each shared data source in the source workspace exists in both the development and production environments of the destination workspace. The data sources in the two environments are consistent. Share data sources between workspaces in standard mode: Each shared data source in the development environment of the source workspace exists in the development environment of the destination workspace. The same rule applies to the shared data sources in the production environment. Share data sources from a workspace in standard mode to a workspace in basic mode: You can share a data source in the production or development environment of the source workspace with the destination workspace. Only the data source in the production or development environment exists in the destination workspace. If you share a data source in both environments of the source workspace with the destination workspace, the newly shared data source overrides the existing data source in the destination workspace. If the destination workspace is upgraded to a workspace in standard mode, the shared data source in the development environment of the source workspace exists in the development environment of the destination workspace. The same rule applies to the shared data source in the production environment. In the top navigation bar, select the workspace with which the data sources are shared from the drop-down list. The **Data Sources** page of the selected workspace appears. On this page, you can view the data source that is shared with the workspace. On the **Data Sources** tab, you can view the information about each shared data source in the following columns: **Data Source Information**, **Connection Information**, **Description**, and **Created At**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain only letters, digits, and underscores ( ) and must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Connection URL | The endpoint of the AnalyticDB for MySQL V2.0 data source, in the format of host:port . |

A shared data source is named in the format of `Name of the workspace from which the data`

```
source is shared.Name of the data source .
```

##### Add an OSS data source

DataWorks provides Object Storage Service (OSS) Reader and OSS Writer for you to read data from and write data to OSS data sources. This topic describes how to add an OSS data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **OSS**.
4. In the **Add OSS Data Source** dialog box, configure the following parameters.

| AccessKey ID | This parameter is displayed only if you set Access Mode to AccessKey Mode. AccessKey ID: the AccessKey ID of the AccessKey pair. AccessKey Secret: the AccessKey secret that is used to access the OSS data source. The AccessKey secret is equivalent to a login password. |
|---|---|
| AceessKey Secret |  |
| Data Source VPC Region | The region in which the OSS bucket resides. |
| Endpoint | The OSS endpoint. The endpoint of the OSS service is subject to the region. Enter the endpoint of OSS based on the region. If you use the OSS data source as the reader, the format is http://my bucket name.aliyuncs.com . _ _ If you use the OSS data source as the writer, the format is http://aliyuncs.com . Note When you test the connectivity, you must add a bucket value, such as http://my bucket name.aliyuncs.com . _ _ |
| Bucket | The name of the OSS bucket. A bucket is a container that stores objects in OSS. You can create one or more buckets and add one or more objects to each bucket. During data synchronization, DataWorks can search for objects only in the bucket that is specified by this parameter. |

**Important**

If data in OSS is stored as CSV files, the data must comply with the standard CSV format. For example, if the data in a column of a CSV file is enclosed in a pair of single quotation marks (' '), you must replace this pair of single quotation marks with a pair of double quotation marks (" "). Otherwise, the data in the CSV file may be incorrectly parsed.
5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.
6. After the connectivity test is passed, click **Complete Creation**.

**What to do next**

Now you have learned how to add an OSS data source. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In subsequent tutorials, you will learn how to configure OSS Reader and OSS Writer. For more information, see Configure OSS Reader and Configure OSS Writer.

| AccessKey ID | This parameter is displayed only if you set Access Mode to AccessKey Mode. AccessKey ID: the AccessKey ID of the AccessKey pair. AccessKey Secret: the AccessKey secret that is used to access the OSS- HDFS data source. The AccessKey secret is equivalent to a login password. |

##### Add a PolarDB data source

DataWorks provides PolarDB Reader and PolarDB Writer for you to read data from and write data to PolarDB data sources. This topic describes how to add a PolarDB data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **PolarDB**.
4. On the **Add PolarDB Data Source** page, configure the parameters.
You can use one of the following modes to add a PolarDB data source: **Alibaba Cloud**
**instance mode** and **connection string mode**.
The following table describes the parameters that you need to configure when you add a PolarDB data source in **Alibaba Cloud instance mode**.

| Alibaba Cloud Account | Valid values: Current Alibaba Cloud Account and Another Alibaba Cloud Account. |
|---|---|
| ID of Another Alibaba Cloud Account | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. Set this parameter to the ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account to which the instance belongs. |
| Name of Role Assigned to RAM User | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. The RAM role provided by the Apsara Stack tenant account. This role must have the permissions to use the destination instance. |
| Data Source VPC Region | The region in which the database instance resides. |
| Instance | The name of the instance to which you want to connect. |
| Instance Address | After you select an instance, click Obtain Latest Address. The system automatically obtains the instance address information, including the public endpoint, private endpoint, virtual private cloud (VPC), and vSwitch of the instance. |
| Database Name | The name of the database to which the data source connects. Make sure that the specified user has permissions to access the database. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Configure Secondary Instance | Specifies whether to enable the secondary database feature. If the data source has read-only instances, you can select one of the read-only instances for data read when you configure a node. This way, the performance of the data source is not affected. If the data source has multiple read-only instances, only data of one of the read-only instances is read. Note If you turn on Configure Secondary Instance, you can use only one exclusive resource group to run the node that uses the data source. |
| Secondary Instance URL | The URL of the secondary database. This parameter is required after you turn on Configure Secondary Instance. |

| Authentication Method | Default value: No Authentication. If SSL authentication is enabled for your PolarDB instance, you must configure the Truststore File, Truststore Password, Keystore File, and Keystore Password after you select SSL Authentication. |
|---|---|

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Compute Engine Type | The type of the database. Valid values: MySQL and PostgreSQL. |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Configuration Mode | The mode in which you want to add the data source to DataWorks. In this example, Connection String Mode is selected. This way, you are connected to the database by using a JDBC URL. |
| JDBC Connection String Preview | After you configure the Connection Address and Database Name parameters, DataWorks automatically concatenates them into a JDBC URL for preview. |
| Connection Address | Host IP Address: the IP address or domain name of the database. If the database is an ApsaraDB RDS instance, you can view the endpoint on the instance details page. Port Number: the port number of the database. |
| Database Name | The name of the database to which the data source connects. Make sure that the specified user has permissions to access the database. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Advanced Parameters | Click Add Property and configure parameters and values based on your business requirements. Parameter: Select a parameter from the Parameter drop-down list. Value: Enter a valid value for the selected parameter. |

The following table describes the parameters that you can configure when you add a PolarDB data source in **connection string mode**.

| Authentication Method | Default value: No Authentication. If SSL authentication is enabled for your ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance, you must configure the Truststore File, Truststore Password, Keystore File, and Keystore Password after you select SSL Authentication. |
|---|---|
| Whether the data source is in a VPC | If your database resides in a virtual private cloud (VPC), you can select this option. In this case, you must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP, VPC ID, and Data source VPC Region parameters. Note You must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP parameter. If the data source is a self-managed database deployed on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, enter the ID of the ECS instance in the Data Source ID field. If the data source is a self-managed server deployed in a data center, enter the IP address of the server in the Data Source IP field. |

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.
6. After the connectivity test is passed, click **Complete Creation**.

**What to do next**

Now you have learned how to add a PolarDB data source. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In subsequent tutorials, you will learn how to configure PolarDB Reader and PolarDB Writer. For more information, see Configure PolarDB Reader and Configure PolarDB Writer.

DataWorks provides MySQL Reader and MySQL Writer for you to read data from and write data to MySQL data sources. This topic describes how to add a MySQL data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.

describes the parameters. You can use one of the following modes to add a MySQL data source: **Alibaba Cloud**
**instance mode** and **connection string mode**.
The following table describes the parameters that you need to configure when you add a MySQL data source in **Alibaba Cloud instance mode**.

| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
|---|---|
| Configuration Mode | The mode in which you want to add the data source to DataWorks. In this example, Alibaba Cloud Instance Mode is selected. |
| Alibaba Cloud Account | Valid values: Current Alibaba Cloud Account and Another Alibaba Cloud Account. |
| ID of Another Alibaba Cloud Account | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. Set this parameter to the ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account to which the instance belongs. |
| Name of Role Assigned to RAM User | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. The RAM role provided by the Apsara Stack tenant account. This role must have the permissions to use the destination instance. |
| Data Source VPC Region | The ID of the region in which the ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance resides. |
| Data Source ID | The name of the instance to which you want to connect. |
| Instance Address | After you select an instance, click Obtain Latest Address. The system automatically obtains the instance address information, including the public endpoint, private endpoint, virtual private cloud (VPC), and vSwitch of the instance. |
| Database Name | The name of the database to which the data source connects. Make sure that the specified user has permissions to access the database. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Authentication Method | Default value: No Authentication. If SSL authentication is enabled for your ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance, you must configure the Truststore File, Truststore Password, Keystore File, and Keystore Password after you select SSL Authentication. |

| Configure Secondary Database | Specifies whether to enable the secondary database feature. If the data source has read-only instances, you can select one of the read-only instances for data read when you configure a node. This way, the performance of the data source is not affected. If the data source has multiple read-only instances, only data of one of the read-only instances is read. Note If you turn on Configure Secondary Database, you can use only one exclusive resource group to run the node that uses the data source. |
|---|---|
| Secondary Instance ID | The ID of the secondary database. This parameter is required after you turn on Configure Secondary Instance. |
| Version | You can log in to the MySQL server, run the SELECT VERSION() command to query the version number, and then select the version from the drop-down list. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Configuration Mode | The mode in which you want to add the data source to DataWorks. In this example, Connection String Mode is selected. That way, you are connected to the database by using a JDBC URL. |
| JDBC Connection String Preview | After you configure the Connection Address and Database Name parameters, DataWorks automatically concatenates them into a JDBC URL for preview. |
| Connection Address | Host IP Address: the IP address or domain name of the database. If the database is an ApsaraDB RDS instance, you can view the endpoint on the instance details page. Port Number: the port number of the database. In most cases, MySQL uses port 3306. |
| Database Name | The name of the database to which the data source connects. Make sure that the specified user has permissions to access the database. |

| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |

| Version | You can log in to the MySQL server, run the SELECT VERSION() command to query the version number, and then select the version from the drop-down list. |
| Advanced Parameters | Click Add Property and configure parameters and values based on your business requirements. Parameter: Select a parameter from the Parameter drop-down list. Value: Enter a valid value for the selected parameter. |
| Whether the data source is in a VPC | If your database resides in a VPC, you can select this option. In this case, you must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP, VPC ID, and Data Source VPC Region parameters. Note You must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP parameter. If the data source is a self-managed database deployed on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, enter the ID of the ECS instance in the Data Source ID field. If the data source is a self-managed server deployed in a data center, enter the IP address of the server in the Data Source IP field. |

| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |

| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Authentication Method | Default value: No Authentication. If SSL authentication is enabled for your Oracle database, you must configure the Truststore File, Truststore Password, Keystore File, and Keystore Password after you select SSL Authentication. |
| Whether the data source is in a VPC | If your database resides in a virtual private cloud (VPC), you can select this option. In this case, you must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP, VPC ID, and Data Source VPC Region parameters. Note You must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP parameter. If the data source is a self-managed database deployed on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, enter the ID of the ECS instance in the Data Source ID field. If the data source is a self-managed server deployed in a data center, enter the IP address of the server in the Data Source IP field. |

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.

3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **Oracle**.
4. On the **Add Oracle Data Source** page, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
