##### Add a PolarDB data source

DataWorks provides PolarDB Reader and PolarDB Writer for you to read data from and write data to PolarDB data sources. This topic describes how to add a PolarDB data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **PolarDB**.
4. On the **Add PolarDB Data Source** page, configure the parameters.
You can use one of the following modes to add a PolarDB data source: **Alibaba Cloud**
**instance mode** and **connection string mode**.
The following table describes the parameters that you need to configure when you add a PolarDB data source in **Alibaba Cloud instance mode**.

| ID of Another Alibaba Cloud Account | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. Set this parameter to the ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account to which the instance belongs. |
|---|---|
| Name of Role Assigned to RAM User | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. The RAM role provided by the Apsara Stack tenant account. This role must have the permissions to use the destination instance. |
| Data Source VPC Region | The region in which the database instance resides. |
| Instance | The name of the instance to which you want to connect. |
| Instance Address | After you select an instance, click Obtain Latest Address. The system automatically obtains the instance address information, including the public endpoint, private endpoint, virtual private cloud (VPC), and vSwitch of the instance. |
| Database Name | The name of the database to which the data source connects. Make sure that the specified user has permissions to access the database. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Configure Secondary Instance | Specifies whether to enable the secondary database feature. If the data source has read-only instances, you can select one of the read-only instances for data read when you configure a node. This way, the performance of the data source is not affected. If the data source has multiple read-only instances, only data of one of the read-only instances is read. Note If you turn on Configure Secondary Instance, you can use only one exclusive resource group to run the node that uses the data source. |
| Secondary Instance URL | The URL of the secondary database. This parameter is required after you turn on Configure Secondary Instance. |

| Authentication Method | Default value: No Authentication. If SSL authentication is enabled for your PolarDB instance, you must configure the Truststore File, Truststore Password, Keystore File, and Keystore Password after you select SSL Authentication. |
|---|---|

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Compute Engine Type | The type of the database. Valid values: MySQL and PostgreSQL. |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Configuration Mode | The mode in which you want to add the data source to DataWorks. In this example, Connection String Mode is selected. This way, you are connected to the database by using a JDBC URL. |
| JDBC Connection String Preview | After you configure the Connection Address and Database Name parameters, DataWorks automatically concatenates them into a JDBC URL for preview. |
| Connection Address | Host IP Address: the IP address or domain name of the database. If the database is an ApsaraDB RDS instance, you can view the endpoint on the instance details page. Port Number: the port number of the database. |
| Database Name | The name of the database to which the data source connects. Make sure that the specified user has permissions to access the database. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Advanced Parameters | Click Add Property and configure parameters and values based on your business requirements. Parameter: Select a parameter from the Parameter drop-down list. Value: Enter a valid value for the selected parameter. |

The following table describes the parameters that you can configure when you add a PolarDB data source in **connection string mode**.

| Authentication Method | Default value: No Authentication. If SSL authentication is enabled for your ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance, you must configure the Truststore File, Truststore Password, Keystore File, and Keystore Password after you select SSL Authentication. |
|---|---|
| Whether the data source is in a VPC | If your database resides in a virtual private cloud (VPC), you can select this option. In this case, you must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP, VPC ID, and Data source VPC Region parameters. Note You must configure the Data Source ID or Data Source IP parameter. If the data source is a self-managed database deployed on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, enter the ID of the ECS instance in the Data Source ID field. If the data source is a self-managed server deployed in a data center, enter the IP address of the server in the Data Source IP field. |

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.
6. After the connectivity test is passed, click **Complete Creation**.

Now you have learned how to add a PolarDB data source. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In subsequent tutorials, you will learn how to configure PolarDB Reader and PolarDB Writer. For more information, see Configure PolarDB Reader and Configure PolarDB Writer.

##### Add an SQL Server data source

DataWorks provides SQL Server Reader and SQL Server Writer for you to read data from and write data to SQL Server data sources. This topic describes how to add an SQL Server data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add data source** dialog box, click **SQL Server**.
4. In the **Add SQL Server Data Source** dialog box, configure the following parameters.
You can set the Data Source Type parameter to **Alibaba Cloud Instance Mode** or
**Connection String Mode** for an SQL Server data source.
The following table describes the parameters that you need to configure when you add an SQL Server data source in **Alibaba Cloud Instance Mode**.

| Applicable Environment | The environment in which the data source is used. Valid values: Development and Production. Note This parameter is displayed only if the workspace is in standard mode. |
|---|---|
| Rds Instance Id | The ID of the ApsaraDB RDS for SQL Server instance. You can log in to the ApsaraDB RDS console to view the ID. |
| Rds Instance Primary Account Id | The ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account that is used to purchase the ApsaraDB RDS for SQL Server instance. |
| Default Database Name | The name of the database that you created in the ApsaraDB RDS for SQL Server instance. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Special Authentication Method | Specifies whether to enable identity authentication. By default, None Auth is selected. If SSL encryption is configured for your database, set this parameter to SSL Auth. In this case, the Truststore File and Truststore Password parameters are required. |
| Configure Secondary Instance | Specifies whether to enable the secondary database feature. If the data source has read-only instances, you can select one of the read-only instances for data read when you configure a node. This way, the performance of the data source is not affected. If the secondary ApsaraDB RDS for SQL Server instance has multiple read-only ApsaraDB RDS for SQL Server instances, only data of one of the read-only instances is read. Note If you turn on Configure Secondary Instance, you can use only one exclusive resource group to run the node that uses the data source. |
| Secondary Instance ID | The ID of the secondary database. This parameter is required after you turn on Configure Secondary Instance. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

The following table describes the parameters you can configure when you add an SQL Server data source in **Connection String Mode**.

| Data Source Type | The mode in which you want to add the data source to DataWorks. In this example, set this parameter to Connection String Mode. |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain only letters, digits, and underscores ( ) and must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Applicable Environment | The environment in which the data source is used. Valid values: Development and Production. Note This parameter is displayed only if the workspace is in standard mode. |
| JDBC URL | The Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) URL of the database, which is in the jdbc:sqlserver://ServerIP:Port;DatabaseName=Database format. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |
| Special Authentication Method | Specifies whether to enable identity authentication. By default, None Auth is selected. If SSL encryption is configured for your database, set this parameter to SSL Auth. In this case, the Truststore File and Truststore Password parameters are required. |
| Whether Data Source in VPC | Specifies whether to connect to the data source by using a virtual private cloud (VPC). If yes, select this option. After you select this option, the Datasource instanceId or Datasource IP parameter and the Datasource VPC ID and Datasource VPC Region parameters are required. Note You must configure the Datasource instanceId or Datasource IP parameter. If the data source is a self-managed database deployed on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, enter the ID of the ECS instance in the Datasource instanceId field. If the data source is a self-managed server deployed in a data center, enter the IP address of the server in the Datasource IP field. |

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.
6. After the connectivity test is passed, click **Complete Creation**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |

| Host Address/IP Address | The IP address or domain name of the database. |
| Port | The port number of the database. |

i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| JDBC Connection String Preview | After you configure the Host Address/IP Address, Port, and Database Name parameters, DataWorks automatically concatenates them into a JDBC URL for preview. |
| Host Address/IP Address | The IP address or domain name of the database. |
| Port | The port number of the database. |
| Database Name | The name of the database that you created on the MariaDB instance. |
| Username | The username that is used to connect to the database. |
| Password | The password that is used to connect to the database. |

2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **MariaDB**.

##### Add a Hive data source

DataWorks provides Hive Reader and Hive Writer for you to read data from and write data to Hive data sources. This topic describes how to add a Hive data source.

**Usage notes**

If you use Object Storage Service (OSS) as the underlying storage service, you must take note of the following items:

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Data source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Configuration Mode | The mode in which you want to add the data source to DataWorks. In this example, Alibaba Cloud Instance Mode is selected. |
| Alibaba Cloud Account | You can select Current Alibaba Cloud Account or Another Alibaba Cloud Account. |

You must configure advanced parameters that are required for connecting to OSS. The following sample code provides an example:

```json
{
    "hiveConfig":{
     "fs.oss.accessKeyId":"<yourAccessKeyId>",
      "fs.oss.accessKeySecret":"<yourAccessKeySecret>",
      "fs.oss.endpoint":"oss-cn-<yourRegion>-internal.aliyuncs.com"
   }
  }
```

**Limits**

DataWorks supports only Hive 2.3.3 and Hive 2.3.5. Hive data sources support Kerberos authentication and SSL authentication. If you do not need to perform identity authentication for a Hive data source, you can set the
**Authentication Method** parameter to **No Authentication** when you add the data
source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **Hive**.
4. On the **Add Hive Data Source** page, configure the parameters.
You can add a Hive data source in one of the following modes: **Alibaba Cloud instance**
**mode**, **connection string mode**, and **CDH Cluster Mode**.
The following table describes the parameters that you need to configure when you add a Hive data source in **Alibaba Cloud instance mode**.

| UID Of Alibaba Cloud Account | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. Set this parameter to the ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account to which the instance belongs. |
|---|---|
| RAM Role | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. The RAM role provided by the Apsara Stack tenant account. This role must have the permissions to use the destination instance. |
| Data Source VPC Region | The ID of the region in which the instance resides. |
| Instance | The name of the instance. |
| Hive Version | The Hive version that you want to use. |
| Database Name | The name of the Hive database to access. You can run the SHOW DATABASES command in the Hive client to view existing databases. |
| Identity to Access OSS | This parameter is available only if you set Alibaba Cloud Account to Alibaba Cloud Instance Mode. Valid values: Alibaba Cloud Account, Alibaba Cloud RAM User, and Alibaba Cloud RAM Role. Note If you need to synchronize OSS tables in the database, this identity is used to access OSS. Make sure that the selected identity has the required permissions on OSS. Otherwise, data synchronization fails due to insufficient read or write permissions. Connectivity tests do not verify the data read and write permissions. |
| Logon Method | Valid values: Anonymous Logon and Logon with Username and Password (LDAP). If you select Logon with Username and Password (LDAP), you must configure the Username and Password parameters. |

| me | DATABASES |
|---|---|

| Authentication Method | Specifies whether to enable identity authentication. Valid values: No Authentication: If you do not need to enable identify authentication for a data source, select No Authentication when you add the data source. By default, No Authentication is selected. Kerberos Authentication: If you select this authentication method, you must configure the following parameters: Keytab File: the keytab file that you want to use. If no keytab file is available, click Add Authentication File to upload a keytab file. CONF File: the CONF file that you want to use. If no CONF file is available, click Add Authentication File to upload a CONF file. Principal: the Kerberos principal. Specify a value for this parameter in the format of Principal name/Instance name@Domain name . Example: ****/hadoopclient@**.*** . SSL Authentication: If you select this authentication method, you must configure the following parameters: Truststore File: the truststore certificate file that you want to use. If no truststore file is available, click Add Authentication File to upload a truststore file. Truststore Password: the password specified when the truststore certificate file is generated. Keystore File: the password specified when the keystore file certificate file is generated. If no keytab file is available, click Add Authentication File to upload a keytab file. Keystore Password: the password specified when the keystore certificate file is generated. |
|---|---|
| Advanced Parameters | The advanced parameters of Hive. Click Add Property and configure parameters and values based on your business requirements. Parameter: Select a parameter from the Parameter drop-down list. Value: Enter a valid value for the selected parameter. |

|  | Principal name/Instance name@Domain name |
|---|---|
| ****/hadoopclient@**.*** |  |

##### Configure a Hologres data source

Hologres data sources provide a bidirectional channel to read data from and write data to Hologres. This topic describes how to configure a Hologres data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **Hologres**.
4. On the **Add Hologres Data Source** page, configure the parameters.

| Alibaba Cloud Account | The Apsara Stack tenant account to which the AnalyticDB for MySQL V2.0 instance to be accessed belongs. Valid values: Current Alibaba Cloud Account and Another Alibaba Cloud Account. If you select the Another Alibaba Cloud Account option, you also need to configure the UID Of Alibaba Cloud Account, RAM Role, Hologres Instance, and Database Name parameters. |
|---|---|
| Region | The region in which the Hologres instance resides. |
| Hologres Instance | The ID of the Hologres instance. This parameter is required when the Alibaba Cloud Account parameter is set to Current Alibaba Cloud Account. |
| Database Name | The name of the Hologres instance. This parameter is required when the Alibaba Cloud Account parameter is set to Current Alibaba Cloud Account. |
| Database Name | The name of the Hologres instance. This parameter is required when the Alibaba Cloud Account parameter is set to Another Alibaba Cloud Account. |
| Default Access Identity | The default identity used to access the Hologress data source. This parameter is required when the Alibaba Cloud Account parameter is set to Current Alibaba Cloud Account. Valid values: Alibaba Cloud Account, Alibaba Cloud RAM User, and Alibaba Cloud RAM Role. Note If you use an Apsara Stack tenant account, you can select any of these options. If you use a Resource Access Management (RAM) user or RAM role: If you are granted the AdministratorAccess permission, you can select any of these options. If you are not granted the AdministratorAccess permission, you can select only Alibaba Cloud RAM User or Alibaba Cloud RAM Role. |

| Authentication Method | The method used to authenticate the login user. Valid values: No Authentication and SSL Authentication. Default: No Authentication. If you select SSL Authentication, you must also specify SSL Encryption. |
|---|---|

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| Environment | The environment in which the data source is used. Valid values: Development and Production. Note This parameter is displayed only if the workspace is in standard mode. |
| Kafka server address | The address of a Kafka broker. If you specify multiple addresses, separate them with commas (,). Example: 10.0.0.1:9092,10.0.0.2:9092 . |

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.

##### Add a Kafka data source

DataWorks provides Kafka Reader and Kafka Writer for you to read data from and write data to Kafka data sources. This topic describes how to add a Kafka data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **Kafka**.
4. In the **Add Kafka Data Source** dialog box, configure the following parameters.

| Authentication | The authentication method supported for connecting to a Kafka broker. Valid values: None SASL PLAINTEXT _ SASL SSL _ SSL |
|---|---|
| Sasl Mechanism | This parameter is displayed only if the Authentication parameter is set to SASL PLAINTEXT or SASL SSL . Valid values: _ _ GSSAPI(Kerberos) PLAIN |
| Truststore File | This parameter is displayed only if the Authentication parameter is set to SASL SSL or SSL . _ The truststore file and password used for verifying SSL certificates. |
| Truststore Password |  |
| Keystore File |  |
| Keystore Password |  |
| Key Password |  |
| Keytab File | You must upload a keytab file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) . The keytab file must contain the key for the principal that is specified in the Java Authentication and Authorization Service (JAAS) configuration file and be verifiable by the Key Distribution Center (KDC). For example, if the client.keytab file exists in the local working directory, you can run the following command to check whether the keytab file contains the key for a specific principal: klist -ket ./client.keytab Keytab name: FILE:client.keytab KVNO Timestamp Principal ---- ------------------- ---------------------------------------- ------------- 7 2018-07-30T10:19:16 test**@demo.com (des-cbc-md5) |

| Kerberos Config File | You must upload a Kerberos configuration file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) . A Kerberos configuration file must contain the following modules: [libdefaults] and [realms]. The [libdefaults] module contains configuration items that are relevant to Kerberos authentication. Each configuration item is specified in the key=value format. The [realms] module specifies a KDC address and can contain multiple realm submodules. Each realm submodule starts with a realm name that is followed by an equal sign (=). A pair of braces {} are used to enclose all configuration items for each realm submodule. Each configuration item is specified in the key=value format. The following example provides a typical configuration format of a Kerberos configuration file. Replace xxx in the following content based on your business requirements. [libdefaults] default realm = xxx _ [realms] xxx = { kdc = xxx } |
|---|---|
| Jaas Config File | You must upload a JAAS configuration file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) or PLAIN . The content of a JAAS configuration file must start with KafkaClient. Then, a pair of braces {} are used to enclose all configuration items. The first line in braces {} defines the login module class. The login module class is fixed for different SASL authentication mechanisms. All subsequent configuration items are specified in the key=value format. All configuration items except for the last configuration item cannot contain a semicolon (;) at the end. The last configuration item must end with a semicolon (;). A semicolon (;) must also be added after the right brace }. If the content of a JAAS configuration file does not meet the preceding format requirements, the JAAS configuration file fails to be parsed. The following example provides a typical configuration format of a JAAS configuration file. Replace xxx in the following content based on your business requirements. KafkaClient { com.sun.security.auth.module.Krb5LoginModule required useKeyTab=true keyTab="xxx" storeKey=true serviceName="kafka-server" principal="kafka-client@EXAMPLE.COM"; }; |

| Extended parameters | The advanced parameters of Kafka, such as those related to the producer and consumer. |
|---|---|

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Source Name | The name of the data source. The name can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). It must start with a letter. _ |
| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |
| JDBC Connection String Preview | After you configure the Host Address/IP Address, Port, and Database Name parameters, DataWorks automatically concatenates them into a JDBC URL for preview. |
| Host Address/IP Address | The IP address or domain name of the database. |
| Port | The port number of the database. |

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.
6. After the connectivity test is passed, click **Complete Creation**.

**Related operations**

Now you have learned how to add a Kafka data source. You can proceed with the next tutorial. In subsequent tutorials, you will learn how to configure Kafka Reader and Kafka Writer. For more information, see Configure Kafka Reader and Configure Kafka Writer.

##### Add a Kafka data source

DataWorks provides Kafka Reader and Kafka Writer for you to read data from and write data to Kafka data sources. This topic describes how to add a Kafka data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **Kafka**.
4. In the **Add Kafka Data Source** dialog box, configure the following parameters.

| Environment | The environment in which the data source is used. Valid values: Development and Production. Note This parameter is displayed only if the workspace is in standard mode. |
|---|---|
| Kafka server address | The address of a Kafka broker. If you specify multiple addresses, separate them with commas (,). Example: 10.0.0.1:9092,10.0.0.2:9092 . |
| Authentication | The authentication method supported for connecting to a Kafka broker. Valid values: None SASL PLAINTEXT _ SASL SSL _ SSL |
| Sasl Mechanism | This parameter is displayed only if the Authentication parameter is set to SASL PLAINTEXT or SASL SSL . Valid values: _ _ GSSAPI(Kerberos) PLAIN |
| Truststore File | This parameter is displayed only if the Authentication parameter is set to SASL SSL or SSL . _ The truststore file and password used for verifying SSL certificates. |
| Truststore Password |  |
| Keystore File |  |
| Keystore Password |  |
| Key Password |  |

| Keytab File | You must upload a keytab file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) . The keytab file must contain the key for the principal that is specified in the Java Authentication and Authorization Service (JAAS) configuration file and be verifiable by the Key Distribution Center (KDC). For example, if the client.keytab file exists in the local working directory, you can run the following command to check whether the keytab file contains the key for a specific principal: klist -ket ./client.keytab Keytab name: FILE:client.keytab KVNO Timestamp Principal ---- ------------------- ---------------------------------------- ------------- 7 2018-07-30T10:19:16 test**@demo.com (des-cbc-md5) |
|---|---|
| Kerberos Config File | You must upload a Kerberos configuration file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) . A Kerberos configuration file must contain the following modules: [libdefaults] and [realms]. The [libdefaults] module contains configuration items that are relevant to Kerberos authentication. Each configuration item is specified in the key=value format. The [realms] module specifies a KDC address and can contain multiple realm submodules. Each realm submodule starts with a realm name that is followed by an equal sign (=). A pair of braces {} are used to enclose all configuration items for each realm submodule. Each configuration item is specified in the key=value format. The following example provides a typical configuration format of a Kerberos configuration file. Replace xxx in the following content based on your business requirements. [libdefaults] default realm = xxx _ [realms] xxx = { kdc = xxx } |

| Jaas Config File | You must upload a JAAS configuration file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) or PLAIN . The content of a JAAS configuration file must start with KafkaClient. Then, a pair of braces {} are used to enclose all configuration items. The first line in braces {} defines the login module class. The login module class is fixed for different SASL authentication mechanisms. All subsequent configuration items are specified in the key=value format. All configuration items except for the last configuration item cannot contain a semicolon (;) at the end. The last configuration item must end with a semicolon (;). A semicolon (;) must also be added after the right brace }. If the content of a JAAS configuration file does not meet the preceding format requirements, the JAAS configuration file fails to be parsed. The following example provides a typical configuration format of a JAAS configuration file. Replace xxx in the following content based on your business requirements. KafkaClient { com.sun.security.auth.module.Krb5LoginModule required useKeyTab=true keyTab="xxx" storeKey=true serviceName="kafka-server" principal="kafka-client@EXAMPLE.COM"; }; |
|---|---|
| Extended parameters | The advanced parameters of Kafka, such as those related to the producer and consumer. |

5. In the **Connection Configuration** section, click **Test Network Connectivity**.
6. After the connectivity test is passed, click **Complete Creation**.

**Related operations**

**Usage notes**

If you use Object Storage Service (OSS) as the underlying storage service, you must take note of the following items: You must configure advanced parameters that are required for connecting to OSS. The following sample code provides an example:

```json
{
    "hiveConfig":{
     "fs.oss.accessKeyId":"<yourAccessKeyId>",
      "fs.oss.accessKeySecret":"<yourAccessKeySecret>",
      "fs.oss.endpoint":"oss-cn-<yourRegion>-internal.aliyuncs.com"
   }
  }
```

**Limits**

DataWorks supports only Hive 2.3.3 and Hive 2.3.5. Hive data sources support Kerberos authentication and SSL authentication. If you do not need to perform identity authentication for a Hive data source, you can set the
**Authentication Method** parameter to **No Authentication** when you add the data
source.

##### Add a Kafka data source

DataWorks provides Kafka Reader and Kafka Writer for you to read data from and write data to Kafka data sources. This topic describes how to add a Kafka data source.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the **Data Sources** page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Integration > Data Integration**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Sources**.
2. On the **Data Sources** page, click **Add Data Source**.
3. In the **Add Data Source** dialog box, click **Kafka**.
4. In the **Add Kafka Data Source** dialog box, configure the following parameters.

| Kafka server address | The address of a Kafka broker. If you specify multiple addresses, separate them with commas (,). Example: 10.0.0.1:9092,10.0.0.2:9092 . |
|---|---|
| Authentication | The authentication method supported for connecting to a Kafka broker. Valid values: None SASL PLAINTEXT _ SASL SSL _ SSL |
| Sasl Mechanism | This parameter is displayed only if the Authentication parameter is set to SASL PLAINTEXT or SASL SSL . Valid values: _ _ GSSAPI(Kerberos) PLAIN |
| Truststore File | This parameter is displayed only if the Authentication parameter is set to SASL SSL or SSL . _ The truststore file and password used for verifying SSL certificates. |
| Truststore Password |  |
| Keystore File |  |
| Keystore Password |  |
| Key Password |  |
| Keytab File | You must upload a keytab file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) . The keytab file must contain the key for the principal that is specified in the Java Authentication and Authorization Service (JAAS) configuration file and be verifiable by the Key Distribution Center (KDC). For example, if the client.keytab file exists in the local working directory, you can run the following command to check whether the keytab file contains the key for a specific principal: klist -ket ./client.keytab Keytab name: FILE:client.keytab KVNO Timestamp Principal ---- ------------------- ---------------------------------------- ------------- 7 2018-07-30T10:19:16 test**@demo.com (des-cbc-md5) |

| Kerberos Config File | You must upload a Kerberos configuration file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) . A Kerberos configuration file must contain the following modules: [libdefaults] and [realms]. The [libdefaults] module contains configuration items that are relevant to Kerberos authentication. Each configuration item is specified in the key=value format. The [realms] module specifies a KDC address and can contain multiple realm submodules. Each realm submodule starts with a realm name that is followed by an equal sign (=). A pair of braces {} are used to enclose all configuration items for each realm submodule. Each configuration item is specified in the key=value format. The following example provides a typical configuration format of a Kerberos configuration file. Replace xxx in the following content based on your business requirements. [libdefaults] default realm = xxx _ [realms] xxx = { kdc = xxx } |
|---|---|
| Jaas Config File | You must upload a JAAS configuration file if the Sasl Mechanism parameter is set to GSSAPI(Kerberos) or PLAIN . The content of a JAAS configuration file must start with KafkaClient. Then, a pair of braces {} are used to enclose all configuration items. The first line in braces {} defines the login module class. The login module class is fixed for different SASL authentication mechanisms. All subsequent configuration items are specified in the key=value format. All configuration items except for the last configuration item cannot contain a semicolon (;) at the end. The last configuration item must end with a semicolon (;). A semicolon (;) must also be added after the right brace }. If the content of a JAAS configuration file does not meet the preceding format requirements, the JAAS configuration file fails to be parsed. The following example provides a typical configuration format of a JAAS configuration file. Replace xxx in the following content based on your business requirements. KafkaClient { com.sun.security.auth.module.Krb5LoginModule required useKeyTab=true keyTab="xxx" storeKey=true serviceName="kafka-server" principal="kafka-client@EXAMPLE.COM"; }; |

| Extended parameters | The advanced parameters of Kafka, such as those related to the producer and consumer. |
|---|---|

| Data Source Description | The description of the data source. The description can be up to 80 characters in length. |

#### Connectivity testing

This topic describes the FAQ about connectivity testing on connections. When configuring a security group for a connection hosted on an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, add the IP address of the scheduling cluster to the inbound and outbound rules of the security group. If the security group is not properly configured, data synchronization fails due to a connection failure. To set a wide port range for a security group rule, call relevant API operations, instead of using the console.

**Common scenarios of connectivity test failures**

When a connection fails the connectivity test, check whether the region, network type, whitelist, database name, and username are properly configured for the connection. The following errors may occur during connectivity testing: The database password is incorrect. The network connection fails. A network error occurs during data synchronization. Check the log and determine which resource group is used. Check whether the resource group is a custom one. For a Relational Database Service (RDS) connection or a MongoDB connection, if a custom resource group is used, check whether its IP addresses are added to the whitelist of the connection. Check whether both the source and destination connections pass the connectivity test. For an RDS connection or a MongoDB connection, check whether all relevant IP addresses are added to the whitelist of the connection. If the IP address of a server is not added to the whitelist, the sync node fails when it runs on this server. However, the sync node succeeds when it runs on another server whose IP address is added to the whitelist. The result shows that a sync node is run but the log contains a disconnection error in port 8000. This issue occurs because a custom resource group is used and no inbound rule is configured for the corresponding IP address and port 8000 in the security group. To resolve the issue, add the IP address and port to the inbound rule of the security group and run the node again.

**Examples of connectivity test failures**

Example 1 Symptom A connection failed the connectivity test. The database connection failed. The following information is involved: Database URL: jdbc:mysql://xx.xx.xx.x:xxxx/t_uoer_bradef. Username: xxxx_test. Error message: Access denied for user 'xxxx_test'@'%' to database 'yyyy_demo'. Troubleshooting i. Check whether the configuration of the connection is correct. ii. Check whether the database password is correct, the whitelist is properly configured, and your account has the permission to access the database. You can grant the required permissions in the RDS console. Example 2 Symptom A connection failed the connectivity test. The following error message is returned:

```
error message: Timed out after 5000 ms while waiting for a server that matches Read PreferenceServerSelector{readPreference=primary}. Client view of cluster state is { type=UNKNOWN, servers=[(xxxxxxxxxx), type=UNKNOWN, state=CONNECTING, exception={com .mongodb.MongoSocketReadException: Prematurely reached end of stream}}]
```

Troubleshooting Before testing the connectivity to a MongoDB connection that is not deployed in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), add relevant IP addresses to the whitelist of the connection.

### Synchronization node

#### Supported synchronization types

DataWorks supports multiple types of data synchronization, including single-table batch or real-time synchronization, full-database batch or real-time synchronization, batch or real-time synchronization of full or incremental data in a database, and real-time synchronization of tables in shared databases. The supported data sources and destinations are listed for each type. You can choose the appropriate synchronization method for various scenarios and consult the relevant configuration method.

**Note**

The supported destination types displayed in the console prevail.

**Single-table batch synchronization**

The batch synchronization feature provides readers and writers for you to read data from and write data to data sources. Supported data sources and destinations: You can configure a batch synchronization task to synchronize data of a single table between any data sources that support readers for data extraction and writers for data insertion. Configuration method: Configure a single-table batch synchronization task The single-table real-time synchronization feature allows you to use multiple source and destination data sources to build synchronization links for real-time ETL synchronization of single-table data. Supported data sources and destinations: Data destination: MaxCompute, Hologres, AnalyticDB for MySQL (V3.0), Elasticsearch, Configuration method: Configure a single-table real-time synchronization task

**Full-table batch/real-time synchronization, real-time**

**synchronization of full or incremental data in a database, and**

**real-time synchronization of data from tables in sharded**

#### Configure a batch synchronization node

**to synchronize data from a single table**

##### Configure a batch synchronization node by

**using the codeless UI**

DataWorks allows you to configure offline synchronization nodes without the need to write code. You only need to select the data source and destination in the interface, and then use the scheduling parameter to periodically synchronize full or incremental data of a single source table to the destination table. This topic describes how to configure a batch synchronization node by using the codeless UI.

**Usage notes**

You cannot use codeless UI to configure batch synchronization nodes for some data sources. After you select a data source, the system prompts that the data source does not support codeless UI. You can click the icon in the toolbar to switch to the script mode and continue to configure the node. For more information, see Configure a batch synchronization node by using the code editor. The codeless UI is easy to use but provides only limited features. If you want to make finergrained configurations for your batch synchronization node, you can click the Conversion script icon in the top toolbar of the configuration tab of the node in DataStudio to switch to the code editor and configure the node by using the code editor. The source and destination data sources that are required by the synchronization node are created. For more information, see Data sources.
1. . Create a workflow.**
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. On the **DataStudio** page, move the pointer over the
**Workflow**.
3. In the **Create Workflow** dialog box, specify the **Workflow Name** and **Description**
parameters. Then, click **Create**.
1. Find the workflow in the Business Flow pane, right-click the workflow and choose **Create**
**Node > Data Integration > Offline synchronization**.
2. In the **Create Node** dialog box, configure the **Name** parameter and click **Confirm**.
3. . Configure network connections and resources**
After you create a batch synchronization node, you must select a data source and a destination.
1. In the **Source** section, select a data source. In the **Destination** side, select a data source.

**Note**

For more information about supported data sources and destinations, see Supported data sources.
2. Select a resource group to run batch synchronization nodes.
3. Click **Next**.
4. . Configure the source and destination**
In this step, select the tables from which you want to read data and the tables to which you want to write data, and specify a filter condition when you configure the source.

**Important**

The data source and destination configurations vary based on the type of the data source. The following examples show only common configurations. The configurations and

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Specify a filter condition | If you specify a filter condition after you select the tables from which you want to read data, only the data that meets the filter condition in the tables can be synchronized. You can use a filter condition together with scheduling parameters to implement incremental synchronization. This way, the filter condition can dynamically change with the settings of the scheduling parameters, and incremental data can be synchronized. Note You can define variables in the data filtering and destination table configurations, and click Properties in the right-side navigation pane to implement incremental or full data synchronization to the destination table corresponding to the time partitioning policy. For more information about how to use scheduling parameters, see Configure scheduling parameters. The syntax of the filter condition that is used to implement incremental synchronization is almost the same as the syntax supported by a database. During data synchronization, the batch synchronization node uses a complete SQL statement that is obtained based on the filter condition to extract data from the source. If you do not specify a filter condition, full data in the source tables is synchronized by default. |

parameters of each data source in the console shall prevail.

| Specify a shard key used to shard data in a relational database | A shard key specifies a field based on which source data is sharded. After you specify a shard key, source data is sharded and distributed to multiple shards. This way, the batch synchronization node can run parallel threads to read the data in batches. Note We recommend that you use the primary key column of the table. Data can be evenly distributed to different shards based on the primary key column, instead of being intensively distributed only to specific shards. A shard key can be used to shard only data of integer data types. If you set this parameter to a field of an unsupported data type, such as a string, floating point, or date data type, PolarDB Reader ignores the setting of the shard key and uses a single thread to read data. If no shard key is specified, only a single thread is used to read data. Support of data sources for the configuration of a shard key varies based on the data source type. The instructions provided in this topic are for reference only. The instructions in the console shall prevail. |
|---|---|

| Operation | Procedure |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
| Configure SQL statements that you want to execute before and after data synchronization | DataWorks allows you to execute SQL statements before and after data is written to specific types of destinations. For example, when you configure a batch synchronization node that uses MySQL Writer, you can configure the SQL statement truncate table tablename as a statement to be executed before data is written to the destination. This statement is used to delete existing data in a specified table. You can also configure an SQL statement as a statement to be executed after data is written to the destination. |  |  |
|  |  | truncate table |  |
| Specify the write mode that is used when a conflict occurs | You can specify the write mode in which you want to write data to the destination when a conflict occurs, such as a path conflict or primary key conflict. The configuration varies based on the attributes of destinations and the support of writers. To configure this item, refer to the topic for the related writer. |  |  |

| and after data | tablename |
|---|---|

**Destination**

5. . Map the fields in the source and destination tables**
After you specify the source and destination tables, you must configure the mappings between fields in the source and destination tables.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Map Fields with the Same Name | Click Map Fields with the Same Name to establish mappings between fields with the same name. The data types of the fields must match. |
| Map Fields in the Same Line | Click Map Fields in the Same Line to establish mappings between fields in the same row. The data types of the fields must match. |
| Delete All Mappings | Click Delete All Mappings to remove the established mappings. |
| Auto Layout | Click Auto Layout. Then, the system automatically sorts the fields based on specific rules. |
| Change Fields | Click the Change Fields icon. In the Change Fields dialog box, you can manually edit the fields in the source table. Each field occupies a row. The first and the last blank rows are included, whereas other blank rows are ignored. |
| Add | You can enter constants. Each constant must be enclosed in single quotation marks ('), such as 'abc' and '123' . You can use scheduling parameters, such as ${bizdate} . You can enter functions that are supported by relational databases, such as now() and count(1) . If the field that you entered cannot be parsed, the value of Type for the field is Unidentified. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Expected Maximum Concurrency | The maximum number of parallel threads that the synchronization node can use to read data from the source or write data to the destination. You can configure the parallelism for the data synchronization node in the codeless UI. |

**Note**

Make sure that the data type of a source field is the same as that of the mapped destination field or the data type conversion is feasible.
6. . Configure channel control**
After you complete the preceding steps, you can configure channel control policies for the synchronization node.

| Bandwidth Throttling | Specifies whether to enable throttling. You can enable throttling and specify a maximum transmission rate to prevent heavy read workloads on the source. We recommend that you enable bandwidth throttling and set the maximum transmission rate to an appropriate value based on the configurations of the source. |
|---|---|
| Policy for Dirty Data Records | dirty data refers to data records that fail to be written to the destination due to exceptions such as type conflicts and constraint violations. Batch synchronization allows you to define dirty data policies to define the number of dirty data to be tolerated and the impact on nodes. Ignore Dirty Data Records: Dirty data records are ignored during data synchronization, and the batch synchronization node can continue to run if dirty data records are generated. Disallow Dirty Data Records: If dirty data records are generated during data synchronization, the batch synchronization node fails. Allow Limited Dirty Data Records: Specify the maximum number of tolerable dirty data records. If the number of dirty data records that are generated during data synchronization is less than or equal to the value that you specified, the dirty data records are ignored and are not written to the destination, and the batch synchronization node continues to run. If the number of dirty data records that are generated during data synchronization is greater than the value that you specified, the batch synchronization node fails. Important If a large amount of dirty data is generated during data synchronization, the overall data synchronization speed is affected. |
| Distributed Execution | Specifies whether to enable the distributed execution mode for the batch synchronization node. Enable: In distributed execution mode, your node slices can be divided into multiple processes for concurrent execution. This breaks the bottleneck of single-process execution and improves the synchronization efficiency. Disable: Processes are executed one by one. If you have a high requirement for data synchronization performance, you can use the distributed execution mode to run your batch synchronization node. If you run your batch synchronization node in distributed execution mode, fragment resources of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances can be utilized. This improves resource utilization. Important The distributed execution mode can be enabled only if the maximum number of parallel threads that you specified is greater than or equal to 8. If you enable the distributed execution mode for a batch synchronization node, more resources will be occupied. If an out of memory (OOM) error is reported during the running of the batch synchronization node, you can disable the distributed execution mode. |

In the Properties panel, you can configure the properties of the synchronization node, such as the recurrence, time when the synchronization node is run, and dependencies. To filter data based on a scheduling parameter, perform the following steps to configure a **scheduling**
**parameter**:
1. On the configuration tab of the batch synchronization node, click **Properties** in the right-
side navigation pane.
2. You can specify a variable in scheduling parameters in the format of ${Variable name} .
After a variable is specified, enter the initial value of the variable in the corresponding field. In this example, the initial value of the variable is identified by $[] . The content can be a time expression or a constant. For example, if you write ${today} in the code and enter today=$[yyyymmdd] in the corresponding field, the value of the time variable is the current date. For more information about how to add or subtract the date, see Configure scheduling parameters.
3. After the synchronization node is configured, save and commit the node.

```json
}
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

**Note**

Each operator is defined in the `steps` . At least one `Reader` and one `Writer` are required. Assume that you set the concurrency to 2. Then, a job has two parallel data processing streams, and each Reader and Writer belongs to a `step` in the node configuration. The `steps` define the type and parameters of each operator. The data synchronization and processing process strictly follow the order of each `step` in the JSON configuration. Configure the Reader. Configure the Writer.

**Note**

Some synchronization nodes may need to synchronize incremental data. In this case, you can use the scheduling parameters of DataWorks to specify the date and time for incremental data synchronization. For more information, see Overview of scheduling parameters.

**Map the fields in the source and destination tables.**

The code editor supports only the mappings of fields in the same row. The data types of the fields must match.

**Note**

Make sure that the data type of a source field is the same as that of the mapped destination field or the data type conversion is feasible.

**Step 6: Configure channel control policies**

After the preceding steps are performed, you can configure the channel control policies for the synchronization node. The `setting` parameter specifies node efficiency parameters, including the number of parallel threads, bandwidth throttling, dirty data policy, and resource group.

```json
"setting": {
        "errorLimit": {
            "record": "1024"   // The maximum number of dirty data records allowed.
        },
        "speed": {
            "throttle": false,   // The synchronization rate. false indicates that the
synchronization rate is unlimited.
            "concurrent": 1 // The expected maximum parallelism of the node.
        }
    },
```

| Expected Maximum Concurrency | The maximum number of parallel threads that the synchronization node can use to read data from the source or write data to the destination. You can configure the parallelism for the data synchronization node in the codeless UI. |
|---|---|
| Bandwidth Throttling | Specifies whether to enable throttling. You can enable throttling and specify a maximum transmission rate to prevent heavy read workloads on the source. We recommend that you enable bandwidth throttling and set the maximum transmission rate to an appropriate value based on the configurations of the source. |
| Policy for Dirty Data Records | dirty data refers to data records that fail to be written to the destination due to exceptions such as type conflicts and constraint violations. Batch synchronization allows you to define dirty data policies to define the number of dirty data to be tolerated and the impact on nodes. Ignore Dirty Data Records: Dirty data records are ignored during data synchronization, and the batch synchronization node can continue to run if dirty data records are generated. Disallow Dirty Data Records: If dirty data records are generated during data synchronization, the batch synchronization node fails. Allow Limited Dirty Data Records: Specify the maximum number of tolerable dirty data records. If the number of dirty data records that are generated during data synchronization is less than or equal to the value that you specified, the dirty data records are ignored and are not written to the destination, and the batch synchronization node continues to run. If the number of dirty data records that are generated during data synchronization is greater than the value that you specified, the batch synchronization node fails. Important If a large amount of dirty data is generated during data synchronization, the overall data synchronization speed is affected. |

In the Properties panel, you can configure the properties of the synchronization node, such as the recurrence, time when the synchronization node is run, and dependencies. To filter data based on a scheduling parameter, perform the following steps to configure a **scheduling**
**parameter**:
1. On the configuration tab of the batch synchronization node, click **Properties** in the right-
side navigation pane.
2. You can specify a variable in scheduling parameters in the format of ${Variable name} .
After a variable is specified, enter the initial value of the variable in the corresponding field. In this example, the initial value of the variable is identified by $[] . The content can be a time expression or a constant. For example, if you write ${today} in the code and enter today=$[yyyymmdd] in the corresponding field, the value of the time variable is the current date. For more information about how to add or subtract the date, see Configure scheduling parameters.
3. After the synchronization node is configured, save and commit the node.

##### Configure a batch synchronization node to

**synchronize data from tables in sharded databases**

DataWorks allows you to configure a batch synchronization node by using the codeless user interface (UI) or code editor to synchronize data from tables in sharded databases to a single table. This topic uses MySQL as an example to describe how to configure a batch synchronization node in the DataWorks console to synchronize data from tables in sharded databases. The data sources from which you want to read data and to which you want to write data are prepared. For more information, see Supported data sources.

**Background information**

The following table compares the configuration methods of batch synchronization nodes for synchronizing data from tables in sharded databases to a single table.

| Supported data source types | MySQL, PolarDB, and AnalyticDB | MySQL, PolarDB, AnalyticDB, SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, DM, DB2, and Oracle |
|---|---|---|

**Common data source + codeless UI**

1. Add each desired database to DataWorks as a common data source. In this example, a
MySQL data source is used. For more information, see Add a MySQL data source.
2. Log in to the DataWorks console.
3. Find and right-click the workflow, and choose **Create Node > Data Integration >**
**Offline synchronization**.
4. In the **Create Node** dialog box, configure the **Name** parameter and click **Confirm**.
5. Configure a synchronization node to synchronize data from tables in sharded databases.
Configure the synchronization node by using the codeless UI. In the **Configure Network**
**Connections and Resource Group** step, click **Edit Source** to select multiple data
sources after you select the source type. For more information about how to configure the synchronization node, see Configure a batch synchronization node by using the codeless UI.
6. In the Edit Data Source dialog box, select the desired data sources in the Data Sources to
Be Selected list and click the rightward arrow to move the selected data sources to the
**Selected Data Sources** list. Then, click **OK**.
7. Click **Next**.
8. In the Configure tasks step, select the tables from which you want to synchronize data in
each selected data source in the Source section, and configure the parameters in the Destination section. Then, **save** and **deploy** the synchronization node and perform subsequent operations.

**Important**

The **Data Sources for Sharded Databases Use Same Account and Password** option is selected by default, which indicates that all sharded data sources use the account and password configured in the first data source to access the database. If your sharded databases use different accounts and passwords, clear the check box and use the account and password of each data source to access the database.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. Find and right-click the workflow, and choose **Create Node > Data Integration >**
**Offline synchronization**.
3. In the **Create Node** dialog box, configure the **Name** parameter and click **Confirm**.
4. Click the
icon in the top toolbar of the configuration tab of the node in DataStudio to switch to the code editor and configure the node by using the code editor.
5. Configure a synchronization node to synchronize data from tables in sharded databases.

**Parameters in code for AnalyticDB for MySQL V3.0 Reader**

| splitPk | The field that is used for data sharding when AnalyticDB for MySQL 3.0 Reader reads data. If you specify this parameter, the source table is sharded based on the value of this parameter. Data Integration then runs parallel threads to read data. This way, data can be synchronized more efficiently. We recommend that you set the splitPk parameter to the name of the primary key column of the table. Data can be evenly distributed to different shards based on the primary key column, instead of being intensively distributed only to specific shards. The splitPk parameter supports sharding for data only of integer data types. If you set the splitPk parameter to a field of an unsupported data type, such as a string, floating point, or date data type, the setting of this parameter is ignored, and a single thread is used to read data. If the splitPk parameter is not provided or is left empty, a single thread is used to read data. | No | None |
|---|---|---|---|
| where | The WHERE clause. For example, you can set this parameter to gmt create > $bizdate to read the data that is generated _ on the current day. You can use the WHERE clause to read incremental data. If the where parameter is not provided or is left empty, AnalyticDB for MySQL 3.0 Reader reads all data. Do not set the where parameter to limit 10. This value does not conform to the constraints of MySQL on the SQL WHERE clause. | No | None |

| Category | AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL data type |
|---|---|
| Integer | BIGINT, BIGSERIAL, INTEGER, SMALLINT, SERIAL, and GEOMETRY |
| Floating point | DOUBLE, PRECISION, MONEY, NUMERIC, and REAL |

An example JDBC URL is jdbc:OceanBase://127.0.0.1:3306/database. You must specify either jdbcUrl or username . | No | None |
| username | The username that you can use to connect to the database. | No | None |
| password | The password that you can use to connect to the database. | No | None |
| table | The name of the table from which you want to read data. ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader can read data from multiple tables. The tables are specified in a JSON array. If you specify multiple tables, make sure that the tables have the same schema. ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader does not check whether the tables have the same schema. Note The table parameter must be included in the connection parameter. | Yes | None |

**Parameters in code for ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader**

| column | The names of the columns from which you want to read data. Specify the names in a JSON array. The default value is [ * ], which indicates all the columns in the source table. You can select specific columns to read. The column order can be changed. This indicates that you can specify columns in an order different from the order specified by the schema of the source table. Constants are supported. Example: '123'. Functions are supported. Example: date('now'). The column parameter must explicitly specify all the columns from which you want to read data. The parameter cannot be left empty. | Yes | None |
|---|---|---|---|
| splitPk | The field that is used for data sharding when ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader reads data. If you configure this parameter, the source table is sharded based on the value of this parameter. Data Integration then runs parallel threads to read data. This improves data synchronization efficiency. We recommend that you set the splitPk parameter to the name of a primary key column of the table. Data can be evenly distributed to different shards based on the primary key column, instead of being intensively distributed only to specific shards. The splitPk parameter supports sharding for data only of integer data types. If you set this parameter to a field of an unsupported data type, such as a string, floating point, or date data type, ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader returns an error. If you leave the splitPk parameter empty, ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader uses a single thread to read data. | No | None |
| supportNorm alSplitForSin gleTable | If the number of parallel threads is less than the number of tables, the setting of the splitPk parameter does not take effect. If you want to forcibly run parallel threads to read source data, we recommend that you set this parameter to true . | No | None |
| where | The WHERE clause. ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader generates an SQL statement based on the column, table, and where parameters that you have configured and uses the generated statement to read data. For example, when you perform a test, you can set the where parameter to limit 10. To read the data that is generated on the current day, you can set the where parameter to gmt create > $bizdate . _ You can use the WHERE clause to read incremental data. If the where parameter is not provided or is left empty, all data is read. | No | None |

| querySql | The SQL statement that is used for refined data filtering. If you configure this parameter, ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader filters data based only on the value of this parameter. If you configure this parameter, ApsaraDB for OceanBase Reader ignores the settings of the table, column, where, and splitPk parameters. | No | None |
|---|---|---|---|
| fetchSize | The number of data records to read at a time. This parameter determines the number of interactions between Data Integration and the database and affects read efficiency. Note If you set this parameter to a value greater than 2048, an out of memory (OOM) error may occur during data synchronization. | No | 1,024 |

| Data type | PolarDB-X data type |
|---|---|
| Integer | INT, TINYINT, SMALLINT, MEDIUMINT, and BIGINT |
| Floating point | FLOAT, DOUBLE, and DECIMAL |
| String | VARCHAR, CHAR, TINYTEXT, TEXT, MEDIUMTEXT, and LONGTEXT |
| Date and time | DATE, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP, TIME, and YEAR |
| Boolean | BIT and BOOLEAN |

The following sample DDL statements are used to create a partitioned Hologres table:

```bash
begin; drop table if exists holo_reader_basic_part_src;
  tag text not null,
  id int not null,
  title text not null,
  body text,
  primary key (tag, id))
  partition by list( tag );
  call set_table_property('holo_reader_basic_part_src', 'orientation', 'column');
  call set_table_property('holo_reader_basic_part_src', 'shard_count', '3');
commit; create table holo_reader_basic_part_src_1583161774228 partition of holo_reader_basic_part_src for values in ('foo');
# Make sure that the child partitioned table from which you want to read data is cr
eated and data is inserted into the child partitioned table.
 Column |  Type   | Collation | Nullable | Default | Storage  | Stats target | Desc
--------+---------+-----------+----------+---------+----------+--------------+------- -----

 body   | text    |           |          |         | extended |              |
Partition key: LIST (tag) Indexes:

Partitions: holo_reader_basic_part_src_1583161774228 FOR VALUES IN ('foo')
```

| column | The names of the columns from which you want to read data. The names of the primary key columns in the source Hologres table must be included. If you want to read data from all columns in the source Hologres table, set this parameter to ["*"] . | Yes | None |
|---|---|---|---|
| partition | The partition key column and the related value of the source Hologres table, in the format of column=value . This parameter is valid only for partitioned tables. Important Hologres supports only list partitioning. You can specify only one column as the partition key column. The data type of the partition key column must be INT4 or TEXT. The value of this parameter must match the partition filter expression in the DDL statements that are used to create the source Hologres table. You must specify a child partitioned table that exists and contains data. | Not supporte d | Left empty, which indicates that the source Hologres table is a non- partitioned table |

###### Configure MaxCompute Reader

MaxCompute Reader reads data from MaxCompute data sources. This topic describes the parameters in MaxCompute Reader.

**Limits**

MaxCompute Reader can read data from only partitioned and non-partitioned tables. It cannot read virtual views or read data from foreign tables. When you configure a batch synchronization task used to synchronize data from a MaxCompute partitioned table, you cannot directly configure mappings between the partition fields in the partitioned table and fields in a destination table. You must specify information about the partition from which you want to synchronize data when you configure the source. For example, a partitioned table named t0 contains the id and name fields. The level-1 partition field is pt and the level-2 partition field is ds. If you want to read data from the partition pt=1,ds=hangzhou in the t0 table, you must specify pt=1,ds=hangzhou when you configure the source. This way, you can configure mappings for the id and name fields later.

| Field type | MaxCompute Reader for batch data read |
|---|---|
| BIGINT | Supported |
| DOUBLE | Supported |
| DECIMAL | Supported |
| STRING | Supported |
| DATETIME | Supported |
| BOOLEAN | Supported |
| ARRAY | Supported |
| MAP | Supported |
| STRUCT | Supported |

| Data type | MaxCompute Reader for batch data read |
|---|---|
| TINYINT | Supported |
| SMALLINT | Supported |
| INT | Supported |
| BIGINT | Supported |

**Supported data types**

The following data type editions are supported: MaxCompute V1.0 data type edition, MaxCompute V2.0 data type edition, and Hive-compatible data type edition. This section provides the support status of data types of each edition.

**MaxCompute V2.0 data type edition and Hive-compatible data**

**type edition**

| BINARY | Supported |
|---|---|
| FLOAT | Supported |
| DOUBLE | Supported |
| DECIMAL(pecision, scale) | Supported |
| VARCHAR(n) | Supported |
| CHAR(n) | Not supported |
| STRING | Supported |
| DATE | Supported |
| DATETIME | Supported |
| TIMESTAMP | Supported |
| BOOLEAN | Supported |
| ARRAY | Supported |
| MAP | Supported |
| STRUCT | Supported |

| Category | Data Integration data type | MaxCompute data type |
|---|---|---|
| Integer | LONG | BIGINT, INT, TINYINT, and SMALLINT |
| Boolean | BOOLEAN | BOOLEAN |

**Data type mappings**

The following table lists the data type mappings based on which MaxCompute Reader converts data types.

| Date and time | DATE | DATETIME, TIMESTAMP, and DATE |
|---|---|---|
| Floating point | DOUBLE | FLOAT, DOUBLE, and DECIMAL |
| Binary | BYTES | BINARY |
| Complex | STRING | ARRAY, MAP, and STRUCT |

**Important**

If the data conversion fails or the data fails to be written to the destination, the data is regarded as dirty data. You can specify the maximum number of dirty data records allowed.

|  |  | partition | The partitions from which you want to read data. You can use Linux Shell wildcards to specify the partitions. An asterisk ( * ) indicates multiple numbers of characters, and a question mark ( ? ) indicates a single character. The partitions that you specify must exist in the source table. Otherwise, the system reports an error for the synchronization node. If you want the synchronization node to be successfully run even if the partitions that you specify do not exist in the source table, use the code editor to modify the code of the synchronization node. In addition, you must add "successOnNoPartition": true to the configurations of MaxCompute Reader. For example, the partitioned table test contains four partitions: pt=1,ds=hangzhou, pt=1,ds=shanghai, pt=2,ds=hangzhou, and pt=2,ds=beijing. In this case, you can configure the partition parameter based on the following instructions: To read data from the partition pt=1,ds=hangzhou, specify "partition":"pt=1,ds=hangzhou" . To read data from all the ds partitions in the pt=1 partition, specify "partition":"pt=1,ds=*" . To read data from all the partitions in the test table, specify "partition":"pt=*,ds=*" . You can also specify other conditions to read data from partitions based on your business requirements. To read data from the partition that stores the largest amount of data, add /*query*/ ds=(select MAX(ds) from DataXODPSReaderPPR) to the configurations of MaxCompute Reader. To filter data based on filter conditions, add /*query*/ pt+Expression to the configuration of MaxCompute Reader. For example, /*query*/ pt>=20170101 and pt<20170110 indicates that you want to read the data that is generated from January 1, 2017 to January 9, 2017 from all the pt partitions in the test table. Note MaxCompute Reader processes the content after /*query*/ as a WHERE clause. |  |  | If the MaxCo mpute table is partiti oned, specif y this param eter. To read the data in the columns in sequence, specify "column":["id","name","age"] or "column": ["*"] . Note We recommend that you do not use "column":["*"]. If you specify "column":["*"], MaxCompute Reader reads data from all the columns in a source table in sequence. If the column order, data type, or number of columns is changed in the source table, the columns in the source and destination tables may be inconsistent. As a result, the data synchronization node may fail, or the data synchronization results do not meet your expectations. To read the name and id fields in sequence, enter "column":["name","id"] . You can add constant fields to the source table to establish mappings between the source table columns and destination table columns. In this case, when you configure the column parameter, you must enclose each constant in single quotation marks ( ' ). For example, if you add the constant 1988-08-08 08:08:08 to the source table and want to read data from the age, name, 1988-08-08 08:08:08, and id columns in sequence, specify "column": ["age","name","'1988-08-08 08:08:08'","id"] . The single quotation marks ( ' ) are used to identify constant columns. When MaxCompute Reader reads data from the source table, the constant column values that are read by MaxCompute Reader exclude the single quotation marks ( ' ). Note MaxCompute functions are supported in column when data filtering is enabled ( enableWhere=true and the WHERE clause is not empty). When data filtering is disabled, MaxCompute functions are not supported. The column parameter must explicitly specify all the columns from which you want to read data. Object Storage Service (OSS) Reader reads data from OSS data sources. This topic describes the parameters in OSS Reader.

**Data type mappings and limits**

OSS Reader reads data from OSS and converts the data to a format that is readable to Data Integration. OSS stores only unstructured data. The following table lists the features that are supported and not supported by OSS Reader:

**Important**

If data in OSS is stored as CSV files, the data must comply with the standard CSV format. For example, if the data in a column of a CSV file is enclosed in a pair of single quotation marks (' '), you must replace this pair of single quotation marks with a pair of double quotation marks (" "). Otherwise, the data in the CSV file may be incorrectly parsed. OSS is an unstructured data source that stores file-based data. Before you synchronize data from an OSS data source, you must check whether the field structure meets your expectation. If the field structure in an unstructured data source changes, you must re-confirm the field structure when you configure a synchronization task. Otherwise, the synchronized data may be out of order.
