| datasource | The name of the data source. It must be the same as the name of the added data source. You can add data sources by using the code editor. |  | Enable | No default value |
| table | The name of the table to which you want to write data. |  | Enable | No default value |
| writeMode | The write mode. Valid values: insert, replace, and update. insert: If no primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, data is directly written to the destination table. If a primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, data that you want to write to the destination table is automatically ignored and no update is performed. replace: If no primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, data is directly written to the destination table. If a primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, rows that contain the conflicting data are deleted and then new rows are inserted. This indicates that all fields of the original rows are replaced with new rows. update: If no primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, data is directly written to the destination table. If a primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, all fields of the original rows are replaced with new rows. Note This mode is supported only in script mode. |  | No | insert |
| column | The names of the columns to which you want to write data. Separate the names with commas (,), such as "column": ["id", "name", "age"] . If you want to write data to all the columns in the destination table, set this parameter to an asterisk (*), such as "column": ["*"] . Note If the column name contains select, enclose the column name in backticks (`). For example, item select no is _ _ presented as `item select no`. _ _ |  |  | No default value |
|  |  | "column": |  |  |
|  |  |  | Enable |  |

|  | ["id", "name", "age"] |
|---|---|

You can execute only one SQL statement on the codeless UI and multiple SQL statements in the code editor. Note If you specify multiple SQL statements, the statements are not executed in the same transaction. | No | No default value. |
|---|---|---|---|
| postSql | The SQL statement that you want to execute after the batch synchronization task is run. For example, you can set this parameter to the SQL statement that is used to add a timestamp. You can execute only one SQL statement on the codeless UI and multiple SQL statements in the code editor. Note If you configure multiple SQL statements, the statements are not executed in the same transaction. | No | No default value. |
| batchSize | The number of data records to write at a time. Set this parameter to an appropriate value based on your business requirements. This greatly reduces the interactions between Data Integration and MySQL and increases throughput. If you set this parameter to an excessively large value, an out of memory (OOM) error may occur during data synchronization. | No | 1,024 |

###### Configure DRDS Writer

The DRDS Writer plug-in is used to write data to a DRDS data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

Currently, the DRDS plug-in is only suitable for MySQL engine scenarios. DRDS is a set of distributed MySQL databases, and most communication protocols follow MySQL usage scenarios. At the underlying implementation level, DRDS Writer connects to the proxy of a remote DRDS database through JDBC and executes the corresponding `replace into` statement to write data to DRDS. The SQL statement that is executed is a `replace into` . To avoid repeated data writes, your table must have a primary key or a unique index. DRDS Writer obtains the protocol data generated by Reader through the data synchronization framework, and writes the data to DRDS by using the `replace into` (if no primary key or unique index conflict occurs, the behavior is the same as that of `insert` `into` . If a conflict occurs, all fields of the original row are replaced with new rows) statement. DRDS Writer sends data to the DRDS proxy when the amount of buffered data reaches a specific threshold. The proxy determines whether to write the data to one or more tables and how to route the data when the data is written to multiple tables.

**Note**

A synchronization task that uses DRDS Writer must have at least the permissions to execute the `REPLACE INTO` statement. Whether other permissions are required depends on the statements that you specify in preSql and postSql when you configure the task.

###### Configure DataHub Writer

DataHub Writer writes data to a DataHub data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

STRING strings support only UTF-8 encoding. The maximum size of a single STRING column is 1MB.

**Supported field types**

When you synchronize data from DataHub, DataHub synchronizes data to the corresponding data type based on the data type of the DataHub field. DataHub supports only the **BIGINT**,
**STRING**, **BOOLEAN**, **DOUBLE**, **TIMESTAMP**, and **DECIMAL** data types.

Data Integration can accumulate before it commits the data to the destination. Unit: by tes.
                 // DataHub allows for a maximum of 10,000 data records to be written in
a single request. If the number of data records exceeds 10,000, the synchronization tas k fails. In this case, the maximum amount of data that can be written in a single reque st is calculated by using the following formula: Average amount of data in a single dat a record × 10,000. You need to set maxCommitSize to a value less than the maximum amoun t of data calculated. This ensures that the number of data records to be written in a s ingle request does not exceed 10,000. For example, if the data size of a single data re cord is 10 KB, the value of this parameter must be less than the result of 10 multiplie d by 10,000.

| partition | The partition key column and the related value in the destination Hologres table. Configure this parameter in the format of column=value . This parameter is valid only for partitioned tables. Note Hologres supports only list partitioning. You can specify only one column as the partition key column. The data type of the partition key column must be INT4 or TEXT. The value of this parameter must match the partition filter expression in the DDL statements that are used to create the destination Hologres table. | No | Empty, indicating non- partition table |
|---|---|---|---|
| reShuffleByD istributionKe y | In Hologres, batch import of primary key tables triggers a table lock by default. This limits the concurrent write capability of multiple connections. You can enable the reShuffle feature to allow different tasks to write data to the specified Holo shard based on the data shard key in offline synchronization scenarios. In this way, concurrent batch writes can be implemented, which significantly improves the write performance. Compared with real-time writing in traditional JDBC mode, enabling this feature not only reduces the load on the Holo server, but also further improves the writing efficiency. Important This feature is enabled only for Serverless resource groups. | No | false |

| truncate | Indicates whether the destination table needs to be cleared before writing data to the Holo table. true: clears the destination table. Note Currently, you can only clear non- partition table and static partition table, but not dynamic partition table. If you use dynamic partition table and set the parameter value to true, the synchronization task will crash. If you use a static partition table and set the parameter value to true, the data in the child table of the partition is cleared. The data in the parent table is not cleared. false: does not clear the destination table. | No | false |
|---|---|---|---|

###### Configure MaxCompute Writer

MaxCompute Writer writes data to MaxCompute data sources. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

If the data has a null value, MaxCompute Writer does not support the VARCHAR type. If the table to be written is a `DeltaTable` , set **Synchronization Completed** to **Yes**. Otherwise, the task will report an error if the concurrency is greater than 1.

**Supported field types**

MaxCompute supports 1.0 data types, 2.0 data types, and Hive-compatible data types. The following table shows the field types supported by different data type editions.

| BIGINT | Yes. |
|---|---|
| DOUBLE | Yes. |
| DECIMAL | Yes. |
| STRING | Yes. |
| DATETIME | Yes. |
| BOOLEAN | Yes. |
| ARRAY | Yes. |
| MAP | Yes. |
| STRUCT | Yes. |

| Field Type | MaxCompute Writer for batch data write |
|---|---|
| TINYINT | Yes. |
| SMALLINT | Yes. |
| INT | Yes. |
| BIGINT | Yes. |
| BINARY | Yes. |
| FLOAT | Yes. |
| DOUBLE | Yes. |
| DECIMAL(pecision,scale) | Yes. |

**type edition**

| VARCHAR(n) | Yes. |
|---|---|

| DATETIME | Yes. |
| TIMESTAMP | Yes. |
| BOOLEAN | Yes. |
| ARRAY | Yes. |
| MAP | Yes. |
| STRUCT | Yes. |

| datasource | The name of the data source. It must be the same as the name of the added data source. You can add data sources by using the code editor. | Enable | No default value |
|---|---|---|---|
| table | The name of the table to which you want to write data. The name is not case-sensitive. You can specify only one table. | Enable | No default value |
| partition | The names of the partitions to which you want to write data. The last-level partition must be specified. For example, if you want to write data to a table with three-level partitions, set the partition parameter to a value that contains the third-level partition information, such as pt=20150101, type=1, biz=2 . To write data to a non-partitioned table, do not configure this parameter. The data is directly written to the destination table. MaxCompute Writer does not support data write operations based on the partition route. To write data to a partitioned table, make sure that the data is written to the lowest-level partition. | Required only for partitioned tables If the MaxCompute table is not partitioned, do not specify this parameter. | None |
| column | The names of the columns to which you want to write data. To write data to all the columns in the destination table, enter "column": ["*"] . To write data to specific columns in the destination table, set this parameter to the names of the columns and separate the names with commas (,), such as "column": ["id","name"] . MaxCompute Writer can filter columns and change the order of columns. For example, a MaxCompute table has three columns: a, b, and c. If you want to write data only to Column c and Column b, you can enter "column": ["c","b"] . During data synchronization, the values in Column a are automatically set to NULL. The column parameter must explicitly specify all the columns to which you want to write data. The parameter cannot be left empty. | Enable | No default value |

| "column": |  |
|---|---|

|  | ["*"] |
|---|---|

| "column": |  |
|---|---|

|  | ["id","name"] |
|---|---|

| truncate | To ensure the idempotence of write operations, set the truncate parameter to true. If a failed synchronization node is rerun due to a write failure, MaxCompute Writer deletes the data that has been written to the destination table and writes the source data again. This ensures that the same data is written for each rerun. MaxCompute Writer uses MaxCompute SQL to delete data. MaxCompute SQL cannot ensure data atomicity. Therefore, the TRUNCATE operation is not an atomic operation. Conflicts may occur when multiple synchronization tasks delete data from the same table or partition in parallel. To prevent this issue, we recommend that you do not execute multiple DDL statements to write data to the same partition at the same time. You can create different partitions for synchronization tasks that need to run in parallel in advance. | Enable | No default value |
|---|---|---|---|

**ORC or Parquet files are written to OSS**

You can use HDFS Writer to write ORC or Parquet files to OSS. In addition to the existing parameters of OSS Writer, extended configuration parameters such as **Path** and **FileFormat** are added. The following example shows how to write an ORC or Parquet file to OSS:

**Important**

The following code is only for reference. You can modify the parameters based on your business requirements. Write an ORC file to OSS If you want to write ORC files to OSS, you can use only the code editor. You must set the
**fileFormat** parameter to `orc` , the **path** parameter to the path where the file to be
written is stored, and the **column** parameter to a value in the `{"name":"your column` `name","type": "your column type"}` format. The following table lists the data types of data in ORC files that OSS Writer can write to OSS.

| BOOLEAN | Yes. |
|---|---|
| DECIMAL | Yes. |
| BINARY | Yes. |

```json
{ "stepType": "oss", "parameter": { "datasource": "", "fileFormat": "orc", "path": "/tests/case61", "fileName": "orc", "writeMode": "append", "column": [ { "name": "col1", "type": "BIGINT" }, { "name": "col2", "type": "DOUBLE" }, { "name": "col3", "type": "STRING" }
```

`],`

```json
"writeMode": "append", "fieldDelimiter": "\t", "compress": "NONE", "encoding": "UTF-8" } }
```

Write a Parquet file to OSS

| Parameter s | Describe | Requi red | Default value |
|---|---|---|---|
| datasource | The name of the data source. It must be the same as the name of the added data source. You can add data sources by using the code editor. | Enable | No default value |
| object | The prefix for the names of the files that you want to write to OSS. OSS simulates the directory effect by adding delimiters to file names. Examples: If you use "object": "datax" , the written object starts with datax and adds a random string to the suffix. If you use "object": "cdo/datax" , the written object starts with a /cdo/datax and randomly adds a string to the suffix. The delimiter used to simulate a directory in OSS is (/). If you do not need a random UUID suffix, we recommend that you configure "writeSingleObject" : "true" . For more information, see writeSingleObject. | Yes | None |

```json
{ "stepType": "oss", "parameter": { "datasource": "", "fileFormat": "parquet", "path": "/tests/case61", "fileName": "test", "writeMode": "append", "fieldDelimiter": "\t", "compress": "SNAPPY", "encoding": "UTF-8", "parquetSchema": "message test { required int64 int64_col;\n required binary str_col (UTF8);\nrequired group params (MAP) {\nrepeated group key_value {\nrequired binary k ey (UTF8);\nrequired binary value (UTF8);\n}\n}\nrequired group params_arr (LIST) {\n repeated group list {\nrequired binary element (UTF8);\n}\n}\nrequired group params_s truct {\nrequired int64 id;\n required binary name (UTF8);\n }\nrequired group params _arr_complex (LIST) {\nrepeated group list {\nrequired group element {\n required int 64 id;\n required binary name (UTF8);\n}\n}\n}\nrequired group params_complex (MAP) { \nrepeated group key_value {\nrequired binary key (UTF8);\nrequired group value {\nre quired int64 id;\n required binary name (UTF8);\n}\n}\n}\nrequired group params_struct_complex {\nrequired int64 id;\n required group detail {\nrequired int64 id;\n required binary name (UTF8);\n}\n}\n}", "dataxParquetMode": "fields" } }
```

| ossBlockSi ze | The block size of OSS. The default block size is 16MB. If the file is written in the parquet or ORC format, you can configure this parameter at the same level as the object parameter. OSS supports a maximum of 10000 blocks. By default, the maximum size of a file is 160GB. If the number of chunks exceeds the limit, you can adjust the chunk size to support larger file uploads. | No | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| writeMode | The write mode. Valid values: truncate: OSS Writer deletes all existing objects whose names start with the specified prefix before it writes files to OSS. For example, if you set the object parameter to abc, OSS Writer deletes all the objects whose names start with abc before it writes files to OSS. append: OSS Writer writes all files to OSS and suffixes the file names with random UUIDs to ensure that the names of the files are different from the names of existing objects. For example, if you set the object parameter to DI, the actual names of the files written to OSS are in the DI **** **** **** format. _ _ _ nonConflict: If OSS contains objects whose names start with the specified prefix, OSS Writer returns an error. For example, if you set the object parameter to abc and OSS contains an object named abc123, OSS Writer returns an error. | Enable | No default value |
| writeSingl eObject | Specifies whether to write a single file to OSS at a time. Valid values: true: indicates that a single file is written. If no data is read, an empty file is not generated. false: writes multiple files to OSS at a time. If no data is read and a file header is configured, an empty file that contains only the file header is generated. Otherwise, an empty file is generated. Note The writeSingleObject parameter does not take effect for ORC or Parquet files. This indicates that you cannot write a single ORC or Parquet file to OSS if multiple threads are used at a time to synchronize data. If you want to write a single file, you can set the concurrent parameter to 1. In this case, a random suffix is added to the file name. However, the data synchronization speed is affected. | No | false |

| fileFormat | The format in which the file is written. The following formats are supported: csv: Only the strict csv format is supported. If the data to be written contains column delimiters, the column delimiters are escaped based on the escape syntax of the csv. The escape symbol is a double quotation mark ("). text: The column delimiter is used to split the data to be written. If the data to be written includes the column delimiter, the column delimiter is not escaped. parquet: If you use this file type, you must add the parquetSchema parameter to define the data type. Important When you write data of the parquet type, you must switch to the script mode and configure parquetSchema. If you do not configure the parquetSchema parameter, DataWorks converts the data types of the source fields based on specific policies. ORC: If you use this format, you need to switch to script mode. | No | text |
|---|---|---|---|
| compress | The compression type of the files that you want to write to OSS. This parameter is available only in the code editor. Note CSV and text files cannot be compressed. Parquet and ORC files can be compressed in a format such as Snappy and GZIP. | No | No default value. |
| fieldDelimi ter | The column delimiter that is used in the files that you want to write to OSS. | No | , |
| encoding | Write out the encoding configuration of the file. | No | utf-8 |

| parquetSc hema | A required item that is written to OSS in the Parquet file format. It is used to describe the structure of the target file. Therefore, this item takes effect only when the fileFormat is parquet. The format is as follows: message MessageType { Required, data type, column name; ......................; } Fields: MessageTypeName: the name of the MessageType object. required: indicates that the column cannot be left empty. You can also specify optional based on your business requirements. We recommend that you specify optional for all columns. dataType: Parquet files support various data types, such as BOOLEAN, INT32, INT64, INT96, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BINARY, and FIXED LEN BYTE ARRAY. Set this parameter to BINARY if _ _ _ the column stores strings. Note Each line, including the last line, must end with a semicolon (;). Sample code: message m { optional int64 id; optional int64 date id; _ optional binary datetimestring; optional int32 dspId; optional int32 advertiserId; optional int32 status; optional int64 bidding req num; _ _ optional int64 imp; optional int64 click num; _ } | No | No default value. |
|---|---|---|---|
| nullFormat | The string that represents a null pointer. No standard strings can represent a null pointer in text files. You can use this parameter to define a string that represents a null pointer. For example, if you set nullFormat to null , Data Integration considers null as a null pointer. | No | No default value. |
| header | The headers in the files that you want to write to OSS. Example: ['id', 'name', 'age'] . | No | No default value. |

| maxFileSiz e (advanced parameter, which is available only in the code editor) | The maximum size of a single object file when the object is written to OSS. The default value is 10,000*10MB. This is similar to how you control the size of a log file when you print a log4j log. When OSS is uploaded in chunks, the size of each chunk is 10MB (which is also the minimum granularity of log rotation files, that is, a maxFileSize smaller than 10MB will be used as 10MB). The maximum number of chunks supported by each OSS InitiateMultipartUploadRequest is 10,000. When rotation occurs, the object name rule is to concatenate suffixes such as 1, 2, 3 based on the original object prefix _ _ _ plus a random number of UUIDs. Note The default unit is MB. Configuration example:"maxFileSize":300, which indicates that the size of a single file is set to 300 MB. The maxFileSize takes effect only for the CSV and TEXT formats. It is based on the memory level of the synchronization task process and cannot accurately control the actual size of the target file. When actually writing a target, the file size may be larger than expected due to data expansion. | No | 100,000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| suffix (advanced configuratio n, not supported in wizard mode) | The file name extension that is generated when data is written out synchronously. For example, if the configuration suffix is .csv, the final written-out file name is fileName****.csv. | No | None |

| Data type after conversion | Parquet type | Parquet logical type |
|---|---|---|
| CHAR / VARCHAR / STRING | BINARY | UTF8 |
| BOOLEAN | BOOLEAN | N/A |
| BINARY / VARBINARY | BINARY | N/A |

###### Configuration OSS-HDFS Writer

OSS-HDFS Writer plug-ins write data to OSS-HDFS data sources. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

When using OSS-HDFS Writer, note the following: Currently, OSS-HDFS Writer only supports text, orc, and parquet files, and the file content must be a logical two‑dimensional table. For the TEXT type, make sure that the delimiter used to write data to the OSS-HDFS file is the same as the delimiter used to create a table in Hive. This way, data in the written OSS- HDFS can be associated with fields in the Hive table.

To associate the columns in a file with those in a Hive table, set the path parameter to the storage path of the Hive table in OSS-HDFS. For example, you can specify a storage path for the Hive data warehouse. | Ena ble | No defa ult valu e |
|---|---|---|---|
| fileName | The name prefix of the files that you want to write to OSS-HDFS. A random suffix is appended to the specified prefix to form the actual file name that is used by each thread. | Ena ble | No defa ult valu e |
| column | The names of the columns to which you want to write data. You cannot write data only to some columns in the Hive table. To associate the columns in a file with those in a Hive table, configure the name and type parameters for each column. The name parameter specifies the name of the column, and the type parameter specifies the data type of the column. You can configure the column parameter in the following format: { "column": [ { "name": "userName", "type": "string" }, { "name": "age", "type": "long" } ] } | Req uire d if the fileF orm at para met er is set to text or orc | Non e |
| writeMode | The write mode. Valid values: append: OSS-HDFS Writer writes the files based on the specified file name prefix and ensures that the actual file names do not conflict with the names of existing files. nonConflict: OSS-HDFS Writer returns an error if a file with the specified file name prefix exists in the destination directory. truncate : OSS-HDFS Writer deletes all existing files whose names start with the specified file name prefix from the destination directory before files are written to the directory. For example, if you set fileName to abc, all existing files whose names start with abc are deleted from the destination directory. | Ena ble | No defa ult valu e |

| fieldDelimit er | The column delimiter that is used in the files you want to write to OSS-HDFS. Note Only single-character delimiters are supported. If you specify multi-character delimiters, an error is reported. | Req uire d if the fileF orm at para met er is set to text or orc | Non e |

| encoding | The encoding format of the files that you want to write to OSS-HDFS. | No | utf-8 |

| parquetSch ema | The schema of the Parquet files that you want to write to OSS-HDFS. This parameter is available only if the fileFormat parameter is set to parquet. Format: message MessageName { required, dataType, columnName; .....................; } Parameters: MessageName: the name of the MessageName object. required: indicates that the column cannot be left empty. You can also specify optional based on your business requirements. We recommend that you specify optional for all columns. dataType: Parquet files support various data types, such as BOOLEAN, INT32, INT64, INT96, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BINARY, and FIXED LEN BYTE ARRAY. Set this parameter to BINARY if the _ _ _ column stores strings. Note Each line, including the last line, must end with a semicolon (;). Sample code: message m { optional int64 id; optional int64 date id; _ optional binary datetimestring; optional int32 dspId; optional int32 advertiserId; optional int32 status; optional int64 bidding req num; _ _ optional int64 imp; optional int64 click num; _ } | No | No defa ult valu e. |

###### Configure Tablestore Writer

Tablestore Writer allows you to read data from a Tablestore data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

Tablestore Writer allows you to write data from Tablestore. Tablestore Writer allows you to read data from and write data to wide tables and time series tables in **row mode** and
**column mode**.
**Column Mode**: In the multi-version model of Tablestore, the data in a table is organized
into three levels: **Rows > Columns > Version**. A row can contain any column, and the column name is not fixed. Each column can contain multiple versions. Each version has a specific timestamp (version number). The column mode exports data in the four-tuple format of (primary key value, column name, timestamp, column value). The data imported in the column mode is also in the four-tuple format of (primary key value, column name, timestamp, column value).
**Row Mode**: This mode extracts the updated records into rows, which are in the format of
primary key values and column values. In row mode, each row of data corresponds to a piece of data in a Tablestore table. Data in the write row mode includes primary key column values and common column values. Tablestore columns consist of primary key column **primaryKey** and common column
**column**. The source column sequence must be the same as that of primary key columns
and common columns target Tablestore. Otherwise, a column mapping error occurs.

**Supported field types**

| Type Classification | Tablestore data type |
|---|---|
| Integer Class | INTEGER |
| Floating-point class | DOUBLE |
| String | STRING |
| Boolean value | BOOLEAN |
| Binary | BINARY |

Tablestore Writer supports all Tablestore data types. The following table lists the Tablestore data types.

**Note**

Tablestore does not support the DATE data type. The application layer uses the LONG-type UNIX timestamp to indicate time. To write data of the INTEGER type, set the data type to INT in the code editor. During data synchronization, Tablestore Writer converts the data from the INT data type to the INTEGER data type. If you set the data type to INTEGER, an error is reported in the log, and the synchronization task fails.

| Parameters | Describe | Requi red | Default value |
|---|---|---|---|
| datasource | The name of the data source. It must be the same as the name of the added data source. You can add data sources by using the code editor. | Enable | No default value |
| endPoint | The endpoint of the Tablestore server. | Enable | No default value |
| accessId | The AccessKey ID of the account that you use to connect to the Tablestore server. | Enable | No default value |
| accessKey | The AccessKey secret of the account that you use to connect to the Tablestore server. | Enable | No default value |
| instanceName | The name of the Tablestore instance. The instance is an entity for you to use and manage Tablestore. After you activate Tablestore, you must create an instance in the Tablestore console before you can create and manage tables. Tablestore instances are the basic units that you can use to manage your Tablestore resources. Access control and resource measurement for applications are performed at the instance level. | Enable | No default value |
| table | The name of the table to which you want to write data. You can specify only one table name. Multi- table synchronization is not required for Tablestore. | Enable | No default value |

| newVersion | Specifies whether to use the latest version of Tablestore Writer. false: Uses an earlier version of Tablestore Writer. In this case, if you want to write data to wide tables, you must set the mode parameter to normal. true: Uses the latest version of Tablestore Writer. In this case, you can write data to time series tables and wide tables in row or column mode, and the auto-increment primary key column feature is supported. The latest version of Tablestore Writer provides new features and consumes less system resources. Therefore, we recommend that you use the latest version of Tablestore Writer. The settings of the latest version of Tablestore Writer are compatible with the settings of an earlier version of Tablestore Writer. If you add the newVersion=true setting to a task in which an earlier version of Tablestore Writer is used, the task can be run as expected. | Enable | false |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode | The mode in which you want to write data. Valid values: normal: You write data in row mode. multiVersion: You write data in column mode. This setting takes effect only for Tablestore Writer for which the newVersion parameter is set to true. An earlier version of Tablestore Writer ignores the setting of the mode parameter, and you can write data only in row mode. | No | normal |
| isTimeseriesTable | Specifies whether to write data to a time series table. false: The table is a wide table. true: The table is a time series table. This configuration takes effect only in the newVersion:true & mode:normal configuration (column mode is not compatible with time series tables). | No | false |

**Additional configurations of Writer script parameters**

Tablestore Writer allows you to write data to a wide table in row mode, a time series table in row mode, and a wide table in column mode. Additional configurations for each mode are described below.

| Parameters | Description | Requi red | Default value |
|---|---|---|---|
| primaryKey | The primary keys of the destination table in Tablestore. Specify the primary keys in a JSON array. Tablestore is a NoSQL database service. You must specify column names for Tablestore Writer to write data. Data Integration supports data type conversion. Tablestore Writer can convert data from a data type other than STRING or INT to the STRING or INT data type. Sample configuration: "primaryKey" : [ {"name":"gid", "type":"INT"}, {"name":"uid", "type":"STRING"} ], Note The PrimaryKey of Tablestore supports only the STRING and INT types. Therefore, Tablestore Writer is limited to the STRING and INT types. | Yes | None |
| column | The names of the columns to be synchronized in the configured table. A JSON array is used to describe the field information. Configuration example: "column" : [ {"name":"col1", "type":"INT"}, {"name":"col2", "type":"DOUBLE"}, {"name":"col3", "type":"STRING"}, {"name":"col4", "type":"BINARY"}, {"name":"col5", "type":"BOOL"} ], Name indicates the name of the Tablestore column to which data is written, and type indicates the type of data that is written. Tablestore supports the STRING, INT, DOUBLE, BOOL, and BINARY types. Note The write process does not support constants, functions, or custom expressions. | Yes | None |

| writeMode | The mode in which data is written to the Tablestore. Valid values: PutRow: the PutRow operation of Tablestore, which is used to insert data into a specified row. If a specified row does not exist, a new row is added. If a specified row exists, the row is overwritten. UpdateRow: the UpdateRow operation of Tablestore, which is used to update the data in a specified row. If the specified row does not exist, a new row is added. If a specified row exists, the values of the specified columns in the row are added, modified, or removed based on the content in the request. | Enable | No default value |
|---|---|---|---|
| enableAutoIncreme nt | Specifies whether you can write data to a Tablestore table that contains auto-increment primary key columns. true: Tablestore Writer scans for information about auto-increment primary key columns in the destination table and adds the auto-increment primary key columns during the data write process. Users do not need to specify the names of the auto-increment primary key columns. false: The error is returned if you write data to a Tablestore table that contains auto-increment primary key columns. | No | false |
| requestTotalSizeLim itation | The maximum size of data that can be written to a single row in Tablestore. The parameter value must be of a numeric data type. | No | 1MB |
| attributeColumnSize Limitation | The maximum size of data that can be written to a single attribute column in Tablestore. The parameter value must be of a numeric data type. | No | 2MB |
| primaryKeyColumnS izeLimitation | The maximum size of data that can be written to a single primary key column in Tablestore. The parameter value must be of a numeric data type. | No | 1KB |
| attributeColumnMax Count | The maximum number of attribute columns to which data can be written in Tablestore. The parameter value must be of a numeric data type. | No | 1,024 |

###### Configure DB2 Writer

The DB2 Writer plug-in enables you to read data from a DB2 data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

Db2 Writer obtains the protocol data generated by the reader through the data synchronization framework, and writes the data to Db2 by using the `insert into` statement. If the primary key or unique index conflict occurs, the conflicting rows cannot be written to Db2. In addition, a `PreparedStatement + Batch` is used for performance considerations, and a `rewriteBatchedStatements=true` is set to buffer data into the thread context buffer, and a write request is initiated only when the buffer accumulates to a predetermined threshold.

**Note**

The entire task must have at least `insert into` permissions. Whether other permissions are required depends on the statements that you specify in the **preSql** and **postSql** when you configure the task. The DB2 AES encryption algorithm is not currently supported.

**Supported field types**

When performing offline reads and writes, DB2 Writer supports most DB2 data types, but some data types are not supported. Check your data types. The following table lists the DB2 data types that are converted by DB2 Writer.

| Integer Class | SMALLINT |
|---|---|
| Floating-point class | DECIMAL, REAL, and DOUBLE |
| String class | CHAR, CHARACTER, VARCHAR, GRAPHIC, VARGRAPHIC, LONG VARCHAR, CLOB, LONG VARGRAPHIC, and DBCLOB |
| Date and time | DATE, TIME, and TIMESTAMP |
| Boolean | No default value. |
| Binary | BLOB |

| writeMode | The import mode. You can select insert into, on duplicate key update, or replace into. insert into: When a primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, the conflicting rows cannot be written to, which is reflected in the form of dirty data. If you configure the task in script mode, set the writeMode to insert. on duplicate key update: If no primary key or unique index conflict is encountered, the behavior is the same as that of the insert into . If a conflict occurs, the value of the specified field is replaced with a new row and data is written to MySQL. If you configure the task in script mode, set the writeMode to update. replace into: If no primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, the data is processed in the same way as that when you set this parameter to insert . If a conflict occurs, the original rows are deleted, and new rows are inserted. This indicates that all fields of the original rows are replaced. If you configure a synchronization task by using the code editor, set writeMode to replace. | No | insert |

When you configure this parameter, you must also configure skipNullColumn parameters. Important If you set this parameter to skipNull, the task dynamically concatenates SQL statements for writing data to support the default values on the destination. ###### Configure PostgreSQL Writer

PostgreSQL Writer allows you to read data from PostgreSQL data sources. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

You cannot directly write data to a Postgres data source based on a unique index. We recommend that you write data to a temporary table and then perform the `RENAME` operation to complete the update.

**Supported field types**

Most PostgreSQL data types are supported. If you write data to an **offline database** instance, some data types are not supported. Check your data types. The following table lists the data type conversions for PostgreSQL.

Valid values: insert into, on duplicate key update, and replace into. insert into: If a primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, data cannot be written to the conflicting rows, and the data that is not written to these rows is regarded as dirty data. If you configure a synchronization task by using the code editor, set writeMode to insert into. on duplicate key update: If no primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, the data is processed in the same way as that when you set this parameter to insert into. If a conflict occurs, specified fields in the original rows are replaced with new rows, and data is written to MariaDB. If you configure a synchronization task by using the code editor, set writeMode to on duplicate key update. replace into: If no primary key conflict or unique index conflict occurs, the data is processed in the same way as that when you set this parameter to insert into. If a conflict occurs, the original rows are deleted, and new rows are inserted. This indicates that all fields of the original rows are replaced. If you configure a synchronization task by using the code editor, set writeMode to replace into. | No | insert into |

You can also configure other properties, such as those related to the cache and batch for scan operations to optimize interaction with servers. Note You must use an internal endpoint to access an ApsaraDB for HBase database. | Enable | No default value |
| mode | The write mode. Only the normal mode is supported. The dynamic column mode will be available in the future. | Enable | No default value |
| table | The name of the HBase table to which you want to write data. The name is case-sensitive. | Enable | No default value |

| encoding | The encoding format that is used to convert a string into data in the HBase byte[] format. Valid values: utf-8 and gbk. | No | utf-8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| column | The names of the columns to which you want to write data. index: the ID of a column in the source table, starting from 0. name: the name of a column in the destination HBase table. Specify this parameter in the Column family:Column name format. type: the data type of data that you want to write to the destination HBase table. This parameter is used for converting data into the HBase byte[] format. | Enable | No default value |
| rowkeyCol umn | The rowkey column of each row in the destination HBase table. index: the ID of a column in the source table, starting from 0. If the value is a constant, the value of the index is -1. type: specifies the data type to be written, which is used to convert HBase byte[]. value: a constant that is used as a concatenator for multiple fields. HBase Writer concatenates all columns in the rowkeyColumn as the rowkey that is used to write data to HBase. The rowkey cannot be all constants. The following figure shows the configuration format. "rowkeyColumn": [ { "index":0, "type":"string" }, { "index":-1, "type":"string", "value":" " _ } ] | Enable | No default value |

| versionCol umn | The version of each HBase cell. You can specify the current time, the specified time column, or the specified time. If you do not specify this value, the current time is used. index: specifies the index that corresponds to the column of the reader, starting from 0. Make sure that the index can be converted to LONG. type: If it is a Date type, it will try to parse it withy yyy-MM- dd HH:mm:ss and yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss SSS. If the time is specified, the index is -1. value: the value of the specified time. The value is of the LONG type. The configuration format is as follows. "versionColumn":{ "index":1 } "versionColumn":{ "index":-1, "value":123456789 } | No | No default value. |
|---|---|---|---|
| nullMode | The method used to process null values. Valid values: skip: HBase Writer does not write data of columns for which null values are returned to HBase. empty: HBase Writer writes HConstants.EMPTY BYTE ARRAY (new byte [0]) to HBase _ _ instead of null values. | No | skip |
| walFlag | Specifies whether to enable WAL for HBase. If you set this parameter to true, WAL is enabled. All edits, such as PUT and DELETE operations, that are requested by an HBase client for all regions carried by the RegionServer are first recorded in the WAL log file (HLog). After the edits are recorded in the WAL log file, they are implemented to the MemStore, and a success notification is sent to the HBase client. If the edits fail to be recorded in the WAL log file, a failure notification is sent to the HBase client, and the edits are not implemented to the MemStore. If you set this parameter to false, WAL is disabled. This way, HBase Writer can write data more efficiently. | No | false |
| writeBuffe rSize | The write buffer size, in bytes, of the HBase client. If you specify this parameter, you must also specify the autoflush parameter. By default, the value of the autoflush parameter is false. autoflush: If the value is true, the HBase client sends a PUT request each time it receives an edit. If the value is false, the HBase client sends a PUT request only when its write buffer is full. | No | 8M |

###### Configure HBase11xsql Writer

HBase11xsql Writer allows you to read data from an HBase data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

Data import with timestamps is not supported. Only tables created by using Phoenix are supported. Native HBase tables are not supported. The definition order of the columns in the Writer must match the column order of the Reader. The column order in the Reader defines the order in which the columns are organized in each row of the output. The column order of the writer defines the order of the columns that the writer expects in the received data. Example: The column sequence of the reader is c1,c2,c3, and c4. The column order of Writer is x1,x2,x3, x4. Then, the output column c1 of Reader is assigned to the column x1 of Writer. If the column sequence of the writer is x1,x2,x4,x3, c3 is assigned to x4 and c4 is assigned to x3. Supports importing data from indexed tables. All index table can be updated simultaneously.

Hive Writer writes data from Hive to HDFS. This topic describes how Hive Writer works, parameters, and examples.

**Limits**

When you use Data Integration to synchronize data to a Hive cluster, temporary files are generated on the server and are automatically deleted when the synchronization task is complete. You need to pay attention to the limit on the number of files in the HDFS directory on the server to avoid unavailability of the HDFS file system if the number of unexpected files reaches the upper limit. DataWorks cannot ensure that the number of files in the HDFS directory is within the allowed range.

**Note**

The server can modify the **dfs.namenode.fs-limits.max-directory-items** parameter to define the maximum number of directories or files in a single directory excluding recursion. The default value is 1048576 and the value range is 1 to 6400000. You can increase the parameter **dfs.namenode.fs-limits.max-directory-items** of HDFS or clean up unnecessary files to avoid this problem.

**Supported field types**

Hive data sources support the following types of offline fields:

                    "name",
                    "age"

This parameter specifies the mode in which Hive Writer loads data from the HDFS file to the Hive table. Valid values: truncate: Hive Writer deletes existing data before it loads data to the Hive table. append: Hive Writer retains the existing data and appends data to the Hive table. Note Before you configure this parameter, make sure that the value that will be specified for the parameter does not affect your business. The client that is specified by the hiveCommand parameter provides access information about Hive. jdbcUrl, username, and password: the information that is required to connect to Hive by using JDBC. ###### Configure Kafka Writer

Kafka Writer reads data from Kafka data sources. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Supported field types**

Kafka stores data in unstructured storage. Generally, the data modules recorded in Kafka include key, value, offset, timestamp, headers, and partition. When you write data to Kafka, DataWorks processes the data based on the following policy: When DataWorks writes data to Kafka, you can write data in the JSON or text format. Different data synchronization solutions have different data processing policies for writing data to Kafka data sources.

**Important**

When you write data in the text format, field names are not written. Instead, delimiters are used to separate field values. When data is synchronously written to Kafka in real time, the written data is in the built-in JSON format. The written data includes all the data that contains the data of database change messages, business time, and DDL information.

| writeMode | If valueIndex is not configured, this configuration items determines that all columns of the source read record are concatenated as the format of the value written to Kafka. Valid values: text and JSON. Default value: text. Set this parameter to text and concatenate all columns based on the delimiter specified by fieldDelimiter. Set this parameter to JSON and concatenate all columns into a JSON string based on the field names specified by the column parameter. For example, if a source record has three columns and the values a, b, and c are set to text for writeMode and# for fieldDelimiter, the value of the record written to Kafka is the string a#b#c. If writeMode is set to JSON and column is set to [{"name":"col1"},{"name":"col2"},{"name":"col3"}] the value of the record written to Kafka is the string {"col1":"a","col2":"b","col3":"c"}. If valueIndex is configured, this configuration items is invalid. | No |

| keyIndexes | source the sequence number array of the column in the read record as the key to write the Kafka record. The column sequence numbers start from 0, for example, [0,1,2]. The values of all configured column sequence numbers are connected by commas (,) as the keys to be written to Kafka records. If you do not specify this parameter, the Kafka record key is null, and data is written to each partition of the topic in turn. You can specify one or more characters as delimiters, configure Unicode characters in the \u0001 format, and support escape characters such as \t and \n. The default value is \t. If writeMode is not set to text or valueIndex is set, this configuration items is invalid. | No |

| acks | The ack configuration when the Kafka producer is initialized determines the confirmation method for successful writing. The default acks parameter is all. acks values are as follows: 0: does not confirm successful writing. 1: confirms that the primary replica is written successfully. all: confirms that all replicas are written successfully. | No |

| datasource | The name of the data source. It must be the same as the name of the added data source. You can add data sources by using the code editor. | Enable | No default value |
| timeout | The timeout period of the connection to an FTP server. Unit: milliseconds. | No | 60,000 |
| path | The directory on the FTP server to which you want to write files. FTP Writer uses parallel threads to write multiple files to the directory based on the parallelism setting. | Enable | No default value |
| fileName | The name prefix of the files that you want to write to the FTP server. A random suffix is appended to file names to form the actual file names that is used by each thread. | Enable | No default value |
| singleFile Output | Specifies whether to add a random suffix to the names of the files that you want to write to the FTP server. The names of the files that FTP Writer writes to the FTP server are related to the value of the fileName parameter. If you do not need the random suffix, set the singleFileOutput parameter to true. In this case, FTP Writer writes the files to the FTP server by using the name prefix of the files. | No | false |
| writeMode | The mode in which FTP Writer writes files. Valid values: truncate: If the singleFileOutput parameter is set to true, FTP Writer deletes files with the same names in the destination directory before it writes files to the directory. If the singleFileOutput parameter is set to false, FTP Writer deletes all existing files whose names contain the prefix specified by fileName in the destination directory before it writes files to the directory. append: FTP Writer directly writes files based on the file name prefix specified by fileName and ensures that the actual file names do not conflict with the names of existing files. nonConflict: FTP Writer returns an error if the destination directory contains a file whose name contains the prefix specified by fileName. | Enable | No default value |
| fieldDelimi ter | The column delimiter that is used in the files that you want to write to the FTP server. The delimiter must be a single character. | Yes | None |
| skipHeade r | Specifies whether to skip the headers in a CSV-like object if the object has headers. By default, the headers are not skipped. The skipHeader parameter is unavailable for compressed objects. | No | false |

|---|---|---|---|
| encoding | The encoding format of the object from which you want to read data. | No | utf-8 |
| nullFormat | The string that represents a null pointer. No standard strings can represent a null pointer in text files. You can use this parameter to define which string represents a null pointer. For example, if you set nullFormat to null, Data Integration considers null as a null pointer (4 characters). | No | No default value. |
| dateForma t | The format in which the data of the DATE type is serialized in a file, such as "dateFormat":"yyyy-MM-dd". | No | No default value. |
| fileFormat | The format in which files are written to the FTP server. Valid values: CSV and TEXT. If a file is written as a CSV file, the file must follow CSV specifications. If the data in the file contains column delimiters, the column delimiters are escaped by double quotation marks ("). If a file is written as a TXT file, the data in the file is separated by column delimiters. In this case, the column delimiters are not escaped. | No | TEXT |
| header | The table headers if files are written as TXT or CSV files, such as ["id","name","age"]. This indicates that the id, name, and age fields are written to a CSV file as the first row. | No | No default value. |

Set this parameter to the absolute path of the file. For batch synchronization tasks that are periodically scheduled, we recommend that you add a scheduling parameter to the name of the file. For example, you can set the name of a file to /user/ftp/markDone ${bizdate}.txt, in _ which ${bizdate} indicates a scheduling parameter. | No | No default value. |

###### Configure HDFS Writer

HDFS Writer allows you to read data from an HDFS data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

When you use HDFS Writer, take note of the following items: Currently, HDFS Writer supports only TextFile, ORCFile, and ParquetFile files, and the file content must be a logical two‑dimensional table. Because HDFS is a file system and does not have the concept of schema, it does not support writing to some columns.

| Category | Hive data type |
|---|---|
| Integer | TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT, and BIGINT |
| Floating point | FLOAT and DOUBLE |
| String | CHAR, VARCHAR, and STRING |
| Boolean value | BOOLEAN |
| Date and time | DATE and TIMESTAMP |

Hive data types such as DECIMAL, BINARY, ARRAYS, MAPS, STRUCTS, and UNION are not supported. For Hive partition table, only a single partition can be written at a time. To write a text file to HDFS, make sure that the delimiter in the file is the same as that in the Hive table that you want to associate with the file. This way, you can associate the columns in the file that is written to HDFS with those in the Hive table. You can use HDFS Writer in the environment in which Hive 1.1.1 and Hadoop 2.7.1 (JDK version: 1.7) are installed. JDK is short for Java Development Kit. HDFS Writer can write files to HDFS in test environments in which Hive 1.2.0 and Hadoop 2.5.0 or Hadoop 2.6.0 are installed.

**Supported data types**

HDFS Writer can write text, ORC, or Parquet files to a specified directory in HDFS. You can associate the columns in the files with the columns in Hive tables. HDFS Writer supports most Hive data types. Make sure that the data types of your system are supported. The following table lists the data type mappings based on which HDFS Writer converts data types.

**Note**

The data types of the specified columns in the file must be the same as those of the columns in the Hive table.

###### Configure RestAPI Writer

The RestAPI Writer plug-in is used to read data from a RestAPI data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

Currently, you cannot set the timeout parameter. The built-in request timeout period of DataWorks is 60s. If your API query takes more than 60 seconds to return, the task fails.

**Supported field types**

**Important**

When data is synchronized to a target, only a single-layer table structure is supported. Nested field structures are not supported. For example, the API returns the structure {data: {user: { id: 1, name:'lily'},value: 123 }}, which is synchronized to the target. The fields can only be processed as user_id, user_name, and value in parallel.

| actionType | Indicates the action type of the Elasticsearch when data is written out. Currently, the index and update actionType are Data Integration supported. Default value: index: index: The underlying layer uses the Index.Builder of the Elasticsearch SDK to construct a batch request. When inserting Elasticsearch index, you need to first determine whether the ID is specified in the inserted document data: If no ID is specified, the Elasticsearch generates a unique ID by default. In this case, the document is added directly to the Elasticsearch. If an ID is specified, the update is made (the entire document is replaced) and modification is not supported for a specific Field. Note The update here is not an update in the Elasticsearch (replacing partially specified columns). The update: updates the document according to the ID specified by the user. If the ID value does not exist in the index, the document is inserted. If it exists, the content of the specified column field is updated (the content of other document fields remains unchanged). Each time the update is completed, the entire document information is obtained, thus enabling modification for specific fields. The update does not support conditional filtering. The update operation is performed only based on the specified ID value. Because the original document needs to be fetched once for each update, the performance impact can be significant. ###### Configure MongoDB Writer

MongoDB Writer allows you to read data from MongoDB data sources. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

If the concurrency is greater than 1, the data types of all `_id` fields in the data synchronization task must be the same. For example, `_id` fields are of the string or ObjectId type. Otherwise, some data cannot be synchronized.

**Note**

If the concurrency is greater than 1, task splitting uses `_id` fields to split tasks. Therefore, in this scenario, `_id` fields do not support mixed types. If the `_id` has multiple field types, you can synchronize data in a single-concurrency mode and do not configure **splitFactor** or set **splitFactor** to 1.

|  | splitVector |
|---|---|
| no such cmd splitVector |  |

| Type Classification | MongoDB data type |
|---|---|
| Integer Class | INT and LONG |
| Floating-point class | DOUBLE |
| String | STRING and ARRAY |
| Date and time | DATE |
| Boolean | BOOL |
| Binary | BYTES |

Data Integration itself does not support the array type, but MongoDB supports the array type, and the array type has a powerful index function. You can use the special configuration of the parameter to convert a string to an array in MongoDB. After the data type is converted, data can be written to MongoDB in parallel. By default, the `splitVector` command is preferentially used for task sharding run time avoid using `splitVector` .

"useSplitVector" : false
```

| writeMode | The write mode. The following parameters are included: isReplace: If you set isReplace to true, MongoDB Writer overwrites the data that contains the same primary key in the destination table. If you set isReplace to false, MongoDB Writer does not overwrite the data. replaceKey: the primary key for each data record. Data is overwritten based on the primary key. The primary key must be unique. Note If you set isReplace to true and set a field other than the id field as the primary key, an error that is similar to _ the following error may occur when the synchronization task is run: After applying the update, the (immutable) field ' id' was found to have been altered to _ id: "2" _ The reason is that the value of the id field does not _ match the value of the replaceKey parameter for some of the data that is written to the destination table. For more information, see What do I do if the following error message is returned when I run a batch synchronization task to synchronize data to MongoDB: After applying the update, the (immutable) field ' id' was found to have been _ altered to id: "2" in the "Batch synchronization" topic. _ | No | No default value. |
|---|---|---|---|
| preSql | The SQL statement that you want to execute before the synchronization task is run. For example, you can set this parameter to the SQL statement that is used to delete outdated data. If the preSql parameter is left empty, no SQL statement is executed before the synchronization task is run. Make sure that the value of the preSql parameter is specified based on the JSON syntax. | No | No default value. |

Before the synchronization task is run, Data Integration executes the SQL statement specified by the **preSql** parameter. Then, Data Integration starts to write data. The **preSql** parameter does not affect the data that is written. You can configure the **preSql** parameter to ensure the idempotence of the write operation. For example, you can configure the **preSql** parameter to delete outdated data before a synchronization task is run based on your business requirements. If the synchronization task fails, you need to only rerun the synchronization task. Requirements on the format of the **preSql** parameter: Configure the type parameter to specify the action type. Valid values: drop and remove. Example: `"preSql":{"type":"remove"}` . drop: deletes the collection specified by the collectionName parameter and the data in the collection. remove: deletes data based on specified conditions. json: the conditions used to delete data. Example: `"preSql":{"type":"remove", "json":"`

```json
{'operationTime':{'$gte':ISODate('${last_day}T00:00:00.424+0800')}}"}} .
```

${last_day} is a scheduling parameter of DataWorks. You can configure this parameter in the format of $[yyyy-mm-dd] . You can use other conditional operation symbols (such as $gt, $lt, $gte, and $lte), logical operators (such as and and or), or functions (such as max, min, sum, avg, and ISODate) supported by MongoDB. Data Integration use the following MongoDB standard API to execute your data and delete the query.

```
query=(BasicDBObject) com.mongodb.util.JSON.parse(json); col.deleteMany(query);
```

**Note**

If you want to delete data with conditions, we recommend that you use the JSON configuration. item: You can configure the column name (name), condition (condition), and column value (value) for data filtering in item. `"preSql":{"type":"remove","item":`

```
[{"name":"pv","value":"100","condition":"$gt"},{"name":"pid","value":"10"}]} , for
```

example. The Data Integration constructs query conditions based on the items that you have configured and deletes the items by calling the MongoDB API operation. col.deleteMany(query); , for example. No **preSql** is recognized and no pre-deletion is required.

###### Configure Redis Writer

Redis Writer allows you to read data from a Redis data source. This topic describes the parameters in the plug-in.

**Limits**

When you use Redis Writer to write data to an ApsaraDB for Redis instance, if the value type is List, the synchronization result of the reruning synchronization task is not idempotent. Therefore, if the value type is List , you must manually clear the corresponding data on the Redis database when you re-run the synchronization task.

**Important**

Redis does not support Bloom filters (Bloom filters). If you need to process duplicate data, you can use an alternative solution: add a node (such as Shell, Python, and PyOPDS) before or after the sync node by using a workflow for processing.

**Supported field types**

Redis supports values of the following data types: STRING, LIST, SET, ZSET (sorted set), and HASH. For more information about Redis, visit redis.io. In the following code, a batch synchronization task is configured to synchronize data from a MySQL database to Redis. The synchronization task of data written to Redis.

###### Configure ShenTong Writer

The ShenTong Writer plugin reads data from a ShenTong database. This topic describes the parameters for this plugin.

**Implementation**

The ShenTong Writer plugin writes data to a destination table in a ShenTong primary database. Under the hood, ShenTong Writer connects to a remote ShenTong database using Java Database Connectivity (JDBC). It then executes `insert into ...` SQL statements to write data to the database. The data is committed in batches. ShenTong Writer is designed for extract, transform, and load (ETL) developers who import data from data warehouses into ShenTong. It can also serve as a data migration tool for database administrators (DBAs) and other users. ShenTong Writer receives protocol data from a Reader through the DataX framework. It then generates the corresponding SQL statements based on your configuration.

**Limits**

`insert into...` : If a primary key or unique index conflict occurs, the conflicting rows are not written. The database that contains the destination table must be a primary database to allow data to be written. The job requires at least `insert into...` permission. Whether other permissions are needed depends on the statements you specify in `preSql` and `postSql`. ShenTong Writer does not support the `writeMode` parameter.

**Supported field types**

ShenTong Writer supports most ShenTong data types. However, some types are not supported. Check your data types carefully. The following table lists the data type conversions supported by ShenTong Writer:

#### FAQ

Q: If the ShenTongWriter job fails while executing a `postSql` statement, is the data imported into the destination database? A: The DataX import process consists of three stages: the pre-operation, the import operation, and the post-operation. If an error occurs in any of these stages, the DataX job fails. Because DataX does not guarantee that these operations are completed within a single transaction, it is possible that some data has already been written to the destination. Q: Based on the previous answer, some dirty data might be imported into the database. What should I do if this affects the production database? A: There are two solutions. First, you can configure a `preSql` statement to clean up the data imported on the same day. Each time DataX runs an import, it can clean up the previous run and then import the complete dataset. Second, you can import the data into a temporary table and then rename the temporary table to the production table after the import is complete. Q: How can I implement the second method to prevent affecting production data? A: You can configure the job to import data into a temporary table.
