### DataWorks Copilot AI in Place

AI in Place is a collection of intelligent features embedded in various DataWorks interfaces. From intelligent code completion in the code editor to code generation during data development, it provides precise, context-aware, and real-time assistance, and makes intelligence an inherent attribute of your development tools.

**Note**

For more information about the comprehensive Data+AI capabilities of DataWorks, see DataWorks Copilot. DataWorks supports the following intelligent features.

**Feature details**

**Code completion**

**Feature introduction**: DataWorks Copilot intelligently completes the SQL statements that
you are writing based on the context information.
**Instructions**: You can press the `TAB` key to accept the completion results, or press the
`ESC` key to abandon the completion results. You can click **DataWorks Copilot** in the lower-right corner of the toolbar at the bottom of the page to enable or disable code completion.

**SQL generation**

**Feature introduction**: DataWorks Copilot automatically converts natural language inputs
into SQL statements in the code editor.
**Instructions**: In the code editor, right-click a blank area and choose **Copilot > SQL**
**Generate** to go to the DataWorks Copilot configuration page. On the DataWorks Copilot
configuration page, enter a command, click Send, and then wait for DataWorks Copilot to return the analysis result. You can then determine whether to accept the result based on your business requirements.

**SQL error correction**

**Feature introduction**: DataWorks Copilot supports detecting and fixing errors in specified
code snippets. It also allows you to trigger Copilot Chat with one click at syntax error locations in the code editor and automatically locate the erroneous code.
**Instructions**: In the code editor, select a code snippet and right-click the code snippet to
choose **Copilot > SQL Rectify**. Then, wait for DataWorks Copilot to return the analysis result and determine whether to accept the result based on your business requirements.

**Comment generation**

**Feature introduction**: DataWorks Copilot generates comments for specified SQL
statements to improve the readability of the SQL statements.
**Instructions**: In the code editor, select a code snippet, right-click the code snippet to choose
**Copilot > SQL Comments**, click **Send**, and then wait for DataWorks Copilot to return the
analysis result. Then, determine whether to accept the result based on your business requirements.

**SQL rewriting**

**Feature introduction**: DataWorks Copilot rewrites the specified code through natural
language interaction.
**Instructions**: In the code editor, select a code snippet, right-click the code snippet to choose
**Copilot > SQL Update**, enter your update requirements, click **Send**, and then wait for
DataWorks Copilot to return the analysis result. Then, determine whether to accept the result based on your business requirements.

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| Overview | This module displays the status of nodes in charts and tables. For more information, see View the statistics on the Overview page. |
| RealTime Task Maintenance | This module displays all the real-time data synchronization nodes that are committed to and run by the scheduling system. For more information, see O&M for real-time synchronization nodes. |
| Cycle Task Maintenance | This module displays all the auto triggered nodes that are committed to and run by the scheduling system, the recurring instances that are generated for the nodes, data backfill instances, and test instances. For more information, see Manage auto triggered nodes. |
| Trigger Task Maintenance | This module displays all the manually triggered nodes that are committed to the scheduling system and the manually triggered node instances that are generated for the nodes. For more information, see Manage manually triggered nodes. |
| Alarm | This module displays the status of the nodes that are monitored. You will receive alerts if the monitored nodes are abnormal. For more information, see Overview. |
| Engine Maintenance | This module allows you to view the jobs, quota groups, and projects of MaxCompute. For more information, see MaxCompute engine O&M. |
| Tenant Schedule Setting | This module provides the scheduling calendar feature, which allows you to define scheduling dates and scheduling methods in a more flexible manner. For more information, see Configure a scheduling calendar. |

## Operation Center

### Overview

Operation Center consists of the following modules: Overview, RealTime Task Maintenance, Cycle Task Maintenance, Alarm, Engine Maintenance, and Tenant Schedule Setting. You can view your nodes and instances, test nodes, and backfill data for nodes in Operation Center. If the workspace that you use is in standard mode, you can switch between the production and development environments by changing the URL of the Operation Center page. If the URL contains **env=dev**, Operation Center in the development environment is used. If the URL contains **env=prod**, Operation Center in the production environment is used. You can change the value of the env parameter to go to Operation Center of the corresponding environment. In the Cycle Task Maintenance and Trigger Task Maintenance modules, you can view the instances of all your nodes and perform related operations on the instances. For example, you can stop and rerun instances.

**Note**

Instances are generated after nodes are run by the scheduling system. An instance is a snapshot of a node at a specific point in time. The instance contains information such as the time when the node is run, the status and operational logs of the node.

### View statistics on the

**Overview page**

The Overview page displays the overall O&M information, including the metrics that require your special attention, overall running information about nodes, and trends on scheduling resource changes. This page also displays information about Data Integration, including the distribution of batch synchronization nodes and real-time synchronization nodes in different states and the data synchronization progress of batch synchronization nodes and real-time synchronization nodes. This information helps you improve O&M efficiency.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products**
**> Data Development and O&M > Operation Center**. The **Workbench Overview** tab
of the **Overview** page appears. The Workbench Overview tab displays the statistics only on auto triggered nodes and auto triggered node instances. You can view the following information on the **Workbench**
**Overview** tab:

**O&M Stability Assessment**

This section displays the health statistics. The health status for O&M stability can be perfect, good, medium, or poor. If high-risk or low-risk items are displayed, the health status of the workspace is poor. You must handle the at-risk items and optimize the performance of the workspace at the earliest opportunity.

**Focus On**

This section displays the O&M exceptions from the workspace and individual perspectives based on exception statistics of intelligent baselines and auto triggered nodes. You can view the overall information in your workspace or view only the information about nodes of which you are the owner to identify and handle exceptions at the earliest opportunity and ensure that your business is not affected.
**Baseline in Overtime**: the number of baseline instances that are in the overtime state on
the current day. If a node in a baseline is still running when the committed completion time of the baseline arrives, an instance that is generated for the node enters the overtime state.
**Baseline in Alert**: the number of baseline instances that are in the alert state on the
current day. You can specify an alert margin threshold to ensure that important data is generated as expected in scenarios in which dependencies between nodes in the baseline are complex. If the alert margin threshold is exceeded, nodes may fail to finish running as expected and exceptions may occur.
**Error-related Events**: the number of error-related events that are generated on the
current day. An error-related event is generated if a node in a baseline fails. In this case, the running of descendant nodes of the node may be blocked. You must handle the error at the earliest opportunity to prevent the node from affecting the running of its descendant nodes.
**Slowdown Events**: the number of slowdown events that are generated on the current day.
A slowdown event is generated if the running duration of a node in a baseline is significantly longer than the average running duration of the node in the historical periods of time. In this case, the running time of a node is significantly longer than the average running time of the node in the previous periods.
**Isolated Nodes**: the number of isolated nodes on the current day.
If an auto triggered node does not have an ancestor node, the auto triggered node becomes an isolated node. In this case, the node cannot be automatically scheduled to run.
**Frozen Nodes**: the number of auto triggered nodes that are frozen on the current day.
If an auto triggered node is frozen, instances that are generated for the node are also frozen. Frozen instances are not automatically scheduled, and the descendant instances of the frozen instances are blocked from running.
**Expired Nodes**: the number of auto triggered nodes for which the effective period of
scheduling expires. The system generates instances for an auto triggered node and runs the instances within the effective period of scheduling of the node. If the effective period of scheduling expires, the system does not generate or schedule auto triggered instances of the node.
**Modified Nodes**: the number of auto triggered nodes whose configurations are modified
on the current day. The **modifications** include code changes, scheduling configuration modifications, node status changes, and node ownership changes. The **statistics** on the following nodes are collected: nodes whose configurations are modified on the DataStudio page and that are deployed to the production environment after configuration modification and nodes whose configurations are modified in the production environment.

**Note**

If you select **Mine** in the upper-right corner of the Focus On section, only the number of modified nodes of which you are the owner is counted.

**Instances Status**

**Statistical scope**: This section displays the statistics on the distribution of auto triggered
instances by status based on a specific data timestamp. You can view the distribution of auto triggered instances in the current workspace or the distribution of auto triggered instances of which you are the owner. The statistics in this section are updated when you load the page.
**Method to view information**: You can click a sector in the donut chart to view the
number and proportion of auto triggered instances in a specific state.
**Instances that are in specific states and need to be focused on**:
**Failed**: An auto triggered instance in this state fails to run. As a result, the running of its
descendant instances may be blocked.
**Frozen**: A frozen auto triggered instance is not automatically scheduled, and the running
of its descendant instances is blocked.
**Slow-running**: An auto triggered instance is considered a slow-running instance if the
auto triggered instance is running and the running duration of the auto triggered instance is at least `15` minutes longer than the average running duration of the auto triggered instance during the last `10` days. If the number of historical auto triggered instances is less than `four` and the running duration of an auto triggered instance exceeds 30 minutes, the auto triggered instance can also be considered a slow running instance.

**Note**

Only statistics on **normal nodes** are collected. Statistics on dry-run nodes and frozen nodes are not collected. Normal node or instance: A normal node or instance is a node or instance that actually runs code. Normal nodes or instances do not include dry-run nodes or instances and frozen nodes or instances. Dry-run nodes or instances include nodes whose scheduling mode is set to dry-run, instances that are not generated during the period of time in which nodes are scheduled, branch nodes that are not selected, and expired instances that are generated when the scheduled time for running nodes is less than 10 minutes from the point in time when the nodes are committed and deployed.

**Instances Completion Status**

**Statistical scope**: This section displays the completion situations of auto triggered
instances between `00:00 and 23:00` of the current day, including the number of auto triggered instances that are successfully run or are not run on the current day, the number of auto triggered instances that were successfully run or were not run on the previous day, and the historical average number of auto triggered instances that are successfully run or are not run, as well as the fluctuation rate in the numbers. The statistics in this section are updated when you load this page.
**Display pattern**: The statistics are displayed in a line chart. If the deviations among the
three lines are large, an exception occurred during a specific period of time. You must perform a further check and analysis.
**Node type**: You can select a node type based on your business requirements.
**Historical Average**: This metric presents the completion situation of auto triggered
instances that are successfully run in the previous `10` days.

**Trend of Nodes and Instances**

**Statistical scope**: This section displays the changing trends of the numbers of auto
triggered nodes and auto triggered instances in the production environment within a specific period of time. You can specify a period of time within the previous 12 months in the upperright corner of this section.

**Distribution of Auto Triggered Nodes**

**Statistical scope**: This section displays the number and proportion of auto triggered
nodes counted by node type and scheduling cycle. The statistics in this section are updated when you load the page.
**Display pattern**: The statistics are displayed in a donut chart. The types of nodes that can
be displayed in the donut chart are limited. If the types of nodes that need to be displayed exceed the upper limit, the statistics are displayed after merging.

**Ranking of Instances on Previous Day**

This section ranks auto triggered instances based on their running duration, time spent in waiting for resources, and slow running duration on the previous day. Only the `top 30` auto triggered instances are displayed. You can identify a time-consuming node based on the ranking, click the **ID of the instance** that is generated for the node to go to the instance details page, and then perform diagnostics on the instance to view the running situation of the instance.

**Note**

**Slow Running**: The difference between the running duration of an instance on the
previous day and the average running duration of the instance over a historical period is collected. Instances are sorted by the difference in descending order.

**Ranking of Auto Triggered Node Instances with Highest Error**

**Rate in Recent Month**

This section ranks nodes on which errors occurred within the recent month and displays the `top 30` nodes. You can identify a node with a high error rate in the recent month, view the running details of the node, and then identify the cause of the error.

**View statistics on batch synchronization nodes on the Data**

**Integration tab**

On the **Overview**, click the **Data Integration** tab. The Data Integration tab displays the statistics on **batch synchronization nodes** within a specified time range. You can specify a time range in the upper-right corner of the **Data Integration** tab. You can view the statistics on batch synchronization nodes in the following sections:
**Status of Resource Group for Data Integration** : This section displays information
about each resource group for Data Integration, including the **status**, **number of running**
**nodes**, **number of queuing nodes**, and **resource usage**.
**Running Status Distribution**: This section displays the distribution of batch
synchronization node instances in different states. The data timestamp of these node instances is in the specified time range. The statistics in this section are updated when you load the page. You can click a sector in the pie chart to view the node instances in a specific state.
**Data Synchronization Progress**: This section displays information about the data that is
involved in batch synchronization within the specified time range. The metrics include
**Total Amount of Data**, **Total Internet Traffic**, and **Total Data Records**.
**Statistics on Amount of Synchronized Data** : This section displays the curves of the
data that is read from or written to different data sources within the specified time range. The **Latest Top 10 Tasks** section displays the **latest 10 node instances that failed to**
**be run** and the **latest 10 node instances that are successfully run** . The statistics
provide you with an overview of the latest node instance status.
**Statistics on Amount of Synchronized Data** : This section allows you to specify filter
conditions to search for node instances. The filter conditions include **submission time**,
**status**, and **node name**. You can click the **ID of a node** to view the details of the node
instance.

**View statistics on real-time synchronization nodes on the Data**

**Integration tab**

On the **Overview** page, click the **Data Integration** tab. On the **Data Integration** tab, click
**Real-time Synchronization**. You can view the statistics on real-time synchronization nodes
in the following sections:
**Status of Resource Group for Data Integration** : This section displays information
about each resource group for Data Integration, including the **status**, **number of running**
**nodes**, **number of queuing nodes**, and **resource usage**.
**Running Status Distribution**: This section displays the distribution of real-time
synchronization node instances in different states. The statistics in this section are updated when you load the page. You can click a sector in the pie chart to view the node instances in a specific state.
**Overview**: This section displays the total data transmission speed and total recording
speed of all real-time synchronization node instances in the current workspace.
**Top 10 Tasks with Highest Latency**: This section displays the top 10 node instances
that have the highest latency. This section can help you quickly find node instances that have high latency.
**Alert Information**: This section displays information about the latest alerts. This section
allows you to quickly view exceptions.
**Failover Information**: This section displays information about failovers within a specific
time period. This section provides you with an overview of failovers.

### Real-time node O&M

#### Manage real-time computing nodes

The Stream Task page of the DataWorks console displays all real-time computing nodes. You can view the basic information and details of the nodes on this page. You can also configure alert rules for the nodes that you want to monitor. This way, you can identify and handle exceptions at the earliest opportunity if an error occurs on a node.

**Limits**

DataWorks supports O&M only for E-MapReduce (EMR) Spark Streaming and EMR Streaming SQL nodes on the Stream Task page.

**Go to the Stream Task page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
icon and choose **All Products > Data Development**
**and O&M > Operation Center**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **RealTime Task Maintenance > Stream Task** to
go to the Stream Task page.

**View real-time computing nodes in the node list**

The Stream Task page displays all real-time computing nodes in the production environment. You can view the basic information of a real-time computing node and perform operations such as starting, stopping, and undeploying a real-time computing node. You can also configure alert rules for a real-time computing node. In the upper part of the page, you can specify filter conditions to search for real-time computing nodes.

**Note**

If you search for nodes by node ID or node name, the search results are affected by other filter conditions that you specified. Only the nodes that meet all the filter conditions that you specified are displayed. If you search for nodes by node name, fuzzy match is supported. After you enter a keyword, all real-time computing nodes whose names contain the keyword are displayed. You can view the basic information and details of a real-time computing node in the realtime monitoring node list:
**Node Name**: the name of the node. You can click the node name to open the details
panel of the node.
**Node ID**: the ID of the node.
**Status**: the state of the node. The node can be in one of the following states: **Not**
**Running**, **Generating**, **Pending (Resources)**, **Starting**, **Running**, **Stopped**, **Failed**,
**Restarting**, and **Undeploying**.
**Start running**: the time when the node started to run.
**End Running**: the time when the running of the node was complete.
**Runtime**: the duration for which the node was running. Unit: seconds.
**Task type**: the type of the node.
**Cluster Type**: the type of the cluster in which the real-time computing node runs.
DataWorks supports O&M only for real-time computing nodes that are run in EMR clusters.
**Cluster Name**: the name of the EMR cluster in which the real-time computing node runs.
**Deployed At**: the time when the node was deployed. The time is in the yyyy-MM-dd
HH:mm:ss format.
**Responsible Person**: the owner of the workspace to which the node belongs.

**Note**

You can rank all real-time computing nodes in ascending or descending order based on the values in the **Start running**, **End Running**, or **Runtime** column. You can perform the following operations on a real-time monitoring node in the Actions column:
**Start**: Start the node if it is not running.
**Terminate**: Stop the node if it is running.
**Undeploy**: Undeploy the node if it is deployed.
**Monitoring Setting**: Configure alert rules for the node. If the node fails to run, the
system sends an alert notification to the specified alert contact by using the alert notification method you configured. You can select multiple nodes and click **Start**, **Terminate**, **Undeploy**, or **Monitoring**
**Setting** in the lower part of the page to perform the related operation on these nodes.

**View the details of a real-time computing node**

On the Stream Task page, find the real-time computing node whose details you want to view and click the node name to open the details panel of the node. In the details panel of the node, you can view the details, run logs, operation logs, and code of the node on the **Details**,
**Runtime Log**, **Operation Log**, and **Code** tabs. This allows you to quickly find the operations
performed on the node, view operation details, obtain the details of the errors reported for the node, and fix the errors.

#### Manage real-time synchronization

**nodes**

The Real Time DI page of the DataWorks console displays all real-time synchronization nodes that are committed to and run by the scheduling system.

**Go to the Real Time DI page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
icon and choose **All Products > Data Development**
**and O&M > Operation Center**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane of the Operation Center page, choose **RealTime Task**
**Maintenance > Real Time DI** to go to the Real Time DI page.

**View real-time synchronization nodes in the node list**

The node list on the Real Time DI page displays real-time synchronization nodes that are run by the scheduling system. You can manage these nodes and perform O&M operations on these nodes. For example, you can view the basic information, properties, and details of a real-time synchronization node. You can also start or undeploy a real-time synchronization node. At the top of the page, you can specify filter conditions to search for specific real-time synchronization nodes. In the real-time synchronization node list, you can view the basic information and running status of each real-time synchronization node.
**ID**: the ID of the node.
**Node Name**: the name of the node. You can click the node name to open the details
panel of the node.
**Status**: the status of the node. The node can be in one of the following states:
**Abnormal**, **Not running**, **In operation**, **Stop**, **Stopping**, and **Waiting for resources**.
**Description**: the description of the node.
**Business delay**: the period of time between the current time and the offset from which
incremental data starts to be synchronized.
**Current Synchronization Site**: the offset at which incremental data is being
synchronized.
**Recent operation time**: the time when the last operation was performed on the node.
**Operated By**: the user who last performed an operation on the node.
**Source Type**: the type of the source.
**Source**: the name of the source.
**Destination Type**: the type of the destination.
**Destination**: the name of the destination.

| Parameter | Description | Required |
|---|---|---|

**Owner**: the owner of the workspace to which the node belongs.
**Current Start Site**: the offset from which incremental data starts to be synchronized.
**Data Read Speed (Bytes per Second)**: the speed at which the data is read.
**Record read speed (RPS)**: the speed at which the read data is written to logs.
**Resource Group for Data Integration**: the resource group that is used to run the
node. You can select multiple real-time synchronization nodes and perform the following operations on these nodes at a time at the bottom of the page:
**Start**: Start the nodes if they are not running.
**Stop**: Stop the nodes if they are running.
**Undeploy**: Undeploy the nodes if they are not running, abnormal, or stopped.
**Configure Alert Rule**: Configure alert rules for the nodes.
**Modify Alert Settings**: Delete, enable, or disable alert rules and modify alert rules
based on the metric type for the nodes.

**View the details of a real-time synchronization node**

On the Real Time DI page, find the real-time synchronization node whose details you want to view and click the node name to open the details panel of the node. In the details panel of the node, you can view the details about the node on the **Running Information**, **Log**, **General**,
**Task Configuration**, **Failover**, and **DDL records** tabs.

**Perform operations on a real-time synchronization node**

Find the task that you want to start and click **Start** in the **Actions** column. In the Start dialog box, configure the parameters and click **Determine**. The system starts to run the node. Find the node that you want to stop and click **Stop** in the Actions column. In the message that appears, click **Stop**. Find the node that you want to undeploy and click **Undeploy** in the Actions column. In the message that appears, click **Undeploy**. View the alert rule settings of a real-time synchronization node Find the node whose alert rule settings you want to view and click View Alert Settings in the Actions column. On the **Alert Events** tab, you can view the alert events of the node and filter alert events by configuring the **Occurrence Time**, **Alert Level**, and **Rules** parameters. Click the **Alert Rules** tab. On this tab, you can view all the alert rules that are created for the node. In the alert rule list, you can view the metric type and status of an alert rule. You can also modify, pause, delete, or test an alert rule by clicking **Edit**, **Pause**, **Delete**, or **Test** in the **Actions** column. If you want to create an alert rule, click **Create Rule** in the upper-right corner of the Alert Rules tab and configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Name | The name of the alert rule. | Yes |
|---|---|---|
| Description | The description of the alert rule. | No |
| Metrics | The type of metric that triggers an alert. The Metrics parameter and the Threshold parameter must be used in pairs. The value of the Threshold parameter varies based on the value of the Metrics parameter. Valid values: Task status, Business delay, Failover, Dirty Data, and Not Supported by DDL Statements. | Yes |
| Threshold | The thresholds for the metric type that is specified by the Metrics parameter. If you set the Metrics parameter to Task status, you must specify the minimum interval at which alerts are triggered. If you set the Metrics parameter to Business delay, you must specify a duration for business latency and another duration during which an alert can last after the duration for business latency elapses. If you set the Metrics parameter to Failover, you must specify a duration and the maximum number of failovers that can be performed within the duration before an alert is triggered. If you set the Metrics parameter to Dirty Data, you must specify a duration and the maximum number of dirty data records that are allowed within the duration before an alert is triggered. If you set the Metrics parameter to Not Supported by DDL Statements, you need to only select an alert level. | Yes |
| Alert Interval | The minimum interval at which alerts are reported. Default value: 5. Unit: minutes. The minimum interval cannot be shorter than 1 minute. | Yes |

| WARNING | The method used to receive a notification for a WARNING-level alert. Valid values: Email, Text Message, Telephone, and DingTalk. Note Email: If you want to use a Resource Access Management (RAM) user to receive the notification, you must use an Apsara Stack tenant account to add the email address of the RAM user to user information. Text Message: If you want to use a RAM user to receive the notification, you must use an Apsara Stack tenant account to add the mobile number of the RAM user to user information. Telephone: If you want to use a RAM user to receive the notification, you must use an Apsara Stack tenant account to add the mobile number of the RAM user to user information. DingTalk: If you want to receive the notification by using a DingTalk chatbot, you must configure a DingTalk chatbot for your DingTalk group and add the keyword DataWorks for the DingTalk chatbot. | No |
|---|---|---|
| CRITICAL | The method used to receive a notification for a CRITICAL-level alert. Valid values: Email, Text Message, Telephone, and DingTalk. | No |
| Receiver | The alert contact to whom alert notifications are sent. | Yes |

### Auto triggered node O&M

#### Manage auto triggered nodes

Auto triggered nodes are automatically run as scheduled after they are committed to the scheduling system. You can view the details of and manage an auto triggered node in the auto triggered node list or in the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of the node.

**Note**

By default, the auto triggered node list displays nodes in all the workflows created by using the current account. After you commit a node, the scheduling system automatically generates instances for the node at 23:30 the next day and runs these instances. If you commit a node after 23:30, the scheduling system automatically generates instances for the node on the third day and runs these instances. Do not freeze the **projectname_root** node, which is the root node of your workspace. All the instances of auto triggered nodes depend on this node. If this node is frozen, the instances of auto triggered nodes cannot be run.

**View the list of auto triggered nodes**

The **Cycle Task** page displays the auto triggered nodes that are committed to the scheduling system in a list. In the upper part of the page, you can specify filter conditions to search for auto triggered nodes. You can perform the following operations in the **Actions** column: Find a node in the node list and click **DAG** in the Actions column to view the DAG of the node. You can view the node information in the DAG, such as properties, operation logs, and code. Find a node in the node list and click **Test** in the Actions column to test the node. Find a node in the node list and click **Backfill Data** in the Actions column to backfill data for the node.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| Show Ancestor Nodes or Show Descendant Nodes | You can view the ancestor or descendant nodes of the node at one or more levels. If a workflow contains three or more nodes, specific nodes are automatically hidden in the DAG. You can select a greater number of levels to view more comprehensive node dependencies. |
| View Auto Triggered Task Details | You can go to the Node Basic Information page to view the node information, including the input table, output table, ancestor nodes, and descendant nodes. |
| View Code | You can view the code of the node. |
| Edit Node | You can go to the DataStudio page and modify the node. |
| View Instances | You can view the auto triggered node instances of the node. |

Find a node in the node list and click **More** in the Actions column to perform more operations on the node, such as freezing and unfreezing the node, and viewing the instances of the node. Select **Freeze** to freeze the node. After the node is frozen, the system generates instances for the node but does not run the instances of the node or its descendant instances. Select **Unfreeze** to unfreeze the node. After the node is unfrozen, the system normally runs the instances of the node and its descendant instances. Select **Change Owner** to change the owner of the node. Select **Modify Scheduling Resource Group** to change the resource group used to run the node if the workspace has multiple resource groups. Select **Configure Data Quality Rules** to configure the rules that are used to monitor the data quality of the node. Select **View Instances** to view the auto triggered node instances of the node. Select **View Lineage** to view the lineage of the node. Select **View Auto Triggered Task Details** to go to the **Node Basic Information** page. On this page, you can view the node information on the **Ancestor Nodes** and
**Descendant Nodes** tabs.
Select **Add Alert Rule** to configure alert rules for the node. Select **Add Baseline** to add the node to a baseline for monitoring. You can also select multiple auto triggered nodes and click **Freeze**, **Unfreeze**, **Change**
**Owner**, or **Modify Scheduling Resource Group** at the bottom of the page to perform
operations on the nodes at a time.

**View the DAG of an auto triggered node**

Find a node in the node list and click its name or **DAG** in the Actions column to view the DAG of the node. In the DAG, you can right-click the node to perform related operations.

| View Lineage | You can view the lineage of the node. |
|---|---|
| Go to Task 360 Page | You can go to the Task 360 page of Data Governance Center and view information about the node in the Basic Information and Governance Items for Node sections. |
| Test | You can perform smoke testing for the node. In theT est dialog box, configure the Test Name and Data Timestamp parameters, and click OK. The Test Instance page appears. |
| Backfill Data | You can backfill data for the node. The following data backfill modes are supported: Backfill Data for Current Node, Current and Descendant Nodes Retroactively, Massive Node Mode, and Advanced Mode. |
| Freeze | You can freeze the node for which a data backfill instance is generated to pause the scheduling of the node. |
| Unfreeze | You can resume the scheduling of the frozen node. |
| Configure Data Quality Rules | You can configure the rules that are used to monitor the data quality of the node. |

#### Manage auto triggered node instances

An auto triggered node instance is a snapshot that is taken for an auto triggered node at the time when the node is scheduled to run. You can view the details of and manage an auto triggered node instance in the list of auto triggered node instances or in the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of the instance. Normal node or instance: A normal node or instance is a node or instance that actually runs code. Normal nodes or instances do not include dry-run nodes or instances and frozen nodes or instances. Dry-run nodes or instances include nodes whose scheduling mode is set to dryrun, instances that are not generated during the period of time in which nodes are scheduled, branch nodes that are not selected, and expired instances that are generated when the scheduled time for running nodes is less than 10 minutes from the point in time when the nodes are committed and deployed. An instance is generated each time an auto triggered node is run as scheduled. You can manage auto triggered node instances that have been scheduled. For example, you can view the status of instances, and stop, rerun, and unfreeze instances.

**Note**

Instances are generated as scheduled for auto triggered nodes. Each generated instance runs the latest code. If you modify and recommit the code of a node after instances are generated for the node, the instances that are not run will run the latest code.

**View and manage auto triggered node instances from the**

**instance perspective**

On the **Cycle Instance** page, click the **Instance Perspective** tab.

**Manage auto triggered node instances in the instance list**

You can manage auto triggered node instances in the instance list and perform O&M operations on the instances. For example, you can check run logs, rerun instances, and stop instances that are running. In the upper part of the page, you can specify filter conditions to search for nodes.

**Note**

By default, the data timestamp is set to the day before the current day. You can select **Slow Node** to find slow running instances. A node instance is considered a slow running instance if the node instance is running and the duration of the node instance is at least 15 minutes longer than the average duration of the node instance during the last 10 days. If the number of historical node instances is less than four and the duration of a node instance exceeds 30 minutes, the node instance can also be considered a slow running instance. In the auto triggered node instance list, you can view the basic information and running status of the instances. You can perform the following operations in the **Actions** column:
**DAG**: You can open the DAG of the auto triggered node instance to view the
dependencies of the instance. In the DAG, you can right-click the instance to perform related operations.
**Rerun**: You can rerun the auto triggered node instance if it is in the Succeeded or Failed
state. After the instance is successfully run, its descendant instances that are in the Pending (Ancestor) state can be scheduled to run. You can perform this operation to handle an instance that fails to be run or is not run as scheduled.

**Note**

Only instances in the **Succeeded** or **Failed** state can be rerun.
**More**:
**Rerun Descendent Nodes**: You can rerun the descendant instances of the auto
triggered node instance if it is in the Succeeded or Failed state. You can select the descendant instances that you want to rerun. After a selected instance is successfully run, its descendant instances that are in the Pending (Ancestor) state can be scheduled to run. You can perform this operation to recover data.

**Note**

Only descendant instances in the **Succeeded** or **Failed** state can be selected. The value No is displayed in the **Meet Rerun Condition** column for instances in other states, and you cannot select these instances.
**Set Status to Successful** : You can set the state of the auto triggered node instance
to Succeeded if it fails to be run. You can perform this operation if you do not want an instance that fails to be run to block the running of its descendant instances. You can perform this operation to handle an instance that fails to be run.
**Stop**: You can stop the auto triggered node instance if it does not need to be run. After
you stop the instance, the instance fails to be run and exits.

**Note**

Only instances in the **Pending (Schedule)**, **Pending (Resources)**, or **Running** state can be stopped.
**Freeze**: You can freeze the auto triggered node instance if you do not need to run the
instance or its descendant instances. The freeze operation takes effect only on the current auto triggered node instance that is in the Running state. The frozen auto triggered node instance cannot be scheduled as expected and does not generate data. In addition, its descendant instances cannot be scheduled and run as expected.

**Note**

Do not perform this operation on the `projectname_root` task, which is the root task of your workspace. All the instances of auto triggered nodes depend on this node. If this node is frozen, the instances of auto triggered nodes cannot be run.
**Unfreeze**: You can unfreeze the auto triggered node instance if it is frozen.
If the instance is not run, it is automatically run after its ancestor instances are successfully run. If all the ancestor instances of the instance are successfully run, the instance enters the Failed state. You must manually rerun the instance.

**Note**

The unfreeze operation takes effect only on the current auto triggered node instance. If the auto triggered node for which the instance is generated is frozen, instances that are scheduled to run on the next day are also frozen.
**View Lineage**: You can view the lineage of the auto triggered node instance.
**View Auto Triggered Task Details**: You can view the basic information of the auto
triggered node instance.
**View Runtime Log**: You can view the run logs of the auto triggered node instance.

#### Manage data backfill instances

You can backfill data over a historical period of time or a period of time in the future for an auto triggered node to write the data to time-based partitions. If scheduling parameters are used in the node code, the scheduling parameters are automatically replaced with specific values based on the data timestamp that you specify to backfill data for the node. The data that corresponds to the data timestamp is written to specific partitions based on the business code. The partitions to which the data is written are related to the logic and content of the node code. This topic describes how to backfill data for an auto triggered node and manage data backfill instances generated for the node.

**Background information**

After an auto triggered node is developed, committed, and deployed to the scheduling system, the scheduling system runs the node based on the scheduling configurations of the node. If you want to run the auto triggered node in a specific time range, you can backfill data for the node. DataWorks allows you to backfill data for the current node and its descendant nodes. The following data backfill modes are supported:
**Backfill Data for Current Node** : This mode allows you to backfill data for the current
node.
**Current and Descendent Nodes Retroactively**: This mode allows you to backfill data
for the current node and its descendent nodes at a time. If the current node has a small number of descendant nodes, we recommend that you use this mode. In this mode, you can specify the descendant nodes for which you want to backfill data.
**Massive Node Mode**: This mode allows you to backfill data for the current node and its
descendant nodes at a time. If the current node has a large number of descendant nodes, we recommend that you use this mode. In this mode, you can filter descendant nodes by workspace to specify the descendant nodes for which you want to backfill data. You can configure a whitelist to backfill data for some nodes that are not in the selected workspaces. You can also configure a blacklist to filter out some nodes that are in the selected workspaces.
**Advanced Mode**: This mode allows you to backfill data for multiple nodes at a time. In this
mode, you can select nodes that do not have dependencies with each other. You can select nodes for which you want to backfill data in the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of an auto triggered node or in the node list on the Cycle Task page. In the DAG, you can use the node aggregation feature to group nodes by workspace, owner, or priority. This way, you can backfill data for multiple nodes at a time by specifying a node group. You can also select nodes in the node list on the Cycle Task page. You can filter nodes based on specific conditions and select the nodes for which you want to backfill data.

**Limits**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Backfill Task Name | DataWorks automatically generates a data backfill instance name. You can modify the name based on your business requirements. |
| Current Task | The name of the node for which you want to backfill data. |

When DataWorks backfills data over a specific time range for a node, if an instance generated for the node fails on a day within the time range, the state of the data backfill instance of the node for that day is also set to Failed. In this case, DataWorks does not run the instances generated for this node for the next day. DataWorks runs the instances generated for a node on a day only after all instances generated for the node on the previous day are successfully run. For a self-dependent auto triggered node, if a previous-cycle instance is not run on the previous day, the first data backfill instance generated for the node cannot be run. If the node has no previous-cycle instance on the previous day, the first data backfill instance generated for the node is directly run. DataWorks generates alerts only for auto triggered node instances that fail. If an auto triggered node instance is running for a node, the data backfill instance and test instance of the node can be run only after the running of the auto triggered node instance is complete. If both an auto triggered node instance and a data backfill node instance are running for a node, you must stop the data backfill node instance to ensure that the auto triggered node instance can be run as expected.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products**
**> Data Development and O&M > Operation Center**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane of the Operation Center page, choose **Cycle Task**
**Maintenance > Cycle Task**.
4. On the Cycle Task page, find the auto triggered node for which you want to backfill data
and open its DAG. In the DAG, right-click the node, move the pointer over **Run**, and then select a data backfill mode.

**Backfill data for the current node**

1. Find the node for which you want to backfill data, click **Backfill Data** in the Actions
column, and then click **Backfill Data for Current Node** .
2. In the **Backfill Data** dialog box, configure the parameters that are described in the
following table.

| Data Timestam p | The data timestamp of the data backfill instance. A data timestamp specifies a specific date. If you want to backfill data for the node for multiple non-consecutive time ranges, click Add Multiple Data Timestamp Ranges to specify multiple data timestamps. If the data timestamp that you specify for a data backfill instance is later than the current date, you can select Run Retroactive Instances Scheduled to Run after the Current Time. The system runs the data backfill instance immediately after the data timestamp passes. For example, if the current date is August 24, 2021 , the data timestamp of a data backfill instance is set to September 17, 2021 , and you select Run Retroactive Instances Scheduled to Run after the Current Time, the data backfill instance is immediately run at the beginning of September 18, 2021 . Note We recommend that you do not set this parameter to a long time range. Otherwise, data backfill instances may be delayed due to insufficient resources. |
|---|---|
| Parallelis m | Specifies whether to run multiple data backfill instances in parallel. Valid values: No: Multiple data backfill instances are run in sequence based on the data timestamps. Yes: A specific number of data backfill instances are generated based on the data timestamps and run in parallel. Data backfill instances with different data timestamps are run at the same time. |

| Number of concurren t instances | The number of data backfill instances that are generated and run in parallel during data backfill. Note You must specify the number of data backfill instances that are run in parallel if you set the Parallelism parameter to Yes. You can set the number of data backfill instances that are run in parallel to an integer from 2 to 10. The details are as follows if multiple data backfill instances are run in parallel: If the number of data timestamps is less than the specified number of data backfill instances that are run in parallel, all data backfill instances are run in parallel. For example, the data timestamps are from January 11 to January 13, and the number of data backfill instances that are run in parallel is 4. In this case, a data backfill instance is generated for each of the three data timestamps. The three data backfill instances are run in parallel. If the number of data timestamps is greater than the specified number of data backfill instances that are run in parallel, the system runs some data backfill instances in sequence and the other data backfill instances in parallel based on the data timestamps. For example, the data timestamps are from January 11 to January 13, and the number of data backfill instances that are run in parallel is 2. In this case, two data backfill instances are generated and run in parallel. One of the instances has two data timestamps, and is run twice in sequence based on the data timestamps. |
|---|---|
| Alert for Data Backfill | If you select Yes, you must configure Trigger Condition and Alert Notification Method. If an exception occurs in the data backfill instance, the system sends alerts based on the specified alert method. |
| Order | The sequence based on which data backfill instances are run. Valid values: Ascending by Data Timestamp and Descending by Data Timestamp. |
| Resource Group for Schedulin g | Specifies whether to select another resource group to run the data backfill instance. If you select Yes, the data backfill instance does not need to compete for resources with auto triggered node instances. Valid values: Yes: You can select a resource group to run the data backfill instance. No: The resource group that is configured for the current node is used to run the data backfill instance. |

| Execution Period | The time range during which you want to run the data backfill instance. If you select Specify Time Period, you can select a time range to run the instance. If you select Follow Task Configuration, the data backfill instance is immediately run in most cases. If you set Data Timestamp to the current date or a date later than the current date and you do not select Run Retroactive Instances Scheduled to Run after the Current Time, the data backfill instance is run as scheduled. |
|---|---|
| Terminate Task Running upon Verificatio n Failure | The basic verification is performed for the data backfill instance. If the verification fails, you can choose whether to terminate the task. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Include Current Task for Data Backfilling | Specifies whether the current node is included for data backfilling. |
| Tasks That Require Data Backfill | You can filter nodes by node name and level, and select the nodes for which you want to backfill data. Note Fuzzy match is supported when you search for nodes byn ode name. After you enter a keyword, all nodes whose names contain the keyword are displayed in the table below the search box. The Tasks That Require Data Backfill section includes the current node and its descendant nodes of all levels. You can select the current node and some or all of its descendant nodes. |

3. Click Submit and Redirect.

**Backfill data for the current node and its descendant nodes**

#### Forcefully rerun the descendant

**instances of an auto triggered node instance**

DataWorks allows you to forcefully rerun the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance. You can specify whether the rerun starts from the auto triggered node instance or from the level-1 descendant instances of the auto triggered node instance. You can also filter descendant instances that you want to rerun by workspace. This topic describes how to forcefully rerun the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance and provides the related usage notes.

**Limits**

You can forcefully rerun the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance only as a workspace administrator or tenant administrator, or by using an Apsara Stack tenant account. When you filter the descendant instances that you want to rerun by workspace, you can select only the workspaces in which you are the administrator. You can forcefully rerun only the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance that meets the following requirements: The data timestamp of the auto triggered node instance is the previous day or the day before the previous day. The state of the auto triggered node instance is Succeeded or Failed. If the auto triggered node instance does not meet the preceding requirements, the Force Heavy Run Downstream option is dimmed. Each tenant in a region can forcefully rerun the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance only once at the same point in time.

**Usage notes**

If you forcefully rerun the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance, the states of the descendant instances are set to Not running. If the descendant instances that you want to forcefully rerun are running, the descendant instances are forcefully stopped when you rerun them. For an auto triggered node, if you set the **Rerun** parameter to **Disallow Regardless of**
**Running Status** in the Schedule section of the Properties tab, you will fail to forcefully
rerun the descendant instances of the instance generated by the auto triggered node. For more information about how to modify the value of the Rerun parameter, see Configure time properties.

**Procedure**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Timestamp | The data timestamp of the auto triggered node instance whose descendant instances you want to forcefully rerun. You can forcefully rerun only the descendant instances of an auto triggered node instance whose data timestamp is the previous day or the day before the previous day. |
| Start Instance | The instance from which the forceful rerun starts in the current workspace. |
| Heavy Run Starting Point | Specifies whether the forceful rerun starts from the current auto triggered node instance or from the level-1 descendant instances of the auto triggered node instance. |

1. Go to the Cycle Instance page in Operation Center, find the auto triggered node instance
whose descendant instances you want to forcefully rerun, and then open the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of the auto triggered node instance. Make sure that the data timestamp of the auto triggered node instance is the previous day or the day before the previous day and that the state of the auto triggered node instance is Succeeded or Failed. In the DAG, right-click the auto triggered node instance and choose **Emergency**
**Operations > Force Heavy Run Downstream**. The Force Heavy Run Downstream dialog
box is displayed.
2. Configure the parameters in the Force Heavy Run Downstream dialog box.
i. Complete the basic settings.

| Heavy Run Cross-Days Instance | Specifies whether to forcefully rerun the instance (Instance B) that depends on the current instance (Instance A) when you rerun the current instance. The data timestamp of Instance B is the current day, and the data timestamp of Instance A is the previous day. For example, in the preceding figure, Instance B is generated by a node scheduled by day and depends on Instance A. The data timestamp of Instance A is the previous day, and the data timestamp of Instance B is the current day. If you want to forcefully rerun Instance A, you can determine whether to rerun Instance B. If you set Heavy Run Cross-Days Instance to Yes, Instance B is rerun after Instance A is rerun. |
|---|---|
