4. On the Data Overview page, view information about all compute engines that belong to
your Apsara Stack tenant account in the current region. The following table lists the overall data of the `MaxCompute` compute engine.

| Total APIs | The total number of MaxCompute APIs that are published to API Gateway up to the current time for the current tenant in the current region. |
|---|---|
| Storage Trend Chart | The trend chart of the logical storage space that is occupied by all MaxCompute projects for the current tenant in the current region. The logical storage space includes the space that is occupied by temporary files of auto triggered tasks and the space that is not released after tables are deleted. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day. |
| Top Projects by Table Storage | The MaxCompute projects that occupy the most logical storage space for the current tenant in the current region. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day. |
| Top Tables by Occupied Storage | The MaxCompute tables that occupy the most logical storage space. You can click a table name to go to the details page of the table. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day. Note The Top Projects by Table Storage and Top Tables by Occupied Storage sections display the logical storage space that is occupied by MaxCompute projects and the logical storage space that is occupied by MaxCompute tables. The statistics are generated and collected in offline mode. The logical storage space displayed for each project includes the logical storage space occupied by tables, resources, recycle bins, and files of other systems. As a result, the logical storage space displayed for each project is greater than the logical storage space occupied by tables in the project. You are charged for the logical storage space of tables but not the physical storage space of tables. |
| Most Frequently Used Tables | The tables that are most frequently accessed. The statistics are generated based on the number of views of the details page of each table. Quasi-real-time statistics are displayed. |

#### Data search

If you want to quickly find data, such as tables, APIs, and workspaces within your data sources, you can perform searches in Data Map.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > Data Governance >**
**Data Map(Data Management)**. The homepage of Data Map appears.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click the **Search** icon.
4. In the **Type** section, select **Table**, **API**, or **Workspace** based on your business
requirements.

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | Select Table. |
| Data Source | Select a data source, such as MaxCompute or MySQL. The data sources displayed in the console shall prevail. |
| Filter Condition | The filter parameters displayed in the console may vary slightly depending on the selected data source. You can enter keywords for the corresponding parameters to perform a more precise search. |
| Keep Current Filters | Specifies whether to retain the currently configured filter conditions. If you want to retain them, select this check box. To reset the settings, click Reset. |

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | Select API. |
| Filter Condition | This section includes the following parameters: Workspace: the workspace to which the API belongs. Enter a keyword to search for the workspace. Owner: the owner of the workspace to which the API belongs. Enter a member name to search for the owner. API Type: Select one of the following API types based on your business requirements. Generate API (Codeless UI) Generate API (Code Editor) Register API Service Orchestration |
| Keep Current Filters | Specifies whether to retain the currently configured filter conditions. If you want to retain them, select this check box. To reset the settings, click Reset. |

Table search API search Workspace search

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | Select Workspace. |
| Filter Condition | Owner: the owner of the workspace. Enter a member name to search for the owner. |
| Keep Current Filters | Specifies whether to retain the currently configured filter conditions. If you want to retain them, select this check box. To reset the settings, click Reset. |

5. After you configure the preceding filter conditions, the search results are displayed on the
right side of the page for you to view them and perform related operations.

##### View the details of a table

This topic describes how to go to the details page of a table and view the details of the table, such as the basic information, output information, and lineage information.

**Go to the details page of a table**

You can go to the details page of a table by searching for the table. For more information, see Data search. On the details page of a table, you can view information about the table in the following sections: **Table Basic Information**, **Business Information**, **Permission Information**,
**Technical Information**, **Details**, **Output**, **Lineage**, **Usage Notes**, **Data Quality**, **Usage**
**Records**, and **Data Preview**.
At the top of this page, you can perform the following operations:
**Request Permissions**: You can find a table and click Request Permissions to apply for
permissions on the table in Security Center and view application records in Data Map.
**Add To/View Album**: You can add the table to a data album and manage the table on
the details page of the data album. You can also view the data albums to which the table is added.
**Add to Favorites** or **Remove from Favorites**: You can add the table to or remove the
table from **My Favorites**.
**Generate API**: You can use the table to generate or register an API in DataService
Studio.
**Data Analysis**: You can query and analyze data in the table by executing SQL
statements on the **SQL Query** page in DataAnalysis.
**Refresh**: You can refresh the table details that are displayed on this page.
On the left side of this page, you can view the following information about the table:
**Table Basic Information**: In this section, you can view the basic information about the
table, such as the number of times the table is viewed, the number of times the table is read, and the number of times the table is added to My Favorites. You can click **View**
**Code** next to the **Output Node** parameter to view the node code.

**Note**

**Views**: This item displays the number of times that the table is viewed in Data
Map over the last 30 days. The number of times is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.
**Reads**: This item displays the number of times that the table is read from the
production environment by executing SQL statements or running Tunnel Download commands, or for data synchronization over the last 30 days. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.
**Favorites**: This item displays the number of times that the table is added to
My Favorites. The number of times is collected in real time.
**Storage**: This item displays the logical storage space occupied by data in the
table. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.
**Output Node**: This item displays the ID of the auto triggered node that
generates the table. If the table is periodically updated but no node ID is displayed, the data in the table may not be generated by an auto triggered node in DataWorks. You can contact the table owner for details. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.
**Business Information**: In this section, you can view information such as the name of
the workspace to which the table belongs, the environment type, and the category to which the table belongs.
**Permission Information**: In this section, you can view your permissions on a table.
After you click **Click to View**, the **Permission Application** tab appears. You can view the request processing status on this tab.
**Technical Information**: In this section, you can view the following information about a
table: **DDL Statement Updated At**, **Data Updated At**, and **Last Viewed At**.

**Note**

Last Viewed At: The value of this parameter indicates the time when the table was last accessed by using a command or in a node scheduling scenario. The time is for reference only and may not be the same as the actual time when the table was last accessed. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day. On the right side of this page, you can view the following information about the table:
**Details**: You can view the following information of the table on this tab: **Field**
**Information**, **Partition Information**, and **Change Records**.
**Output**: If the table data periodically changes with the node that generates the table,
you can view the change status and the data that is continuously updated on this tab. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.
**Lineage**: You can view the inner lineages of the node that generates the table. If the
current table is used as the data source of an API, you can also view the lineages between the table and the API. Data Map also allows you to view the full-link lineage of a MaxCompute table for batch synchronization. The information is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.

**Note**

For more information about how to view the complete lineages of a DataService Studio API, see View the details of an API. Due to the complexity of data cleaning, the impact analysis feature of the current field cannot be completely integrated and accurate. Do not use this feature if you have requirements on integrity and accuracy in your business.
**Usage Notes**: On this tab, you can click **Edit** to modify the table usage notes and click
**View Versions** to view the historical versions of the table usage notes.
**Data Quality**: You can view the monitoring rules that are configured for the table and
the alerts that are generated based on the monitoring rules. You can click **Configure**
**Rules** to go to the Data Quality page and configure monitoring rules for the table.
**Usage Records**: You can view the reference and access records of the table on the
following subtabs:
**Frequently Associated**: You can view the number of times that the table data is
referenced on this subtab.

**Note**

The Frequently Associated subtab displays the number of times that the table data is referenced over the last 30 days. The number of times is collected in offline mode and is updated with a delay of one day.
**Access Statistics**: You can view a list of access records of the table on this subtab:
**Data Preview**: You can preview the data in the table on this tab.

**Important**

You can preview the tables that are in the production environment only if you are granted the required permissions. If the preview feature for tables is enabled for the workspace to which the table belongs, you can preview the table data without the need to apply for permissions on tables in Security Center. If you configure data masking rules and the data masking rules are in the active state, the Data Preview tab displays data based on the data masking rules. The Data Preview tab cannot display data in external tables.

##### View the details of an API

This topic describes how to go to the details page of an API and view the details of the API, such as the basic information, parameters, and sample response.

**Go to the details page of an API**

You can go to the details page of an API by searching for the API on the homepage of Data Map. On the details page of an API, you can view the following information about the API: **Basic**
**Information**, **Technical Information**, **Parameter Information**, **Sample Response**,
**Lineage**, and **Usage Notes**.
At the top of this page, you can click **Edit API** to go to the configuration tab of the API in the related workspace and edit the API.

**Note**

If the account that you use to log in is not added as a member of the workspace to which the API belongs, contact the workspace administrator to add the account to the workspace as a member and assign the developer role to the account. On the left side of this page, you can view the following information about the API.
**Basic Information**: In this section, you can view the basic information about the API,
such as **Views**, **Calls**, **API ID**, **Workspace**, **Owner**, **Created At**, **Updated At**, and
**Description**.
**Technical Information**: In this section, you can view the technical information about the
API, such as the **API Type**, **Request Method**, **Response Type**, **Data Source Type**,
**Data Source Name**, and **Table Name**.
On the right side of this page, you can view the following information about the API.
**Parameter Information**: On this tab, you can view the **Request Parameters** of the
API.
**Request Parameters**: On this sub-tab, you can view information about **Common**
**Request Parameters** and **API Request Parameters**, such as **Parameter Name**,
**Parameter Type**, **Parameter Position**, **Sample Value**, **Default Value**, and
**Description**.
**Sample Response**: If you select **Save the correct response example automatically**
during an API test before the API is published, the sample response is updated based on the test result. You can view the result returned by an API request based on the data content and data structure on the **Sample Response** tab.
**Lineage**: On this tab, you can view the complete lineages of tables, APIs, and
applications.

**Note**

For a generated API, the API is generated based on a data source or by encapsulating a table. The API lineage includes data tables, the API, and applications. For a registered API, the API is obtained by encapsulating a backend address. The API lineage includes only the API and applications. The lineage information is generated and updated with a delay of one day.
**Usage Notes**: On this tab, you can click **Edit** to modify the API usage notes and click
**View Versions** to view the historical versions of the API usage notes.

#### Data album

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Album Name | The name of the data album. Note The name must be unique in each region of a tenant account. |
| Visible Scope | The visible scope of the data album. Valid values: Public and Private. Public: The data album is visible to all users. Private: The data album is visible only to the album creator and the album administrator. If you set this parameter to Private and want to allow a user to view the data album, you must assign the album administrator role to the user. |
| Description | The description of the data album. |

The data album feature allows you to organize and manage data tables based on business categories, data sensitivity levels, and data categories. You can add a specific data table to a data album. This way, you can search for and locate the data table in an efficient manner. This topic describes how to create, use, and manage data albums.

**Go to the Collections page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > Data Governance >**
**Data Map(Data Management)**. The homepage of Data Map appears.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data Album**. The **Collections** page appears.
1. On the **Collections** page, click **Create Collection**.
2. In the **Create Collection** dialog box, configure the parameters that are described in the
following table and click **Confirmation**.
1. On the **Collections** page, click **Created by Me**. Find the data album for which you want to
configure categories and click its name in the **Album Name** column. The details page of the data album appears.
2. In the directory on the **Objects** tab, right-click the category that is automatically created
for the data album to create a subcategory or rename the category. Create a subcategory: Right-click the category and select Create Subcategory. In the
**Create Subcategory** dialog box, configure the **Destination Directory** and **Category**
**Name** parameters.

**Note**

A category can contain at most four levels. Rename a category: Right-click the category and select Rename. In the **Rename** dialog box, configure the Category Name parameter.
3. Click **OK**.

**Method 1: Add data tables on the details page of a data album**

1. On the **Collections** page, click **Created by Me**. Find the data album to which you want to
add data tables and click its name in the Album Name column. The details page of the data album appears.
2. On the **Objects** tab, select a category and click **Add Table** in the right-side pane.
3. In the **Add Table** dialog box, you can filter the tables that you want to add to the data
album based on the search condition or recent browsing history.
4. Click **Add**.

**Method 2: Add a data table to a data album on the details page of the table or in**

**the search result on the All Data page.**

1. On the homepage of Data Map, search for a table by table name and go to the table details
page. In the upper part of the page, move the pointer over **Add To/View Album** and select
**Add to Album**.
2. In the **Add to Collection** dialog box, select the name of the data album to which you want
to add the data table.
3. Click **Confirmation**.

**Note**

You can modify only the data album that you created. i. On the details page of the data album whose attributes you want to modify, click **Edit** to the right of the album name. ii. In the **Modify Album** dialog box, you can modify the **Album Name, Visible Scope,**
**and Description** parameters.
iii. Click **Confirmation**. i. On the details page of the data album for which you want to change the album administrator, click the icon on the right side of **Administrator** below the album name. ii. In the **Edit Collection Administrator** dialog box, select an Apsara Stack account.

**Note**

You can specify up to five administrators for a data album. iii. Click **OK**. i. On the **Usage Notes** tab of the details page for the desired data album, click **Edit**. ii. In the **Edit** input field, modify the usage notes for the data album and click **Preview**. Confirm the modification information and click **Save**. iii. Optional. After the modification is complete, you can click **View Versions** to view the modification details of each version. Remove a data table from a data album. i. In the **Objects** directory, click the desired category. ii. Find the data table that you want to remove and choose **More > Remove from**
**Collection** in the **Actions** column
i. On the details page of the data album, click **Follow** and **Like**. ii. You can quickly locate the data album by clicking **Albums Followed** on the **Homepage** page of **Data Map** or clicking **Followed** on the **Collections** page of Data Map. On the **Collections** page, click **Managed by Me** or **Created by Me**. Find the data album that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

#### My data

This topic describes how to view and manage tables on the Owned by Me, Managed by Me, Managed by Production Account, and My Favorites pages in Data Map. This topic also describes how to view and manage data permissions.

**Background information**

In most cases, Data Map updates data one day after the data is generated. If you want to query real-time data, we recommend that you use SQL statements.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Data Map(Data Management)**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **My Data**. The **Owned by Me** tab of the **My Data**
page appears. You can view the tables owned by the current account and search for tables by keyword, environment, project or database, and visibility on the following pages. You can also view the details of a table and perform relevant operations on the table.
**Owned by Me**: All tables owned by the current account are displayed on this page.
**Managed by Me**: All tables in the workspaces of which the current account is the
workspace administrator are displayed on this page.
**Managed by Production Account**: All tables that belong to the production account of the
current workspace member are displayed on this page.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Table Name | The name of the table. You can click the table name to go to the details page of the table. |
| Project/Datab ase | The name of the project or database to which the table belongs. The suffix of the name varies based on the environment where the table resides. For example, dev _ indicates that the table resides in the development environment. |
| Creation Time | The point in time at which the table was created. |
| Display Name | Click Update Table Information in the Actions column to modify the display name of the table. |
| Environment | The environment where the table resides. Valid values: Development and Production. |
| Storage | The volume of data that is stored in the table. |
| Lifecycle | The time-to-live (TTL) period of the table. The value is the same as that you specified when you created the table. |
| Number of Favorites | The number of times that users added the table to favorites. |
| Number of Views in 30 Days | The number of times that users viewed the table in the last 30 days. |
| Visibility | The display status of the table. Valid values: Hide: The table cannot be found. Visible Only to Project Members: The table can be found only by members of the workspace in which the table resides. Visible: default value. The table can be found by all users. Note The setting of this parameter does not affect the table owner or workspace administrators. |
| Category | The category to which the table belongs. |

After the corresponding page appears, you can search for a table by specifying the
**Project/Database**, **Keyword**, **Environment**, **TTL**, **Visibility Range**, or **Category**
parameters, and view the following information about the table.

| Actions | You can find a table that you want to manage and clickU pdate Table Information, Delete, Transfer, Modify Category, or Add to Album in the Actions column to perform the related operation on the table. |
|---|---|
| Batch operation | The operations that you can perform on multiple tables at a time. You can select multiple tables and click Batch Transfer, Batch Update Table Information, Batch Delete, or Modify Category below the table list to transfer the tables, update the information about the tables, delete the tables, or modify the table categories at a time. |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Request Type | The type of the object on which you want to apply for permissions. Valid values: Function and Resource. |
| Grant To | The account to which permissions will be granted. Valid values:C urrent Account and Specified Account. If you select Current Account, permissions will be granted to your account after the application is approved. If you select Specified Account, you must configure the Username parameter. Permissions will be granted to the specified account after the application is approved. |

When you view the details of a table, you can click Add to Favorites on the details page of the table to add the table to **My Favorites**. Then, you can view the details in the **My Favorites** section on the **My Data** page. You can use the following two methods to remove a table from favorites. A removed table is not displayed on the **My Favorites** tab of the **My Data** page. On the My Favorites tab, find the table that you want to remove and click **Unfavorite** in the Actions column. Go to the details page of a table that has been added to favorites and click **Remove from**
**Favorites** in the upper part of the page.

**View and manage data permissions**

Click the **Permission Management** tab to view and manage permissions. On the **Permission Management** page, click **Request Permissions on Functions and**
**Resources** in the upper-right corner and view requests that are pending for you to process,
requests that you sent, and requests that you processed on the **To Be Processed**,
**Permission Request Records**, and **Processed by Me** tabs, respectively.

**Apply for function and resource permissions**

i. On the Permission Management page, click **Request Permissions on Functions and**
**Resources** in the upper-right corner.
ii. In the **Request Permissions on Functions and Resources** dialog box, configure the parameters. The following table describes the parameters.

| Project Name | The name of the MaxCompute project that contains the function or resource on which you want to apply for permissions. Fuzzy match is supported. |
|---|---|
| Function Name or Resource Name | The full name of the function or resource in the project. If the resource is a file, enter the full name of the file, including the file name extension. Example: my mr.jar. _ |
| Validity Period | The validity period of the permissions. Unit: day. If this parameter is left empty, the permissions are permanently valid. After the validity period has expired, the system automatically revokes the permissions. |
| Request Reason | The reason why you apply for the permissions. |

Approve permission applications on the **To Be Processed** tab If you are a workspace administrator, you can view and approve the applications for permissions on all objects such as tables, resources, and functions in the workspace on the
**To Be Processed** tab.
View permission applications on the **Permission Request Records** tab On the **Permission Request Records** tab, you can view the permission applications that you submit. View permission applications on the **Processed by Me** tab If you are a workspace administrator, you can view the permission applications that you have processed for all objects such as tables, resources, and functions in the workspace on the **Processed by Me** tab.

**Manually refresh table metadata**

If a table exists but cannot be found in Data Map, or a table is updated but the updated table is not displayed in Data Map, you need to manually refresh the table metadata. In the upper-right corner of the search result page, click **Refresh Table Metadata**. On the Data Map page, go to the **My Data > My Tools > Refresh Table Metadata** tab, select a data type for the **Data Type** parameter, enter a table in the **Guid** field, and click
**Refresh**.
After you perform the preceding operations, you can enter a keyword to search for the desired table again on the Search page in Data Map.

#### Metadata collection

DataWorks Data Map provides the **metadata collection** feature that allows you to collect metadata from various data sources to Data Map, manage the collected metadata in a centralized manner, and view the collected metadata by data source in Data Map. This topic describes how to create a crawler to collect metadata from each data source to DataWorks.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Resource Group Name | Select the resource group that is connected to the data source whose metadata you want to collect. You can select the default resource group or your exclusive resource group for scheduling. |

After you add a data source to a workspace, DataWorks can collect metadata from the data source. After you enable the metadata collection feature in Data Map, DataWorks collects full existing metadata at a time, collects incremental metadata every day, and then aggregates the full and incremental metadata to Data Map. Then, you can perform various operations on the metadata in Data Map. For example, you can check the overview of data, manage tables by category and group, and view data lineages. DataWorks can collect metadata from the following types of data sources: Hologres, CDH Hive, CDH HBase, AnalyticDB for MySQL V2.0, AnalyticDB for MySQL V3.0, AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, Tablestore, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and Oracle.

**Note**

The metadata of MaxCompute data sources is automatically collected and no manual collection is required. To collect metadata from a PolarDB for MySQL data source, you need to select MySQL as the type of data source. To collect metadata from a PolarDB for PostgreSQL data source, you need to select PostgreSQL as the type of the data source. The required data sources are created.

**Procedure**

This topic uses a Hologres data source as an example to describe how to collect metadata. The method for collecting metadata from other data sources is similar to this approach.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
3. In the left-side navigation pane of the page that appears, click **Collect Metadata**.
4. In the **Data Source Perspective** section, click **Hologres**. The **Hologres Metadata**
**Collection** page appears.
5. On the **Data Sources for Which No Crawler Is Created** tab, select a workspace from
the **Workspace** drop-down list and enter a name in the **Data Source Name** field.
6. In the data source list, find the data source for which you want to create a crawler and click
**Create Crawler** in the **Actions** column. In the Configure Collection Plan dialog box,
configure the parameters and click **Confirmation**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Test Network Connectivity | Click Test Network Connectivity to check the network connectivity. If the message The connectivity test failed appears, check whether you have configured a valid data source. |
|---|---|
| Collection Plan | The metadata collection plan. Valid values: Manual Crawling, Monthly, Weekly, Daily, and Hourly. The collection plan that is generated varies based on the collection cycle. The system collects metadata from the data source based on the collection cycle that you specify. Manual Crawling: You can manually trigger the crawler to collect metadata from the data source to Data Map and update the collected metadata based on your business requirements. Monthly: The system automatically collects metadata from the data source once at a specified point in time on several specific days of each month. Important Specific months do not have the 29th, 30th, or 31st day. We recommend that you do not select the last few days of a month. Weekly: The system automatically collects metadata from the data source once at a specified point in time on several specific days of each week. If you do not configure the Time parameter, the system automatically collects metadata from the data source once at 00:00:00 on the specific days of each week. Daily: The system automatically collects metadata from the data source once at a specified point in time of each day. Hourly: The system automatically collects metadata from the data source once on the Nth minute of each hour. |

7. Run the collection plan.
Click the **Data Sources for Which Crawler Is Created** tab to view the created collection plans. Find the data source on which you want to run the collection plan, and click **Run** in the **Actions** column. If the operation is successful, the message `The running of the` `crawler is triggered` appears.

**Related operations**

You can also perform the following operations on the data sources for which crawlers are created:
**Edit**: Find the data source that you want to manage and click Edit in the Actions column to
reconfigure the collection plan.
**Remove**: If you no longer need to collect metadata from a data source, find the data
source and click **Remove** in the Actions column. If you remove the crawler, features on the pages such as the table search page, table details page, table statistics page, and table lineage page become unavailable for all tables of the selected data sources whose metadata is collected by using the crawler. Proceed with caution.
**Stop**: Stop the crawler. After you click **Run**, the **Stop** button appears. You can click Stop to
stop the collection plan for a data source. icon in the upper-right corner of the data source list page to customize the columns of the list. Batch operations: You can click **Batch Remove Crawler** and **Batch Test Network**
**Connectivity** to remove multiple data sources and test the network connectivity.

#### Configuration management

This topic describes how to manage the categories and visibility of MaxCompute tables in the workspaces that you manage or own on the Configuration Management page in Data Map.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Data Map(Data Management)**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane of the Data Map page, click **Manage Configurations**.
The **Manage Configurations** module consists of three sub-modules: **Manage**
**Categories**, **Manage Workspaces**, and **Other Settings**.

**Manage categories**

You can use the category management feature to organize and manage tables by category in an efficient manner. After you configure the categories of your MaxCompute tables, you can search for tables by category. The feature also allows you to add specific tables to My Favorites for quick queries. After you configure the categories of MaxCompute tables, all members of the DataWorks workspaces that reside in the current region can search for tables by category.
1. In the left-side navigation pane of the Data Map page, choose **Manage Configurations >**
**Manage Categories**.
2. Create a category.
In the **Manage Categories** section, click the icon next to Categories to create a category.

**Note**

Up to six levels of categories can be created. After a category is created, you can click , , and to add a subcategory to the category, modify the category name, and delete the category, respectively.
3. Manage tables in the category.
You can click **Add Tables** in the upper-right corner of the page to add a table to the current category as prompted. The added table is displayed on the right side of the page. You can also remove the added table from the current category based on your business requirements. Add one or more tables to a category: a. Select a category and click **Quick Add** in the upper-right corner. b. In the **Quick Add** panel, configure the **Data Type** and **Project** parameters, enter a table name or keyword, and then click the icon to search for the tables that you want to add. c. If you want to add a table to the category, find the table that you want to add and click
**Add** in the Actions column.
If you want to add multiple tables to the category at a time, select the tables and click
**Batch Add**.
Remove one or more tables from a category: a. If you want to remove a table from the category, find the table that you want to remove and click **Remove from Category** in the Actions column. #### FAQ: New table not found in data map

In DataWorks, you can search for tables in the data map by entering a keyword on its home page. The data map also displays your recently viewed and accessed tables. Sometimes, a newly created table might not appear in search results because of a delay in metadata synchronization. This topic explains how to resolve this issue. When you search for a table using a keyword on the **Home** page of the data map, the message `No content related to the table is found` is displayed.

**Possible causes**

Possible causes include: You entered an incorrect keyword. The table is new, and its metadata has not yet been synchronized with the data map.

| Module |  | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Quality dashboard |  | The Quality Dashboard page displays an overview of data quality in the current workspace, including the main data quality metrics, the trend and distribution of rule-based check instances, the top N tables that have the maximum number of data quality issues, the owners of the issues, and the coverage status of monitoring rules. This helps data quality owners understand the overall data quality condition of the current workspace and handle data quality issues at the earliest opportunity to improve data quality. |
| Quality Assets | Rules | On this page, you can view all configured monitoring rules. |
|  | Rule Template Library | On this page, you can manage a set of custom rule templates and use the rule templates to improve the efficiency of rule configuration. |
| Configure Rules | Configure by Table | Data Quality allows you to configure a monitoring rule for a single table or for multiple tables based on a rule template. |
|  | Configure by Template |  |

1. Check the keyword.
Ensure the keyword is correct.
2. Manually synchronize the table.
If the keyword is correct, the new table's metadata may not be synchronized yet. To resolve this, manually synchronize the table. In the data map, on the **My Data > Refresh Metadata** page, enter the table GUID in the format `ProjectName.TableName` and click **Refresh**. You can then search for the table again in **All Data**.

### Data Quality

#### Offline data monitoring

You can enable offline data monitoring to periodically check the health of data stored in common big data storage services, such as MaxCompute, Hologres, AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, and AnalyticDB for MySQL. This way, you can detect data quality issues that are caused by errors in the extract, transform, load (ETL) logic or source changes in a timely manner. This prevents the accumulation of errors from affecting the accuracy of reports. This feature not only improves O&M efficiency, but also significantly reduces repair costs and resource waste. The following table describes the modules of Data Quality.

| Quality O&M | Monitor | On this page, you can view all monitors created in the current workspace. |
|---|---|---|
|  | Running Records | On this page, you can view the check results of monitors. After a monitor is run, you can view the details of the monitor on this page. |
| Quality Analysis | Quality Reports | Data Quality allows you to create report templates and add metrics for rule configuration and running based on your business requirements. Reports are generated and sent on a regular basis based on the configured statistical period, sending time, and subscription details. |

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Data Quality**.
3. In the upper part of the page that appears, **Streaming Data Monitoring** is displayed. You
are on the **Stream Data Monitoring** page.

**Note**

The system allows you to switch between the streaming and offline monitoring modes. You can click **Streaming Data Monitoring** or **Offline Data Monitoring** to switch between different monitoring modes.

##### View the quality dashboard

The Quality Dashboard page displays an overview of data quality in the current workspace, including the main data quality metrics, the trend and distribution of rule-based check instances, the top N tables that have the maximum number of data quality issues, the owners of the issues, and the coverage status of monitoring rules. This helps data quality owners understand the overall data quality condition of the current workspace and handle data quality issues at the earliest opportunity to improve data quality.

**Data Quality**.

The Quality Monitoring Overview section displays the trend and distribution of rule-based check instances.

**Instance Trend Analysis**

Displays the trend of the number of rule-based check instances that have different check results. You can click **By Day** or **By Hour** to view the trend from the selected perspective. You can select **All**, **Strong rules**, or **Weak rules** to view the trend of the number of rulebased check instances that have check results of all types of monitoring rules, check results of only strong monitoring rules, and check results of only weak monitoring rules.

**Running status**

Displays the distribution of rule-based check instances with different check results. You can view the number of rule-based check instances that are run on the current day. You can select **All**, **Strong rules**, or **Weak rules** to view the distribution of rule-based check instances with check results of all types of monitoring rules, check results of only strong monitoring rules, and check results of only weak monitoring rules. Rule-based check results:
**Pass**: The rule-based check is successful, and the table passed the quality threshold check.
**Strong Rule-based Check Instances for Which Critical Threshold Is Exceeded** : The
critical threshold check of a strong monitoring rule failed.
**Strong Rule-based Check Instances for Which Warning Threshold Is Exceeded** :
The warning threshold check of a strong monitoring rule failed.
**Weak Rule-based Check Instances for Which Critical Threshold Is Exceeded** : The
critical threshold check of a weak monitoring rule failed.
**Weak Rule-based Check Instances for Which Warning Threshold Is Exceeded** : The
warning threshold check of a weak monitoring rule failed.
**Check Failed**: The rule-based check failed to be executed, and the system failed to obtain
the check value.

**Top N quality issues**

Based on the ranking of the numbers of monitoring rules for tables, the Top N Tables with Maximum Number of Quality Issues section displays the statistics on the **top N tables** sorted based on the number of data quality issues within the specified time range, and the Owners of Top N Tables with Maximum Number of Quality Issues section displays the **owners of the**
**issues**. You can click View more in the upper-right corner to go to the Running Records page.
On this page, you can view the historical checks and check details and resolve data quality issues at the earliest opportunity.

**Note**

The owner of a monitoring rule is the data quality owner of a data table partition. In most cases, the owner is the user who creates a partition filter expression. The Quality Configuration Analysis section displays the overall coverage of monitoring rules from the following dimensions: **Asset Ratio** - **Tables for Which Rules Are Configured** ,
**Number of Tables** - **No Rules Are Configured**, **Number of Tables** - **No Rules Are**
**Enabled**, **Number of Tables** - **Configured with Rules with Which No Scheduling Node**
**Is Associated**, and **Number of Tables** - **Configured with Rules for Which No Alert**
**Recipient Is Configured**. You can also click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of a table
to view the rule configuration details of the table from this dimension. Description of each dimension:
**No Rules Are Configured**: Tables for which no monitoring rule is configured are included
in statistics.

**Note**

This dimension is supported only for MaxCompute data sources.
**No Rules Are Enabled**: Tables for which no monitoring rule is enabled are included in
statistics.
**Configured with Rules with Which No Scheduling Node Is Associated** : Tables
configured with rules with which no scheduling node is associated are included in statistics. If no scheduling node is associated with a monitoring rule, the monitoring rule can be executed only in a test run.
**Configured with Rules for Which No Alert Recipient Is Configured** : Tables
configured with rules for which no alert recipient is configured are included in statistics. If no alert recipient is configured for a monitoring rule, no one can receive the check result in a timely manner if data quality issues occur during the rule execution.

##### Configure monitoring rules

###### Configure a monitoring rule for a single

**table**

Data Quality allows you to configure monitoring rules for a single table to monitor whether the quality of table data meets specific conditions. If data quality issues are detected, nodes on which the issues occur are blocked to prevent dirty data from spreading downstream. This ensures that the generated table data meets your business requirements. This topic describes how to configure monitoring rules for a single table, run a monitor, and perform other related operations. The metadata of a compute engine is collected. Monitoring rules are configured for the data tables of a compute engine and are used to monitor the data quality of the tables. Therefore, before you create and configure monitoring rules, you must collect the metadata of the desired compute engine first. For more information, see **Data map > Data discovery**.

**Procedure**

You need to perform the following steps to configure monitoring rules for a table:
1. Select the table whose data quality you want to check based on monitoring rules.
2. **Create a monitor for the table** .
When you create and configure a monitor for the table, you can specify **the range of**
**table data whose quality you want to monitor**, such as a partition, and select the
monitoring rules that you want to associate with the monitor. This way, the monitor can be used to monitor the quality of the specified table data based on the rules. You can create different monitors for different partitions of the same table and associate different monitoring rules with the monitors. This way, the partitions can be monitored based on different data quality check logic. You can specify a trigger method for the monitor. The monitor can be triggered when the scheduling node that generates the table is run or when you manually run the monitor. You can specify the conditions under which alerts are sent. You can determine whether to send alerts based on the severity of data quality check results. You can determine whether to block the task that generates the monitored table based on the severity of data quality issues when data changes in the table are automatically checked.
3. Associate monitoring rules with the monitor.
You can select the monitoring rules based on which you want to monitor the data quality of the **table**. The specific check methods that are defined in the rules are implemented to determine whether the table data meets your business requirements. Data Quality allows you to create monitoring rules based on built-in rule templates or create custom template rules based on custom SQL statement logic. In the preceding format: Built-in template rules: You can create monitoring rules based on built-in rule templates provided by DataWorks. Custom template rules: You can create custom template rules if the built-in rule templates cannot meet your requirements for monitoring the quality of data specified by partition filter expressions. You can save frequently used custom rules as rule templates for future use.
4. Test and subscribe to the monitor.

**Limits**

You can configure monitoring rules only for specific types of data sources, including MaxComput, Hologres, AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, and AnalyticDB for MySQL. After you configure a monitoring rule for a data source, the rule can be triggered to check the data quality of tables in the data source only if the scheduling node that generates the table data runs in a resource group that is connected to the data source.

| Section | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
|  | Monitor Name | The name of the monitor. |
|  | Monitored Object | The object for which you want to check the data quality. The default value is the current table. |

To perform data quality checks by using a dynamic threshold rule, you must make sure that sampling records of at least 21 days are available. Otherwise, exceptions may occur when you use a dynamic threshold rule. If no sampling records of 21 days are available when you configure a dynamic threshold rule, you can use the data backfill feature to supplement the required data after you associate the rule with scheduling nodes.

2. Create a monitoring rule.
You can use one of the following methods provided by Data Quality to configure monitoring rules based on your business requirements.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Rule Name | The name of the monitoring rule. |
| Template | The template used to create the monitoring rule. Data Quality provides a large number of built-in table-level and field-level rule templates that are ready for use. Note You can configure field-level monitoring rules of the following types only for numeric fields: average value, sum of values, minimum value, and maximum value. |
| Rule Scope | The application scope of the rule. For a table-level monitoring rule, the application scope is the current table by default. For a field-level monitoring rule, the application scope is a specific field. |

**Method 1: Configure a rule based on a built-in rule template**

Data Quality provides dozens of built-in rule templates. You can quickly create a monitoring rule based on a built-in rule template.

**Note**

In the upper part of the Create Rule panel, you can click **+ System Template**
**Rules**. Then, you can configure the **template** parameter to select the desired
rule template. Alternatively, you can find the desired built-in rule template in the left-side navigation pane of the **Create Rule** panel and click **+ Use**. You can add multiple rules at the same time.

| Comparison Method | The comparison method that is used by the rule to check whether the table data is as expected. Manual Settings: You can configure the comparison method to compare the data output result with the expected result based on your business requirements. You can select different comparison methods for different rule templates. You can view the comparison methods that are supported by a rule template in the DataWorks console. Numeric results: You can compare a numeric result with a fixed value, which is the expected value. The following comparison methods are supported: greater than, greater than or equal to, equal to, not equal to, less than, and less than or equal to. You can configure the normal data range (normal threshold) and abnormal data range (critical threshold) based on your business requirements. Fluctuation results: You can compare a fluctuation result with a fluctuation range. The following comparison methods are supported: absolute value, rise, and drop. You can configure the normal data range (normal threshold) based on your business requirements. You can also define data output exceptions (warning threshold) and unexpected data outputs (critical threshold) based on the degree of abnormal deviation. Intelligent Dynamic Threshold: If you select this option, you do not need to manually configure the fluctuation threshold or expected value. The system automatically determines the reasonable threshold based on intelligent algorithms. If abnormal data is detected, an alert is immediately triggered or the related task is immediately blocked. When the Comparison Method parameter is set to Intelligent Dynamic Threshold, you can configure the Degree of importance parameter. Note Only monitoring rules that you configure based on ac ustom SQL statement, a custom range, or a dynamic threshold support the intelligent dynamic threshold comparison method. |
|---|---|

| Monitoring Threshold | If you set the Comparison Method parameter to Manual Settings, you can configure the Normal threshold and Red Threshold parameters. Normal threshold: If the data quality check result meets the specified condition, the data output is as expected. Red Threshold: If the data quality check result meets the specified condition, the data output is not as expected. If the rule that you configure is a rule of thef luctuation type, you must configure the warning threshold. Warning Threshold: If the data quality check result meets the specified condition, the data is abnormal but your business is not affected. |
|---|---|
| Retain problem data | If the monitoring rule is enabled and a data quality check based on the rule fails, the system automatically creates a table to store the problematic data that is identified during the data quality check. Important The Retain problem data parameter is available only for MaxCompute tables. The Retain problem data parameter is available only for specific monitoring rules in Data Quality. For more information, see Appendix 3: Monitoring rules that support the problem data retention feature and specifications for problem data. If you turn off Status for the monitoring rule, problematic data is not stored. |
| Status | Specifies whether to enable the rule in the production environment. Important If you turn off the switch for the rule, the rule cannot be triggered to perform a test run or triggered by the associated scheduling nodes. |
| Degree of importance | The strength of the rule in your business. Strong rules are important rules. If you set the parameter to Strong rules and the critical threshold is exceeded, the scheduling node that you associate with the monitor is blocked by default. Weak rules are regular rules. If you set the parameter to Weak rules and the critical threshold is exceeded, the scheduling node that you associate with the monitor is not blocked by default. |
| Configuratio n Source | The configuration source of the rule. Default value: Data Quality. |
| Description | You can add additional descriptions to the rule. |

**Method 2: Configure a rule based on a custom rule template**

| Paramet er | Description |
|---|---|
| FLAG paramet er | The SET statement that you want to execute before the SQL statement in the rule is executed. |
| SQL | The SQL statement that determines the complete check logic. The returned results must be numeric and consist of one row and one column. In the custom SQL statement, enclose the partition filter expression in brackets []. Example: SELECT count(*) FROM ${tableName} WHERE ds=$[yyyymmdd]; Note In this statement, the value of the ${tableName} variable is dynamically replaced with the name of the table for which you are configuring monitoring rules. For information about how to configure a partition filter expression, see the Appendix 2: Built-in partition filter expressions section in this topic. If you have created a monitor for the table, the setting of the table partition that you specify in the Data Range parameter during the monitor configuration no longer takes effect for the table after you configure this parameter. The rule determines the table partition to be checked based on the setting of WHERE in the SQL statement. |

**Note**

Before you use this method to create a rule, you must choose **Quality Assets >**
**Rule Template Library** in the left-side navigation pane to create a custom rule
template. When you reference a custom rule template, the basic configurations of the template, such as **FLAG parameter** and **SQL**, are automatically displayed. You can configure the
**Rule Name** parameter based on your business requirements, and the Monitoring
Threshold parameter based on the rule type. Only the parameters that are unique to rules created based on custom rule templates are described in the following table. For information about other parameters, see the parameters for configuring a rule based on a built-in rule template.

**Method 3: Configure a rule based on a custom SQL statement**

This method allows you to configure the data quality check logic for the table based on your business requirements.

**Note**

The parameters for configuring monitoring rules based on a custom SQL statement are the same as those for configuring monitoring rules based on built-in rule templates and custom rule templates.
3. Optional. Add the configured rule to a monitor.

**Note**

The configured monitoring rule can be triggered only if you add the rule to a monitor. To associate a rule with a monitor, you can select Add to Monitor in the lower part of the Create Rule panel and select the desired monitor. Alternatively, when you configure a monitor, you can associate an existing rule with the monitor in the **Monitoring Rule** section of the Create Monitor page. You can select **Add Me as an Alert Recipient of the Monitor** to receive notifications in real time when alerts are triggered.
4. Click **Determine**.

**Appendix 1: Calculation formulas of the fluctuation rate and**

**variance**

Calculation formula of the fluctuation rate: `Fluctuation rate = (Sample value - Baseline`

```
value)/Baseline value
```

**Sample value**: The sample value for the current day. For example, if you want to check
the fluctuation in the number of table rows on an SQL task within a day, the sample value is the number of table rows in partitions on that day.
**Baseline value**: The comparison value collected from the previous N days.

**Note**

previous day. Calculation formula of the variance: `(Current sample value - Average value of previous N`

```
days)/Standard deviation
```

**Note**

You can calculate the fluctuation variance only for numeric fields such as **BIGINT** and
**DOUBLE** fields by using the preceding formula.

**Appendix 2: Built-in partition filter expressions**

$[yyyymmdd-1] The partitions are daily partitions. The partition data matching the data timestamp needs to be checked. $[yyyymmdd-1]/hour=$[hh24] The partitions are level-2 partitions. All the level-2 partitions on the scheduling day need to be checked.

| Check type | Check rule | Rule description | Problem data specification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniqu e value | Unique value, fixed value | Data Quality compares the number of unique values of a field after deduplication with a fixed value. | If the check is not passed: If all values of the field are unique, the system generates a problem data table but stores no problem data in the table. If some values of the field are not unique, the system generates a problem data table and stores the duplicate data of the field in the table. In this case, the duplicate data is the problem data. |
|  | Number of unique values/Total number of rows | Data Quality compares the ratio of the number of unique values of a field to the total number of rows with a fixed value. |  |

$[yyyymmdd] The partitions are daily partitions. The partition data on the scheduling day needs to be checked. $[yyyymmddhh24miss] Partitions contain the 24-hour time format information, such as 20211216174847. The partition data at a specific point in time on the day that is specified by bizdate needs to be checked. $[yyyymmddhh24miss-1/24] Partitions contain the 24-hour time format information, such as 20211216174847. The partition data at 1 hour earlier than a specific point in time on the day that is specified by bizdate needs to be checked. $[yyyymmdd]000000 The partitions are partitions at 00:00 each day, such as 20211216000000. The partition data at 00:00 on the day that is specified by bizdate needs to be checked. $[yyyymmdd-7] The partitions are daily partitions, such as 20211216. The partitions that are seven days earlier than the scheduling day need to be checked. $[hh24miss-1/24] The partitions are hourly partitions, such as 180000. The partitions that are 1 hour earlier than the scheduling time need to be checked. $[hh24miss-30/24/60] The partitions are hourly partitions, such as 180000. The partitions that are 30 minutes earlier than the scheduling time need to be checked. $[add_months(yyyymmdd,-1)] The partitions are daily partitions, such as 20211208. The partitions that are one month earlier than the scheduling day need to be checked.

**Appendix 3: Monitoring rules that support the problem data**

**retention feature and specifications for problem data**

System templates

| Null value | Number of null values, fixed value | Data Quality compares the number of null values of a field with a fixed value. Note The IS NULL expression is used in the SQL statements to check whether a value of a field is a null value. | The system generates a problem data table and stores null values of the field in the table. In this case, all null values are problem data. |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | Number of null values/Total number of rows, fixed value | Data Quality compares the ratio of the number of null values of a field to the total number of rows with a fixed value. Note The fixed value is a decimal. |  |
| Duplic ate value | Number of duplicate values/Total number of rows, fixed value | Data Quality compares the ratio of the number of duplicated values of a field to the total number of rows with a fixed value. | The system generates a problem data table and stores duplicate values of the field in the table. In this case, all duplicate values are problem data. |
|  | Number of duplicate values, fixed value | Data Quality subtracts the number of values of a field after deduplication from the total number of rows to obtain the number of duplicate values of the field. Then, Data Quality compares the number of duplicated values with a fixed value. |  |

After you turn on **Retain problem data**, problem data is saved after the monitoring rule that is created based on the custom SQL statement is executed and an alert is generated.

###### Configure a monitoring rule for multiple

**tables based on a template**

Data Quality provides a variety of built-in table-level and field-level monitoring rule templates. This topic describes how to configure a monitoring rule based on a template.

**Limits**

You can configure monitoring rules based on templates for MaxCompute, Hologres, AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, and AnalyticDB for MySQL data sources.

**Procedure**

You can perform the following steps to configure a monitoring rule based on a template:
1. Select a rule template and configure the rule parameters
Built-in rule templates are classified into table-level and field-level rule templates. After you select a template, you can configure a rule based on the template to check the data quality of a **table**. You can use the monitoring rule to determine whether the table data is as expected.
2. Add multiple tables or fields whose data quality needs to be checked by the rule at the
same time You can select tables or fields whose data quality needs to be checked and apply the rule to the tables or fields.
3. Associate the rule with a new monitor or an existing monitor
You can associate the rule with a new monitor or an existing monitor to specify **the range**
**of data whose quality you want to monitor** based on the rule. If you want to monitor
the data quality of a partitioned table, the data range is a partition.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Data Quality**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Configure Rules > Configure by Template**.
Data Quality provides built-in **table-level** rule templates and **field-level** rule templates. You can find the desired template and click **Configure Monitoring Rules** to the right of the template to configure a monitoring rule based on the template for multiple tables or fields at the same time.

**Step 2: Configure the attributes of the monitoring rule**

1. On the Configure by Template page, find the template that you want to use and click
**Configure Monitoring Rules** in the Actions column to go to the **Batch Add Monitoring**
**Rules** wizard.
2. Configure the **basic attributes** of the monitoring rule.

| Data Source Type | The type of the data source of tables for which you want to configure the monitoring rule. |
|---|---|
| Rule Source | The value is fixed to Built-in Template and the rule template that you selected. You cannot modify the rule template. |
| Templat e |  |
| Rule Name | The naming format of the monitoring rule. The name of the monitoring rule is automatically generated. You can change the suffix in the naming format based on your business requirements. |
| Descripti on | The description of the monitoring rule. |

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Degree of importan ce | The strength of the rule in your business. Strong rules are important rules. If you set the parameter to Strong and the critical threshold is exceeded, the scheduling node that you associate with the monitor is blocked by default. Weak rules are regular rules. If you set the parameter to Soft and the critical threshold is exceeded, the scheduling node that you associate with the monitor is not blocked by default. |

3. Configure the advanced attributes of the monitoring rule.

| Comparis on Method | The comparison method that is used by the rule to check whether the table data is as expected. Manual Settings: You can configure the comparison method to compare the data output result with the expected result based on your business requirements. You can select different comparison methods for different rule templates. You can view the comparison methods that are supported by a rule template in the DataWorks console. Numeric results: You can compare a numeric result with a fixed value, which is the expected value. The following comparison methods are supported: greater than, greater than or equal to, equal to, not equal to, less than, and less than or equal to. You can configure the normal data range (normal threshold) and abnormal data range (critical threshold) based on your business requirements. Fluctuation results: You can compare a fluctuation result with a fluctuation range. The following comparison methods are supported: absolute value, rise, and drop. You can configure the normal data range (normal threshold) based on your business requirements. You can also define data output exceptions (warning threshold) and unexpected data outputs (critical threshold) based on the degree of abnormal deviation. Intelligent Dynamic Threshold: If you select this option, you do not need to manually configure the fluctuation threshold or expected value. The system automatically determines the reasonable threshold based on intelligent algorithms. If abnormal data is detected, an alert is immediately triggered or the related task is immediately blocked. When the Comparison Method parameter is set to Intelligent Dynamic Threshold, you can configure the Degree of importance parameter. Note Only monitoring rules that you configure based on ac ustom SQL statement, a custom range, or a dynamic threshold support the intelligent dynamic threshold comparison method. |
|---|---|
| Monitorin g Threshold | If you set the Comparison Method parameter to Manual Settings, you can configure the Normal threshold and Red Threshold parameters. Normal threshold: If the data quality check result meets the specified condition, the data output is as expected. Red Threshold: If the data quality check result meets the specified condition, the data output is not as expected. If the rule that you configure is a rule of thef luctuation type, you must configure the warning threshold. Warning Threshold: If the data quality check result meets the specified condition, the data is abnormal but your business is not affected. |
| Status | Specifies whether to enable the rule in the production environment. Important If you turn off the switch for the rule, the rule cannot be triggered to perform a test run or triggered by the associated scheduling nodes. |

4. Click **Next** to go to the **Generate Monitoring Rule** step.

**Step 3: Add multiple tables or fields whose data quality needs**

**to be checked by the rule at the same time**

You can add multiple tables or fields whose data quality needs to be checked based on the selected **table-level** or **field-level rule template**. Add tables i. Click **Add Table**. In the **Batch Create** panel, select the tables for which you want to configure a monitoring rule.

**Note**

All tables of the **data source type** specified in the **basic attributes** are displayed in the panel. You can also enter a **keyword** to search for the desired tables. ii. Select the tables for which you want to configure the monitoring rule and click **Confirm** to add them to the **Tables for Which You Want to Configure Rules** list. Add fields i. Click **Add Fields**. In the **Select a field** dialog box, select the table that contains the fields for which you want to configure the monitoring rule.

**Note**

In the **Tables to Be Selected** section, all tables of the **data source type** specified in the **basic attributes** are displayed. ii. After you select tables, the **Select Fields** section displays all fields in the selected tables. You can filter the fields by **field name** or **field description**. iii. Select the fields for which you want to configure a monitoring rule and click **Create** to add the fields to the **Fields for Which You Want to Configure Rules** list.

**Step 4: Associate the rule with a new monitor or an existing**

You can associate the rule with a new monitor or an existing monitor to specify the range of data whose quality you want to monitor based on the rule. If you want to monitor the data quality of a partitioned table, the data range is a partition. You can configure a monitor for each table or field or configure a monitor for multiple tables or fields at the same time. i. Associate the monitoring rule with a monitor. To associate the rule with a monitor, find the desired table or field, click the drop-down list in the **Monitor** column, and then select an existing monitor. ii. If no monitor is available, select **Create Monitor** from the drop-down list to create a monitor and associate the rule with the created monitor. For more information about the parameters, see Configure a monitoring rule for a single table. After the monitor is created, return to the Generate Monitoring Rule step and select the monitor from the drop-down list in the **Monitor** column. Configure a monitor for multiple tables or fields at the same time i. Select multiple tables or fields and click **Configure Monitor**. ii. Select **Automatically Associate**, **Disassociate**, or **Batch Add** from the Configure Monitor drop-down list.

| Parameter |  | Description |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data Range | Partitioned Table | The range of table data whose quality you want to monitor. You can use a partition filter expression to define the partition that needs to be checked. Non-partitioned Table: The default value is Full Table. You can specify the range based on the WHERE clause. For a partitioned table, you must set this parameter to a value in the Partition key=Partition value format. The partition value can be a constant or a built-in partition filter expression. |  |  |
|  |  |  | Partition |  |
| Running Settings | Trigger Method | The mode to trigger quality monitoring. Triggered by Node Scheduling in Production Environment: After the scheduling node that you associate with the monitor finishes running in Operation Center, the rules that are associated with the monitor are automatically triggered. Note that dry-run nodes do not trigger monitoring rules to run. Triggered Manually: The monitoring rules that are associated with the monitor are manually triggered. |  |  |
|  | Associated Scheduling Node | If you set the Trigger Method parameter to Triggered by Node Scheduling in Production Environment, you must configure this parameter to select the scheduling nodes that you want to associate with the monitor. After the scheduling nodes finish running, the rules that are associated with the monitor are automatically triggered. |  |  |
|  | Running Resources | The resources that are required to run the rules. By default, the data source to which the monitored table in the current workspace belongs is selected. If you select another data source, make sure that the related resources can access the monitored table. |  |  |

|  | key=Partition value |
|---|---|

**Automatically Associate**: The selected tables or fields are automatically associated
with an existing monitor.
**Disassociate**: The selected tables or fields are disassociated from a monitor.
**Batch Add**: You can create monitors for the selected rules.
iii. Optional. Select **Subscribe to Alerts (By Email)** . iv. Click **OK**.

**Step 5: Test the rule**

1. Click **Generate Monitoring Rule** to go to the **Verify Monitoring Rule** step. On the
**Verify Monitoring Rule** page, you can perform the following operations:
**Test Run**: verifies the validity of the rule configurations.
After the rules of the selected tables are created, you can select one or more rules to perform a **test run**. In the **Test Run** dialog box, configure the **Resource Group** parameter and **Scheduling time** parameter, which specifies the simulated triggering time of the rule. The system calculates the value of a partition key in a partitioned table that you want to monitor based on the specified simulated triggering time and the value of the **Data Range** parameter configured when you associate the rule with a monitor. Click **Test Run** to check whether the data in the partition of the table complies with the configured monitoring rule. After the test run is completed, you can click **Running records** in the Actions column of the rule to view the details of the test run and perform related operations.
**Subscriptions**: defines the alert recipients.
Supported notification methods: **Email**, **Email and SMS**, **DingTalk Chatbot**, **DingTalk**
**Chatbot @ ALL**, and **Custom Webhook**.
**Associated Scheduling**: defines the mode to trigger the rule.
You can click **Use Recommended Running Mode** or **Manually Specify Running**
**Mode** to associate one or more monitoring rules with the auto triggered nodes that
generate table data. In Operation Center, auto triggered nodes generate the table data after the auto triggered node instances, data backfill instances, or test instances generated for the auto triggered nodes are successfully run. When the auto triggered nodes start to run, the monitoring rules are triggered. You can specify the strength of a rule to control whether to block the running of the descendant nodes of an associated auto triggered node. This helps reduce the impact of dirty data records. Use Recommended Running Mode: The system associates the selected monitoring rules with auto triggered nodes based on the lineages of the auto triggered nodes that generate the table data. Manually Specify Running Mode: You can manually associate the selected monitoring rule with specific auto triggered nodes.

**Important**

A monitoring rule can be triggered only when the rule is associated with related auto triggered nodes.
**Delete**: You can select one or more rules that you want to delete.
**View Rule Details**: You can click **View Rule Details** in the Actions column of a rule to
view the rule details. On the page that appears, you can perform the following operations: modify, start, stop, and delete the rule, specify the rule strength, and view logs.
2. After the test on the monitoring rule is completed and the monitoring rule is associated with
auto triggered nodes, click **Complete Check**.

**What to do next**

After the monitor is run, you can choose **Quality O&M** > **Monitor** in the left-side navigation pane of the Data Quality page to view the quality check status of the specified table and choose Quality O&M > **Running Records** to view the complete check records of the rule.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Data Timestamp | The date that corresponds to the data timestamp of the partition for which the noise reduction rule takes effect. After the noise reduction rule is enabled, the related node is not blocked if the data in this partition fails to meet your expectations. |
| Rule Type | The type of the monitoring rule for which the noise reduction rule takes effect. You can select one or more rule types from the drop-down list. |

###### Configure a noise reduction rule

If abnormal data is detected on a scheduling node in a workspace by monitoring rules associated with a monitor, and you do not want such data to trigger alerts, you can create noise reduction rules. This way, alerts are not sent and the node is not blocked. This indicates that the node does not fail to run or exit because the node fails the check of the monitoring rules. Monitoring rules are created in Data Quality. For more information, see Configure a monitoring rule for a single table or Configure a monitoring rule for multiple tables based on a template.

**Limits**

Only workspace administrators can create and manage noise reduction rules. A noise reduction rule takes effect only for the monitoring rules that you specify in the noise reduction rule in the current workspace.

**Create a noise reduction rule**

1. Go to the Dashboard page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quality O&M > Monitor**. In the upper-right
corner of the page, click **Noise**.
3. Click **Create Denoise Rule** in the upper-right corner.
4. In the **Create Denoise Rule** panel, click **Add Denoise Rule** and configure the following
parameters.

| Expected Value | You can use the data in the partition as the sample data or baseline data to denoise data based on the specified types of monitoring rules in the workspace. Valid values: Denoise Sample: The related node is not blocked if the sample data in the specified partition is detected as abnormal based on monitoring rules. In other words, if the data in the specified partition does not meet your expectations, the related node is still run as expected. Denoise Baseline: The related node that is run after the specified date is not blocked if the data in the specified partition is used as the baseline data and does not meet your expectations. In other words, the related node is still run as expected. Note Denoise Sample The sample value for the current day. For example, if you want to check the fluctuation in the number of table rows on an SQL node within a day, the sample value is the number of table rows in partitions on that day. Denoise Baseline The comparison value collected from the previous N days. Examples: If you want to check the fluctuation in the number of table rows on an SQL task within a day, the baseline value is the number of table rows in partitions on the previous day. If you want to check the average fluctuation in the number of table rows on an SQL task within seven days, the baseline value is the average number of table rows in the last seven days. |
|---|---|
| Enable | Specifies whether to enable the noise reduction rule. After this rule is enabled, the related node is not blocked if data of the node fails the check of monitoring rules that are specified in the noise reduction rule. |

5. Click **Save**.

**Manage noise reduction rules**

On the **Noise Reduction Management** page, you can view the details of the created noise reduction rule and **modify** or **delete** the rule.

SELECT max(length(name)) FROM ${tableName}; Note In addition to length verification, custom SQL also supports type verification and range verification. To trigger an alert when the field length isl ess than a specified threshold: for example, set Normal threshold to >= 3 (where 3 is the specified threshold you have set; you can also set it to another value based on your business requirements). |
