##### Create and manage sample libraries

This topic describes how to create and manage sample libraries based on the sample files that you provide. You can associate a sample library with a data identification rule to identify data. If the data to be identified contains data in the sample library, the data identification rule is hit. You can use sample libraries to identify enumerated values, such as employee names and user addresses. This topic describes how to create and manage sample libraries.

**Limits**

You can upload only UTF-8 encoded files in the TXT format as sample files. The size of a sample file cannot exceed 500 KB. Each data entry in a sample file occupies a line.

**Note**

A data identification rule can be used to identify only one type of data. We recommend that you store the data of the same type in a sample library. To identify multiple types of data, you must configure multiple sample libraries. For example, if you want to identify employee names and home addresses, you must configure two sample libraries. One is used to identify employee names and the other is used to identify home addresses.

**Create a sample library**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products**
**> Data Governance > Data Protection**.
3. Click **Try now**. The homepage of the **Data Protection** module appears.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Rule Change > Data Recognition Rules**.
5. On the Data Recognition Rules page, click the **Sample Management** tab.
6. On the Sample Management tab, click **Add Sample**. In the dialog box that appears, specify
a name for the sample library and upload a sample file.

**Note**

You can upload multiple sample files to a sample library.
7. Click **Save**. The sample library is created.
After you create a sample library, you can associate the sample library with a data identification rule. If the data to be identified contains the data in the sample library, the data identification rule is hit. For more information, see Configure a data identification rule. On the **Sample Management** tab, you can perform the following operations to manage existing sample libraries. View the sample libraries. You can view the number of samples in and the data identification rules associated with each existing sample library. You can also view the details of a specific sample library by clicking the icon in the **Actions** column. Modify a sample library. Find the sample library that you want to modify and click the icon in the **Actions** column. You can upload a new sample file or replace an existing sample file. Delete a sample library. Find the sample library that you want to delete and click the icon in the **Actions** column.

**Note**

If the sample library is associated with a data identification rule, you cannot delete the sample library. You can view the data identification rule that is associated with the sample library on the Sample Management tab. Before you delete the sample library, you must disassociate the sample library from the data identification rule on the configuration page of the data identification rule. For more information, see Configure a data identification rule.

##### Configure a data identification rule

DataWorks allows you to identify sensitive data in your workspace by configuring sensitive data identification rules for built-in and custom sensitive field types. This topic describes how to create a sensitive field type and configure a sensitive data identification rule for this type.

**Background information**

DataWorks allows you to configure a sensitive data identification rule based on a specific sensitivity level and a specific category. This helps you identify sensitive data in your workspace. You can manually correct inaccurate identification results. The Data Recognition page displays statistics on the sensitive fields that hit sensitive data identification rules in each workspace in the previous week. The following figure shows how a sensitive data identification rule is configured and used.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the Data Recognition Rules tab
i. Log in to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Governance > Data Protection**.
iii. Click **Try now**. The homepage of the **Data Protection** module appears. iv. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Rule Change > Data Recognition Rules** to go to the **Data Recognition Rules** tab.
2. Configure sensitive field categories.
The first time that you use Data Security Guard, the default categories that are provided by the **built-in data sensitivity level template** are displayed on the left side of the Data Recognition Rules tab. You can search for a category by entering its name in the search box. You can also click the option to create a category or a subcategory, rename the category, or delete the category. If you have used Data Security Guard before, you can create categories in the left-side section on the Data Recognition Rules tab based on your business requirements.

**Note**

The name of a category must be unique. The name must be 1 to 30 characters in length, and can contain letters and digits. If you want to delete a category, make sure that all sensitive field types in this category are not published. Otherwise, the category cannot be deleted. For more information, see the Unpublish multiple sensitive field types at a time section of this topic.
3. Create a sensitive field type.
i. Select the category in which you want to create a sensitive field type. On the left side of the page, select the category in which you want to create a sensitive field type. ii. Create a sensitive field type and configure a data identification rule. Click **Sensitive field type** in the upper-right corner.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Sensitive field type | The name of the sensitive field type, such as name, ID number, and phone number. Note The name must be unique. If the specified name already exists, the Duplicate sensitive field type message appears below the Sensitive field type field. |
| Category | The category in which you want to create the sensitive field type. The default value is the category that you select in Step 1. If you want to change the category, select a category from the drop-down list. |
| Level | The sensitivity level of the sensitive field type. If the existing levels do not meet your business requirements, go to the Data classification and level page and configure sensitivity levels based on your business requirements. For more information, see Manage data sensitivity levels. |
| Description | The description of the sensitive field type. The description must be 0 to 100 characters in length and cannot contain special characters. |

a. In the **Set Basic Info** step, configure the parameters and click **Next**. b. In the **Rule Change** step, configure the rule hit conditions and test the accuracy of the rule. After the sensitive data identification rule is configured and the sensitive field type is published, you can use the rule to identify sensitive data in an identification task.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Identify the rule matching conditions | The rule hit mode. Valid values: Any one of the following conditions is met to hit the rule: The sensitive data identification rule is hit when the condition for sensitive content identification or sensitive field identification is met. The following conditions are met at the same time to hit the rule: The sensitive data identification rule is hit when both the conditions for sensitive content identification and sensitive field identification are met. Note The mode takes effect only for sensitive content identification and sensitive field identification. |
|---|---|
| Data content identification | The sensitive content identification settings. You can specify the content for matching sensitive data. Note Sensitive content identification identifies sensitive data based on field values. For example, if your data contains a field named name and two names Alice and Bob, the system checks Alice and Bob against the data identification rule. Regular expression: Enter a regular expression and sample data. Then, click Test accuracy to test the accuracy of the data identification rule. Built-in recognition rules: Select a built-in identification method and enter sample data. Then, click Test accuracy to test the accuracy of the data identification rule. Sample library: Select a sample library and enter sample data. Then, click Test accuracy to test the accuracy of the data identification rule. Self-generating model: Select a custom data identification model and enter sample data. Then, click Test accuracy to test the accuracy of the data identification rule. For more information about how to configure a self-generated data identification model, see Manage a self-generated data recognition model. Note You can select Self-generating model only if your workspace is associated with a MaxCompute compute engine instance. |

|  | Field name recognition | The sensitive field identification settings. You can specify one or more field names for matching sensitive data. The logical relationship between multiple fields is OR. The value must be in the Project.Table.Column format. You can use an asterisk (*) to represent any number of characters in each section of the value. Examples: abcd.efg.*: All data in the efg table in the abcd workspace is identified as sensitive data. ab*.*.salary: Data in the column named salary in all tables in the workspaces whose names are prefixed with ab is identified as sensitive data. *cd.ef*.sa*ry: Data in the columns whose names are prefixed with sa and suffixed with ry is identified as sensitive data. These columns are contained in the tables whose names are prefixed with ef in the workspaces whose names are suffixed with cd. Note Sensitive field identification identifies sensitive data based on field names. For example, if your data contains a field named name and two names Alice and Bob, the system checks name against the data identification rule. |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | Field to rule out | The fields to be ignored. The ignored fields are not identified as sensitive data. The value must be in the Project.Table.Column format. You can use an asterisk (*) to represent any number of characters in each section of the value. Examples: abcd.efg.*: All data in the efg table in the abcd workspace is ignored by sensitive field identification. ab*.*.salary: Data in the column named salary in all tables in the workspaces whose names are prefixed with ab is ignored by sensitive field identification. *cd.ef*.sa*ry: Data in the columns whose names are prefixed with sa and suffixed with ry is ignored by sensitive field identification. These columns are contained in the tables whose names are prefixed with ef in the workspaces whose names are suffixed with cd. |  |
|  |  | The hit ratio threshold of sensitive content identification for a column. If the ratio of identified sensitive values to non-empty values of a column exceeds the threshold, the sensitive data identification rule is hit. By default, the hit ratio threshold is set to 50%. You can also customize the hit ratio threshold based on your business requirements. The following formula is used to calculate the hit ratio of sensitive content identification for a column: 100% × Number of data |  |
|  |  |  | 100% × Number of data |
|  | Hit ratio | records that match the condition of sensitive content |  |
|  | configuration |  |  |
|  |  | identification/Total number of data records in the column |  |

c. After you confirm the configurations of the data identification rule, click **Save drafts** to save a draft. You can also click **Release to use** to publish the sensitive field type. After you publish a sensitive field type, the sensitive field type enters the **The published** state and an identification task is generated for the sensitive field type. You can filter data by sensitive field type and sensitivity level on the **Data Recognition**,
**Data Activities**, and **Data Risks** pages.
4. Manage sensitive field types.
Copy a sensitive field type Find the sensitive field type that you want to copy and click the icon in the Actions column. A new sensitive field type with the same settings is created. The name of the generated sensitive field type is suffixed with **-copy**. By default, it is in the **The draft** state. You can configure the replicated sensitive field type based on your business requirements. Modify a sensitive field type Find the sensitive field type that you want to modify and click the icon in the Actions column. In the dialog box that appears, you can modify the sensitive data identification rule for the sensitive field type in the **Rule Change** step. You can modify the configurations of a custom sensitive field type. However, you cannot change the name, category, and sensitivity level of a built-in sensitive field type. Delete a sensitive field type Find the sensitive field type that you want to delete and click the icon in the Actions column to delete the sensitive field type. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Important**

The following situations occur if a sensitive field type is deleted. Take note of the information before you delete a sensitive field type. The identification results generated based on the sensitive data identification rule for this type are deleted. For more information, see Manually correct sensitive data identification results. The statistics on this sensitive field type are no longer displayed on the Data Recognition page. For more information, see View sensitive data distribution. If the sensitive field type is referenced by a risk identification rule, the sensitive field type is removed from the configurations of the risk identification rule.
5. Publish multiple sensitive field types at a time.
After you publish sensitive field types, the system identifies sensitive data based on the sensitive data identification rules for these types. For more information about the identification results, see View sensitive data distribution. i. Click **Batch release** and select the sensitive field types that you want to publish.

**Note**

You cannot select sensitive field types whose status is The published. ii. Click **release**. Then, the status of each selected sensitive field type is changed to The published.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|

iii. You can also click **Cancel** to cancel the operation.
6. Unpublish multiple sensitive field types at a time.
After you unpublish sensitive field types, the system stops identifying sensitive data for these types. Records of the unpublished sensitive field types on the Data Recognition page and the Manual Check tab are also deleted. Before you unpublish a sensitive field type, check whether it is referenced by **data masking rules** and **risk identification rules**. If so, change the status of the **data masking rule** to Inactive and remove the sensitive field type from the configurations of the **risk identification rule**. i. Click **The batch from the shelves** and select the sensitive field types that you want to unpublish. ii. Click **The shelves**. Then, the status of each selected sensitive field type is changed to The draft. iii. You can also click **Cancel** to cancel the operation.

##### Data masking management

DataWorks supports dynamic and static data masking. This topic describes how to create data masking rules and perform masked queries in DataWorks. Before you create a data masking rule, you must create data identification rules and define data sensitivity levels. For more information, see Data classification and sensitivity levels and Configure data identification rules.

**Background information**

DataWorks supports dynamic data masking. Concept: When a user queries sensitive data, the data is masked in the query results. Scenarios: DataWorks provides built-in data masking scenarios, such as global configuration, display masking, and underlying masking.
1. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Rule Configuration > Data Masking**
**Management**.
On the **Data Masking Management** page, select a **Data Masking Scenario**. DataWorks provides multiple scenarios, or you can create a custom one.
**Global Configuration**: Data masking and whitelist rules configured in this scenario also
apply to other scenarios, such as display masking and underlying masking.
**DataWorks display masking**:
When you query data on the **Data Development** page, sensitive data is masked according to the configured data masking rules. When you preview or query data in **Data Map**, sensitive data is masked based on the configured data masking rules.
**MaxCompute Underlying Masking**: Masks data when it is queried from any
MaxCompute access point. To create a custom data masking scenario, click **Data Masking Scenario** at the bottom of the data masking scenario drop-down list. In the **Add Data Masking Scenario** dialog box, you can customize the **Scenario Name** and **Scenario Code**. The scenario name can contain only Chinese characters, letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). The scenario code can contain only digits and letters.
2. Create a data masking rule.
After you select a scenario, you can create a data masking rule in that scenario for your applications. For more information, see Create a data masking rule: Global Configuration scenario.

**Create a data masking rule: Global Configuration scenario**

This section describes how to configure data masking using the **Global Configuration**
**(_default_scene_code)** scenario as an example. The steps for the **DataWorks Display**
**Masking** and **MaxCompute Underlying Masking** scenarios are similar to those for the
**Global Configuration** scenario.
1. On the **Data Masking Management** page, set **Data Masking Scenario** to **Global**
**Configuration (_default_scene_code)**.
2. Create a data masking rule.
i. On the **Data Masking Configuration** page, click **Create Masking Rule** in the upperright corner. ii. In the **Create Data Masking Rule** dialog box, you can configure **Sensitive Data Type** and **Masking Method**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Sensitive Field Type | Select an existing sensitive data type as needed. The system automatically filters out sensitive data types that are already used in the current data masking scenario. For more information, see Configure data detection rules. |
| Data Masking Rule Name | The system automatically populates this text box with the name of the selected Sensitive Data Type. You can use the suggested name or enter a new one. The rule name must be 1 to 30 characters long and can contain Chinese characters, letters, and digits. If a rule with the same name already exists in the tenant, a Duplicate Rule Name message is displayed. |

a. Configure basic information. b. DataWorks supports two data masking methods: **Masking** and **HASH Encryption**. Masking conceals parts of the information by replacing characters at specific positions with asterisks (*).
**Recommended Method**: From the drop-down list, select **Show first and last**
**characters**, **Show first 3 and last 2 characters** , or **Show first 3 and last 4**
**characters**.

| Icon | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 | Select Characters or Remaining Characters. |
| 2 | Enter an integer from 1 to 100. |
| 3 | Select Mask or Do Not Mask. |

**Custom**: Provides flexible configuration options. You can configure up to 10
segments from left to right. For each segment, you can specify whether it is masked and the number of characters to mask or leave unmasked. You must set exactly one segment to **Remaining Characters**. For example, you can mask the first 3 characters and leave the remaining characters unmasked.

**Hash Encryption**

**Encryption Algorithm**: The supported algorithms are MD5, SHA256, SHA512,
and SM3.
**Salt Value**: The salt for the selected encryption algorithm. The default value is
5. Valid values are integers from 0 to 9.

**Note**

In cryptography, salting involves inserting a specific string into a password at a fixed position. This action generates a hash value that is different from the hash of the original password. This process is called salting. The salt value is the specific string that is inserted. c. To verify the data masking configuration, enter sample data of up to 100 characters in the **Sample Data** text box and click **Verify Masking**. The masked data is displayed in the **Masking Effect** field. iii. Click **Save**. iv. On the **Data Masking Configuration** page, you can set the data masking rule to **Active** or **Inactive**. After a rule is configured, you can click the icons in the Actions column to **Delete**,
**Modify**, or **View Details**.

**Note**

You cannot **Delete** or **Modify** an active rule. To delete or modify a rule, you must first set its status to **Inactive**. Before you deactivate a rule, check if it is used by any tasks and contact the security administrator for confirmation. When a rule is in the **Inactive** state, you can modify its masking method, but not the **Sensitive Data Type** or **Data Masking Rule Name**. After you modify the rule, set its status to **Active** to resume data masking for tasks that use the rule.
3. Add a whitelist.
i. In the menu bar, click **Whitelist Configuration Management**. ii. On the **Whitelist Configuration Management** page, click the **Add Whitelist** button in the upper-right corner. iii. In the **Add Whitelist** dialog box, you can configure the settings.

**Note**

Sensitive data that meets the whitelist conditions is not masked during the specified effective period. iv. Click **Save** to complete the whitelist configuration.
4. Optional: Configure workspace management.

**Important**

This feature is available only in the **DataWorks Data Masking** scenario. Enabling this feature masks query results in the current workspace. If you do not enable this feature, sensitive information may be exposed. i. Click **Workspace Management** in the menu bar. ii. Turn on the switch in the **Status** column for the target workspace. The configuration is applied immediately.
5. What to do next: After you create data masking rules, sensitive data that you query on
pages such as Data Development, Data Preview, and DataAnalysis is masked based on the rules.

#### Track data

You can create a data tracking task to track the source of leaked data. You can also download a data tracking file and delete a data tracking task.

**Configure a data watermark**

1. Log on to DataWorks console.
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products**
**> Data governance > Data Protection**.
3. On the page that appears, click **Try now**.
4. On the Data Protection page, choose **Rule Change > Data Masking** in the left-side
navigation pane.
5. On the Data Masking page, click Create Rule to create a data masking rule. For more
information, see Customize de-identification rules. When you configure a data masking rule, you can turn on **Data watermark**. This way, a data watermark can be embedded into data when data masking is performed on the data, which facilitates the tracking of the leaked data.

**Note**

A data watermark cannot be added to Chinese data.

**Create a data tracking task**

1. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Data traceability**.
2. On the **Data traceability** page, click **New data tracing task**.
3. Drag the file in which data is leaked to the middle part of the **Traceability tasks** dialog
box or click **Upload** to upload the file.

**Note**

You can upload a CSV file whose size is no more than 200 MB.
4. Click **Start tracing** to track the source of the leaked data.

**Note**

After the tracking computing starts, you can close the dialog box, and the computing is not affected.
5. After the computing is complete, click the
icon that corresponds to your data tracking task and view the tracking result. You can also enter a file name in the search box of the Data traceability page to view the historical data tracking task.

**Note**

Tracking results are for reference only. A data tracking task may not generate results or generate one or more results.

**Download a data tracking file**

On the **Data traceability** page, find a data tracking file that you want to download in the Traceability file column and click the icon to download the file.

**Delete a data tracking task**

1. On the **Data traceability** page, find a data tracking task that you want to delete and click
the icon.
2. In the message that appears, click **Confirm**.

### Data Governance Center

#### Overview

Data Governance Center automatically detects issues that need to be handled in data storage, node computing, code development, data quality, and data security. Data Governance Center provides health scores based on the health assessment model and visualizes the governance results by providing governance reports and the rankings of governance issues from the global, workspace, and personal perspectives. This helps you resolve governance issues and achieve governance goals. To govern costs, Data Governance Center provides features such as node resource consumption details, overall trend of resource consumption, and cost estimation for a single node. These features help you effectively optimize resource utilization and reduce costs of various types of used resources.
**check item**: an item that is used to check nodes for violations against constraints before
data development and generate check events that block the subsequent data development process. Check items can help you restrict and manage the data development process. For example, a check item can be configured to prohibit the use of the `SELECT *` statement or the `CREATE TABLE` statement.
**check event**: an event that is triggered by a check item and blocks the subsequent data
development process.
**governance item**: an item that is used by DataWorks to detect governance issues after
nodes are committed and deployed. Governance items are classified into mandatory governance items and optional governance items. For example, you can enable governance items to detect the nodes that time out, nodes that fail for consecutive times, leaf nodes that are not accessed, or dry-run nodes.
**governance issue**: an issue that is detected by DataWorks based on the specified
governance items and waits to be optimized.
**governance plan template**: a template that contains built-in check items and
governance items. You can use governance plan templates to detect issues in data.
**health score**: the score that is calculated based on the health assessment model provided
by DataWorks and reflects the results of the data governance.
**governance unit**: a unit that consists of one or more workspaces. You can view statistics
on the overall health score, governance issues, and check events of the workspaces within a governance unit.
**knowledge base**: solutions to check events and governance issues detected based on the
built-in check items and governance items.

**User roles**

Data Governance Center supports the following types of roles: Governance administrator A governance administrator organizes and drives governance work. A governance administrator has the majority of the permissions required to globally configure governance items and view governance results. A governance administrator can perform data governance on all workspaces and members of a tenant. By default, a Resource Access Management (RAM) user to which the AliyunDataWorksFullAccess policy is attached is a governance administrator and cannot be deleted. A governance administrator can assign the governance administrator role to other RAM users. For more information, see Manage workspace members and roles. Regular user A regular user takes measures to handle the detected issues for data governance. A regular user can view and handle check events and governance issues from a personal perspective. The regular user role is assigned to the members of a tenant. By default, all users except RAM users to which the AliyunDataWorksFullAccess policy is attached are regular users. Data Governance Center checks nodes for violations against constraints before data development based on check items and detects issues after data development based on governance items. This helps you comprehensively handle issues in data. In addition, Data Governance Center provides unified governance plan templates that contain built-in check items and governance items for you to detect issues to be handled. The following figure shows the logic of data governance. Check for violations against constraints based on check items. Check items are used to check nodes for violations against constraints before nodes are committed and deployed. Before you commit and deploy nodes, you can check whether data violates the constraints that you specify for data development by using the check items. If the system detects the data that violates the constraints, a check event is generated and blocks the subsequent data development process. You can handle issues related to the check event so that the data development process can be completed as expected.

| Operation | Description | References |
|---|---|---|
| Select a governance plan template | Data governance is performed based on a governance plan template in Data Governance Center. The governance plan template contains built-in check items and governance items. To use the data governance feature, you must add a governance plan template before you perform the subsequent operations. | View a governance plan template |
| Select effective check items | Create a check item for a registered custom extension. DataWorks allows you to create a check item in Data Governance Center for a custom extension. After that, Data Governance Center detects the check events triggered by the custom extension. Disable one or more check items. If the governance plan template contains a check item that is unnecessary for a workspace, you can disable the check item for this workspace. After you disable the check item, Data Governance Center does not detect the check event triggered by the check item in the specified workspace. | Create and configure check items |

Detect issues based on governance items. Governance items are used to detect governance issues after data development. After nodes are committed and deployed, you can view governance issues from the **global**,
**personal**, or **workspace** perspective in Data Governance Center. Data governance
engineers can identify governance issues and take measures at the earliest opportunity to achieve the goals of data governance. The following figure shows the procedure of data governance.
1. Make the following preparations:
Add a governance plan template and configure check items and governance items that you want to use.

| Select effective governance items | Disable one or more governance items. If the governance plan template contains a governance item that is unnecessary for a workspace, you can create a rule to disable this governance item in the specified workspace. After the governance item is disabled, Data Governance Center does not detect the governance issue based on the governance item in the specified workspace. In addition, the governance issue is not displayed on the Governance issues page. Note You can disable only the optional governance items and cannot create governance items. | Configure governance items |
|---|---|---|

Configure a governance unit. DataWorks allows you to perform data governance for multiple workspaces in a centralized manner by creating a governance unit based on your business requirements. Then, you can view statistics on the overall health score, governance issues, and check events for the workspaces within the governance unit. For more information, see Create and manage governance units.
2. Start a check and handle detected governance issues.
Check nodes for violations against constraints before data development. DataWorks performs a check based on the check items. Before nodes are committed and deployed, DataWorks checks the nodes based on the check items. If data violates the constraints, check events are generated. After that, you can view and handle the check events. For more information, see View and handle check events. Detect governance issues after data development. DataWorks detects governance issues based on the governance items. After nodes are committed and deployed, DataWorks detects and generates governance issues based on the governance items. After that, you can view and handle the governance issues. For more information, see View and handle governance issues.
3. View governance results.
After you handle the issues, you can go to the Governance assessment page to view the governance results of the operations that you performed from different perspectives on the Report and Rankings tabs. You can analyze the governance results to identify the dimensions and types of governance issues that frequently occur. This can help you handle the governance issues and achieve data governance goals. For more information about how to view the governance results, see View data governance results. Data Governance Center calculates health scores based on the governance items by using the health assessment model. You can view the health scores on the Report and Rankings tabs to understand the governance results. A higher health score indicates a better governance result.

###### View and handle governance issues

After you enable a governance plan template provided by DataWorks and configure the governance items, the system detects governance issues based on the configured governance items for the specified tenant. On the Workbench page of DataWorks, you can view the total number of governance issues for tables and nodes, the ranking list of workspaces based on the number of governance issues that need to be handled, the types of governance issues, and the details of the related nodes or tables. This allows you to handle the issues at the earliest opportunity. This topic describes how to view and handle governance issues. A governance plan template is enabled. For more information, see View governance plan templates. Governance items are configured. For more information, see Configure governance items.

**Background information**

Governance issues are detected based on the governance items that you configure for checking data of the current account. DataWorks can help you handle governance issues. The health score is calculated based on the governance items and the built-in health assessment model. A rating grade is provided based on your health score. For more information about the health score, see the "Health scores" section of the Overview topic. DataWorks allows you to view the governance issues for the specified tenant from different perspectives, such as **global perspective**, **workspace perspective**, and **individual**
**perspective**. The health score decreases with the increase in the number of governance
issues. If the health score is low, a low rating grade is given. To achieve your data governance goals, you must handle issues at the earliest opportunity.

**Limits**

Only tenant administrators can view governance issues from the **global perspective**. To view the governance issues from the global perspective, make sure that you are granted the required permissions. For more information, see Manage members. Only workspace administrators can view governance issues from the **workspace**
**perspective**. To view the governance issues of a workspace, you must be the
administrator of the workspace. For more information, see Manage workspace members and roles. A common user can view the governance issues only from the individual perspective. In this case, the ranking list of governance issues is not displayed.
1. Go to the Data Governance Center page.

**Products > Data Governance > Data Governance Center**.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Workbench**. In the left-side navigation pane, click
**Governance issues**. The **Governance issues** page appears.
3. View and handle governance issues.

###### View and handle check events

After you enable a governance plan template and configure check items, DataWorks inspects events triggered by the check items within the current account. On the Workbench page of DataWorks, you can view the total number of check events, the number and ratio of events that fail to pass the check, and the number and ratio of data development processes that are blocked. This helps you discover and handle check events at the earliest opportunity. This topic describes how to view and manage check events. A governance plan template is enabled. For more information, see View a governance plan template. Check items are configured. For more information, see Create and configure check items.

**Background information**

Check items are used to check nodes for violations against constraints before nodes are committed and deployed. This helps you reduce governance issues detected after data development. A check event is an event triggered by a check item. DataWorks detects governance issues that are to be handled based on the governance items after nodes are committed and deployed. The health score is calculated based on the health assessment model provided by DataWorks and shows the governance grade of the current account. For more information about the health score, see the "Health scores" section of the Overview topic.

| Secti on | Description |
|---|---|

For more information, see Manage members. Only workspace administrators can view check events from the **workspace perspective**. To view the check events of a specific workspace from the workspace perspective, you must be assigned the Workspace Administrator role of the workspace. For more information, see Manage workspace members and roles. Common users can view check events only from the **individual perspective**.

###### View and manage whitelists

If a governance issue is added to a whitelist, the governance issue is not detected by DataWorks within the effective period of the whitelist. This topic describes how to view and manage whitelists. Governance issues are added to a whitelist. For more information, see View and handle governance issues.

To view the whitelists of a specific workspace from the workspace perspective, you must be assigned the Workspace Administrator role of the workspace. For more information, see Manage members and roles. Regular users can view the whitelists that they created only from the **personal**
**perspective**.

##### Automated governance

###### Graceful undeployment

| Operation | Unde ploym ent meth od | Comparison | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Select the nodes that you want to undeploy | Direct undepl oymen t | To directly undeploy a node, go to Operation Center. In the left-side navigation pane, choose Cycle Task Maintenance > Cycle Task. On the page that appears, find the node that you want to manage, click More, and then click Freeze in the Actions column. | You cannot view the impacts and risks of the undeployment and you may undeploy the wrong node. |
|  | Gracef ul undepl oymen t | You can manually specify the objects that you want to undeploy or select the objects that are automatically recommended by the system. You can evaluate the impact scope and risks of the undeployment. | Select the objects that you want to undeploy based on node IDs, lineage, and tables. The impacts and risks of the undeployment are evaluated. |
| Configure settings for node undeployme nt | Direct undepl oymen t | N/A | Notifications cannot be pushed to the corresponding contacts. |
|  | Gracef ul undepl oymen t | You can send notifications to the specified contacts in each phase of the graceful undeployment process by internal messages, emails, DingTalk chatbots, or webhooks. | The undeployment process can be handled through multiple phases and notifications are pushed to the corresponding contacts in each phase. |

Data Asset Governance provides a comprehensive undeployment solution for invalid nodes or tables that are identified during data governance. The solution supports various features, such as undeployment risk evaluation, undeployment notification push, and undeployment process management. This solution eliminates the need to manually identify undeployment risks. This solution also resolves the issue that you cannot undeploy nodes whose descendant nodes are scheduled as normal or you cannot determine whether to undeploy nodes due to unpredictable risks. The solution allows you to undeploy multiple nodes or tables at the same time. This improves the undeployment efficiency.

**Background information**

Graceful undeployment supports undeployment impact analysis and undeployment process management, which are unavailable in the traditional undeployment. Node undeployment notifications can be sent to related contacts by using various methods at each phase of the node undeployment process.

| Specify the method to execute the node undeployme nt plan | Direct undepl oymen t | N/A | After you click to undeploy a node, the node is immediately undeployed. You cannot cancel the undeployment. |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | Gracef ul undepl oymen t | Manually Trigger Execution Automatic Execution | You can select a method to undeploy a node based on the scenario to save you sufficient time to cancel the undeployment. |
| View and manage the node undeployme nt plan | Direct undepl oymen t | N/A | The selected node is directly undeployed without a silence period. You may easily select the wrong node and cause business interruptions. |
|  | Gracef ul undepl oymen t | You can view the details of an undeployment plan and perform various operations on the nodes that are specified in the plan. For example, you can view the details of the nodes, cancel the node undeployment, or roll back the undeployment operation. | The undeployment can be canceled or rolled back when you identify errors within the silence period. |

**Limits**

You can add only objects in the same workspace to an undeployment plan. Up to 200 objects can be added to an undeployment plan. The graceful undeployment feature allows you to roll back the operations performed on a node before the **undeployment** phase of the process, and allows you to roll back the operations performed on a table before the **undeployment completion** phase of the process. To create an undeployment plan, you must meet one of the following requirements: You have an Alibaba Cloud account. You are a workspace administrator. You are a tenant-level data governance administrator. You are a workspace-level data governance administrator. You are an O&M engineer. Only Alibaba Cloud accounts and workspace administrators can perform all operations on an undeployment plan. O&M engineers have full permissions only on the undeployment plans that they create. O&M engineers have only read permissions on the undeployment plans that are created by other users. Tenant-level or workspace-level data governance administrators can create, configure, and delete undeployment plans but cannot start or execute nodes on which they do not have permissions.

**Usage notes**

You cannot select an object that is already added to an undeployment plan. Each object can be added only to one undeployment plan. Specific types of objects cannot be added to an undeployment plan. For example, you cannot add the root node of a workspace to an undeployment plan or add a zero load node that you created for an undeployment plan to the undeployment plan. If an object that you want to undeploy has descendant objects and the scheduling dependencies between the descendant objects and the object are not removed within the specified period of time, the system generates a zero load node and configures the zero load node as the ancestor node of the descendant objects. The operations that you need to perform to create a node undeployment plan vary based on the type of node. You can follow the on-screen instructions to create a node undeployment plan for a type of node. The graceful undeployment feature allows you to roll back an undeployment operation only before the object is undeployed.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Tag Management**.
3. In the top navigation bar, click **Workbench**.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Automated Governance > Graceful Shutdown**.
The **Graceful Shutdown** page appears.
5. In the upper part of the Graceful Shutdown page, select the workspace to which the objects
that you want to undeploy belong from the **Workspace** drop-down list. Only the workspaces to which you are added as a member are displayed in the drop-down list.
6. On the **Graceful Shutdown** page, click **Create Plan**.

**Step 2: Select the objects that you want to undeploy**

1. . Configure the basic information about an undeployment plan**
You can specify the workspace to which the objects that you want to undeploy belong from the **Workspace** drop-down list and enter a custom plan name in the **Plan Name** field. In the **To-Be-Undeployed Object** section, you can select **Task** or **Table** based on your business requirements. Undeploy nodes: Select **Add to-be-undeployed Object** or **Import Based on Lineage** to add nodes that you want to undeploy.
**Add to-be-undeployed Object**: Add nodes that you want to undeploy by specifying the
node IDs.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Undeployment Impact Assessment | Low: The table or output table of the node within the previous month has not been consumed. High: The table or output table of the node within the previous month has been consumed. |
| Impact Item Description | The description of the undeployment impact assessment. |
| The output table is consumed. | Information about the consumption of the output table of the node. |
| Task That Generates Table | The output node of the table. You can click it to view the node information. |
| Number of Affected Baselines/Highest Baseline Level | The number of baselines affected by the output node of the table and the highest baseline level. The number of baselines affected by the node and the highest baseline level. Note For more information about node baseline monitoring, see Manage baselines. |

**Import Based on Lineage**: Select a node and select nodes based on lineage levels.

**Note**

You can view the node ID in the **General** section of the **Properties** panel on the node configuration page. You can also go to Operation Center and choose **Cycle Task Maintenance >**
**Cycle Task** in the left-side navigation pane to view the node ID.
Undeploy tables: You can select **Add to-be-undeployed Object** to undeploy tables.

**Note**

You cannot select an object that is already added to an undeployment plan. Each object can be added only to one undeployment plan. Specific types of objects cannot be added to an undeployment plan. For example, you cannot add the root node of a workspace to an undeployment plan or add a zero load node that you created for an undeployment plan to the undeployment plan.

| Phase | Description | Scenario |
|---|---|---|
| Start Undeploy ment | Start the graceful undeployment. This phase is selected by default and cannot be unselected. | - |
| Delayed Schedulin g | Delay the scheduling time of the objects that you want to undeploy. In this case, you delay the time when the output tables of the objects and their descendant objects are generated. | If no data is generated by the ancestor platform, you can select this phase to ensure that the nodes can run as normal. |
| Suspend Schedulin g | Freeze the objects that you want to undeploy. To freeze the objects, go to Operation Center. In the left-side navigation pane, choose Cycle Task Maintenance > Cycle Task. On the page that appears, find the objects that you want to freeze and freeze the objects. The objects and their descendant objects no longer generate tables. | You can select this phase if you have suspended a business but want to keep the workflow. |
| Undeploy Task | Undeploy the desired objects. After the objects are undeployed, no instance is generated on the next day. The scheduling mode of the existing instances is set to dry run and the system no longer runs these instances. This phase is selected by default and you can unselect it. | You can select this phase to undeploy a node or workflow that is no longer needed. |
| Rename Output Table | Rename the output table of a node or table. | You can select this phase if you want to identify the output table of an undeployed object. |
| Reset Table Lifecycle | Reset the lifecycle of the output table of a node or table. | You can select this phase if you want to retain the output table of an undeployed object for a period of time. Note Only MaxCompute tables are supported. |

After you add objects that you want to undeploy, you can configure fine-grained undeployment settings, including the **Start Undeployment**, **Delayed Scheduling**,
**Suspend Scheduling**, **Undeploy Task**, **Rename Output Table**, **Reset Table Lifecycle**,
**Delete Output Table**, and **Undeploy Completed** phases.

| Delete Output Table | Delete the output table of a node or table. | You can select this phase you do not need the output table of an undeployed object. |
|---|---|---|
| Undeploy Complete d | End the graceful undeployment. This phase is selected by default and cannot be unselected. | - |

**Note**

The steps in the phases of the graceful undeployment plan are performed in sequence. You can specify whether to perform the step in each phase. If you unselect a phase, the phase is skipped by default and the system proceeds to the next phase. The graceful undeployment plan allows you to send notifications to the specified contacts by **internal messages** and **emails**.

**Step 4: Specify the method to execute the undeployment plan**

You can specify the method to perform the step in each phase of the undeployment plan. You can select **Manually Trigger Execution** or **Automatic Execution** for the Execution Mode parameter.

**Manually Trigger Execution**

**Note**: Each step of the undeployment process can be performed only after the previous
step is confirmed by the creator of the undeployment plan.
**Recommended scenario**: The node or table is used in **important** situations of the
business workflow.

**Automatic Execution**

**Note**: Each step of the undeployment process is automatically performed based on the
silence period that you configured. A step is automatically performed when the silence period of the previous step ends.
**Recommended scenario**: You need to undeploy a large number of business workflows
and the importance of the workflows is low. On the **Shutdown** page, you can view the list of undeployment plans. You can **execute**,
**cancel**, or **delete** an undeployment plan.

**Note**

If you cancel an undeployment plan, the system cancels undeployment for nodes that are in the Undeploying state in the undeployment plan. Undeployed nodes are not affected. If you delete an undeployment plan, the system cancels undeployment for nodes that are in the Undeploying state in the undeployment plan. Undeployed nodes are not affected. After the undeployment is canceled, the system deletes the undeployment plan. The deletion operation is irreversible. You can click **Running Details** in the **Actions** column of an undeployment plan to view the configuration details of the plan. You can also perform the operations that are described in the following table on a single node. You can view the undeployment details of a single node, such as the undeployment progress, node status, and execution details of each phase. You can also perform various operations on the node, such as canceling undeployment for the node and rolling back the undeployment operation for the node. Cancel undeployment for a single node: You can cancel the unfinished steps of the node undeployment process for the node. Roll back the undeployment operation for a single node: You can roll back all undeployment steps for the node to the initial states. You cannot roll back a single step for the node.

**Note**

If an undeployment plan is canceled, you cannot perform the rollback operation. If a substep of the step in the current phase is being performed, you cannot perform the rollback operation. You cannot roll back the operations performed on a node after the undeployment phase. You cannot roll back the operations performed on an object (node or table) after the undeployment completion phase.

#### Usage analysis

##### Usage overview

The resource usage overview page displays the resource usage metrics in a specified workspace on a specified date. The page consists of the DataWorks Task Resource Usage, Use of Computing Resources and Storage Resources, Rankings of User Resource Usage, and Fluctuation Analysis. This allows you to learn resource usage at the earliest opportunity and properly use resources.
1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Tag Management**.
3. In the top navigation bar of the Tag Management page, click **Usage Analysis**. In the left-
side navigation pane, click **Core Metrics**. The resource usage overview page appears.

**View resource usage**

You can view the resource usage of DataWorks nodes, the usage of computing and storage resources, and the trend of changes in computing and storage resources in the specified workspace on the specified date. This allows you to learn resource usage at the earliest opportunity and perform resource optimization based on your business requirements.

**View and analyze resource changes**

You can view the fluctuation of resource usage metrics, such as **Computing Resource**
**Consumption**, **Storage Resource Consumption**, **DataWorks Scheduling Resource**
**Consumption**, and **DataWorks Batch Synchronization Consumption** , in the selected
workspace on the selected date. By default, the metrics whose fluctuating values are greater than 0 are displayed. You can sort nodes based on the metrics that you want to display and view the resources whose usage severely fluctuates. You can click a **node name** to view the details of the node.

**View the rankings of users by resource usage**

You can view the rankings of users by resource usage in the selected workspace on the selected date. The resource types include **MaxCompute computing resources**,
**MaxCompute storage resources**, **DataWorks periodic scheduling resources**, and
**DataWorks batch synchronization resources**. You can also click **View Details** in the
lower-left corner of each tab to go to the corresponding page to view the details. For example, if you click View Details in the lower-left corner of the MaxCompute Computing Resources or MaxCompute Storage Resources tab, you can view the details of computing or storage resources. For more information, see Data pivoting from the resource type perspective.

##### Data pivoting from the resource type

**perspective**

Data Governance Center allows you to view and analyze the resource usage of a workspace by resource type, such as computing or storage resources. This helps you determine how to use the overall resources. This topic describes how to view the usage of computing and storage resources.

**Go to Resource Type Pivoting**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Tag Management**.
3. In the top navigation bar of Data Governance Center, click **Usage Analysis**. In the left-side
navigation pane, click an item in the **Resource Type Pivoting** section.

**View the usage details of computing resources**

You can choose **Resource Type Pivoting > Computing Resources** to view the consumption details of computing resources in the specified workspace on a specified date. You can click **Custom columns** to specify the columns that you want to show or hide on the current tab. You can view the details of a resource **by task** or **by job**. You can also click the icon to the right of a column name to sort records based on the column.

**View the usage details of storage resources**

You can choose **Resource Type Pivoting > Storage Resources** to view the consumption details of storage resources in the specified workspace on a specified date. The details include the table storage size, lifecycle, number of partitions, and owner of the table. You can optimize your business based on the analysis results of each dimension on the tab and your business scenario.

##### Data pivoting from the R&D link

**perspective**

Data Governance Center allows you to view and analyze the status and resource consumption of DataWorks batch synchronization nodes and scheduling nodes in a workspace from the R&D link perspective, which involves data synchronization and data development. This way, you can learn the types of resources that have the highest costs and identify nodes that fail to run. Then, you can adjust the proportion of resources to purchase, identify the issues that block the execution of nodes, and fix the issues at the earliest opportunity.

2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Tag Management**.

navigation pane, click an item in the **R&D Link Pivoting** section.

**Average Running Duration in 7 Days** , **Waiting Time Fluctuation Rate**, **Running**
**Duration Fluctuation Rate**, and **Node Owner**.

#### Configuration management

##### View a governance plan template

DataWorks provides governance plan templates that are applicable to various industries. You can directly use a governance plan template to detect and handle governance issues within the current account based on the governance items and check items configured in the template. This topic describes how to view the configurations of a governance plan template.

**Background information**

DataWorks Data Governance Center provides governance plan templates to help you troubleshoot governance issues within the current account. Each governance plan template collects and categorizes common governance items and check items, and provides corresponding solutions. You can use a governance plan template to quickly detect governance issues within the current account. Data Governance Center displays the detected issues in reports or rankings to provide reference for data governance engineers. After the issues are handled, Data Governance Center shows the effectiveness of data governance by using health scores. Implementation rules A governance plan template takes effect in all workspaces of a tenant. After you enable Data Governance Center for a tenant and specify the default governance plan template, this template takes effect in all DataWorks workspaces of the tenant. After you enable a governance plan template, the system generates check items and governance items based on the template. By default, the built-in check items and governance items are enabled and take effect globally. Data Governance Center detects governance issues and displays data for the current tenant based on the check items and governance items configured in the template. You can also go to the details pages of check items and governance items of the default governance plan template to view the details of check items and governance items in the template.

**Note**

The built-in check items in a governance plan template are available only for ODPS SQL nodes. If a governance plan template contains a check item that is unnecessary for a workspace, you can disable the check item for this workspace. After the check item is disabled, Data Governance Center does not inspect events triggered based on the check item in the specified workspace. For more information, see Create and configure check items. If a governance plan template contains a governance item that is unnecessary for a workspace, you can create an exclusion rule on the Governance item configuration page to disable this governance item in the specified workspace. After the governance item is disabled, Data Governance Center does not detect governance issues based on the governance item in the specified workspace. In addition, the detected governance issues are not displayed on the Governance issues page. For more information about how to configure governance items, see Configure governance items.

**Limits**

DataWorks allows you to use only the default template provided by the system. You cannot modify the configurations of this template. DataWorks does not allow you to create custom templates.

**Procedure**

1. Go to the Data Governance Center page.
i. Log on to the DataWorks console. ii. In the upper-left corner of the DataStudio page, click the icon and choose **All**
**Products > Data Governance > Data Governance Center**.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configuration**. The **Solution Template** page appears.
3. View the configurations of a template.
In the **Default Template** section, you can click **Inspector details** or **Governance**
**Details** to view the details of check items or governance items in the template.

**Note**

DataWorks allows you to use only the default template provided by the system. You cannot modify the configurations of this template. View the details of check items. On the **Inspector details** page, check items are categorized in the **R&D**, **quality**,
**security**, **computing**, and **storage** dimensions. On the tab of each dimension, you can
view the information about each check item, such as the ID, name, and applicable module. By default, check items are enabled on the Inspector details page. After a check item is enabled, Data Governance Center inspects events triggered based on this check item. If an event does not pass the check, the subsequent data development process is blocked. In a governance plan template, you cannot modify the configurations of check items. To enable or disable a check item, you can go to the **Inspector Setting** page. For more information about how to enable a check item, see Create and configure check items. The following figure shows the details of check items in the R&D dimension. View the details of governance items. On the **Governance Details** page, **mandatory** and **optional** governance items are categorized in the **R&D**, **quality**, **security**, **computing**, and **storage** dimensions. On the tab of each dimension, you can view the information about each governance item, such as the name, description, associated solution, and health score weight. Data Governance Center provides solutions for different governance items. If issues are detected based on a governance item, you can find the governance item and click the button in the **Associated solution** column to view the provided solution. Then, you can resolve the issues by using the provided solution. In a governance plan template, you cannot modify the configurations of governance items. To configure optional governance items, you can go to the **Governance item** page. On this page, you can enable or disable an optional governance item based on your business requirements, and configure exclusion rules to disable specific optional governance items in a workspace. For more information, see Configure governance items.

**Note**

A health assessment model is built in each governance plan template. This model defines the health score weights of different governance items. You cannot modify the health score weights. Mandatory governance items are part of the criteria for calculating health scores. Therefore, mandatory governance items must be globally enabled. You cannot disable mandatory governance items or specify them in exclusion rules. Optional governance items are excluded from the criteria for calculating health scores. You can enable optional governance items based on your business requirements. The following figure shows the details of governance items in the R&D dimension.

##### Create and configure check items

After you enable a governance plan template, the system automatically generates check items based on the template. You can enable the check items based on your business requirements. If the built-in check items cannot meet your requirements, you can create a check item in Data Governance Center for an extension that you register. You can use check items to inspect events that are generated before files are committed and deployed. If an event does not pass the check, the subsequent process is blocked. A governance plan template is enabled. For more information, see View governance plan templates. An extension is registered. The prerequisite is required if you want to create a check item for an extension.

**Background information**

Data Governance Center allows you to use the out-of-the-box and built-in check items by enabling a governance plan template. The built-in check items include Forbid Use of select* and Forbid Simple Processing. You can enable the check items based on your business requirements. DataWorks allows you to create a check item in Data Governance Center for a custom extension. After the check item is created, Data Governance Center inspects the events triggered by the custom extension. If you do not want DataWorks to inspect events triggered by the custom extension, you do not need to create a check item for the extension.

**Note**

Built-in check items are available only for ODPS SQL nodes. You can use built-in check items to inspect events that are generated before files are committed and deployed. If an event does not pass the check, the subsequent process is blocked.

**Limits**

Only governance administrators and workspace administrators can create, enable, and disable check items. These operations cannot be performed by common users. Governance administrators can view all check items within the current account. Common users can view only the check items in the current DataWorks workspace. Only governance administrators can globally enable or disable the check item feature. An Alibaba Cloud account or a Resource Access Management (RAM) user to which the
**AliyunDataWorksFullAccess** policy is attached is a governance administrator.

**Go to the Inspector Setting page**

1. Go to the Data Governance Center page.
i. Log on to the DataWorks console. icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All**
**Products > Data Governance > Data Governance Center**.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configuration**. In the left-side navigation pane, click
**Inspector**. The **Inspector Setting** page appears.

**Manage check items**

On the **Inspector Setting** page, you can view the check items within the current account or the specified workspace. You can also enable or disable specified check items for a workspace. After a check item is enabled, Data Governance Center inspects events triggered by the check item. The following table describes the sections on the Inspector Setting page.

**Note**

Governance administrators can view all check items within the current account. Common users can view only the check items in the current DataWorks workspace. Only governance administrators can globally enable or disable the check item feature. An Alibaba Cloud account or a Resource Access Management (RAM) user to which the **AliyunDataWorksFullAccess** policy is attached is a governance administrator.

| No. | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 | In this section, you can turn on or off Enable check items. This is a global switch and can be used for the following operations: Globally enable or disable the check item feature. If you turn off Enable check items, Data Governance Center does not inspect events that are generated before a node is committed based on the check items in the governance plan template. Determine whether the switches can be used in the Enable column for each check item. If you turn off Enable check items, the switches in the Enabled column cannot be used. Determine whether the built-in check items are displayed on the Extension page of the Management Center page for all workspaces that reside in the current region. Note You can globally turn on or off Enable check items only by using an Alibaba Cloud account or as a RAM user to which the AliyunDataWorksFullAccess policy is attached. |
| 2 | In this section, you can view check items on the following tabs:R &D, Quality, Security, Computing, and Storage. On each tab, you can specify which check items are displayed by using the Workspace, Name, Enable, and Source parameters. Note You can enter keywords in the Name field to search for specific check items. The keywords are used to perform a fuzzy match. The search result includes all check items whose names match the keywords. |

| 3 | In this section, you can view the information of the specified check items, such as then ame, check event, source, owner, and modification time. You can also perform the following operations: Specify check events. Find the check item that you want to manage and click the icon in the Effective Point column. In the Edit Effective Point dialog box, specify the events to be inspected based on the check item. You can select events that are generated before files are committed and deployed. If an event does not pass the check, the subsequent process is blocked. Enable or disable a specific check item. Turn on or off in the Enable column to enable or disable a check item. After a check item is disabled, Data Governance Center does not inspect events based on this check item. Note If you disable Enable check items, the switches in the Enabled column cannot be operated. Enable or disable multiple check items at a time. You can select multiple check items and click Batch Enable or Batch Disable in the lower part of the page to enable or disable selected check items at a time. Note In this section, operations on check items take effect only in the current workspace. After a check item is disabled, the operation takes effect only in the specified workspace. In other workspaces, this check item is still enabled. |
|---|---|

**Create check items**

After you enable a governance plan template, the system automatically generates check items based on the template. If the built-in check items cannot meet your requirements, you can create check items for extensions that you want.

**Note**

The built-in check items in the governance plan template are available only for ODPS SQL nodes.
1. Click **New Inspector** in the upper-right corner.
2. Configure the check item.
In the **New Inspector** dialog box, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Select Extensions | The extension that you register. Select a registered extension from the drop-down list. If no extension is available, click Go New to register an extension. |
| Type | The type of the check item. Valid values: Development, Quality, Security, Computation, and Storage. After the configuration is complete, you can choose filter check events by type on the Check Events page of Workbench. For more information, see View and handle check events. |

3. Click **OK**.

**Example of a triggered check item**

After you enable a check item in Data Governance Center, when you click the Submit icon to commit a node in DataStudio, the system checks the node based on the logic of the check item. You can go to the Operation Check page to view the check status and click the value in the Status column to view the details. If the node fails the check, a related check event is generated to block the related procedure.

##### Configure governance items

After you enable a governance plan template, the system generates governance items based on the template. Governance items are classified into mandatory governance items and optional governance items. By default, mandatory governance items are globally enabled and cannot be modified. Optional governance items can be enabled based on your business requirements. You can also configure exclusion rules to disable optional governance items in the specified workspace. This topic describes how to view and configure governance items. A governance plan template is enabled. For more information, see View a governance plan template.

**Background information**

If you configure exclusion rules to disable optional governance items in the specified workspace, DataWorks does not detect issues based on the governance items in the workspace.

**Limits**

The mandatory governance items are part of the criteria for calculating health scores. By default, mandatory governance items are globally enabled and take effect in all workspaces of the specified tenant. You cannot disable the mandatory governance items or include them in exclusion rules. DataWorks allows you to specify exclusion rules only for optional governance items. DataWorks does not support custom governance items.

**Procedure**

To handle governance issues that are detected by DataWorks based on a specific governance item, find the governance item and click the link in the Associated solution column to view the provided solution. |

1. Go to the Data Governance Center page.
i. Log on to the DataWorks console. ii. In the upper-left corner of the DataStudio page, click the icon and choose **All**
**Products > Data Governance > Data Governance Center**.

**Configuration** page, click **Governance item**. The **Governance Setting** page appears.
3. View and configure governance items.
On the **Governance Setting** page, you can view the information about governance items, enable or disable optional governance items, and configure exclusion rules on the
**Development**, **Quality**, **Safety**, **Computation**, and **Storage** tabs. The following figure
shows the information displayed and operations that you can perform on the Development tab.

You can also enable or disable a governance item by turning on or off the switch in the Enable column based on your business requirements. |
