| 3 | In this area, you can select a workspace for which you want to create exclusion rules to disable specific optional governance items or delete the disabled optional governance items. After you disable optional governance items for the specified workspace, DataWorks does not detect issues based on the governance items in this workspace. In addition, these issues are not displayed for the workspace on the Governance issues page. |

##### Create and manage governance units

A governance unit consists of one or more DataWorks workspaces. You can view the information about the health score, governance issue, and check events about all workspaces that belong to a governance unit. Members of the workspaces can view the management reports and governance reports of the governance unit to which the workspaces belong, and identify and handle governance issues in the governance unit at the earliest opportunity. This topic describes how to create and view a governance unit. A governance plan template is enabled. For more information, see View a governance plan template. Check items are configured. For more information, see Create and configure check items. Governance items are configured. For more information, see Configure governance items.

**Background information**

A governance unit consists of one or more DataWorks workspaces. You can view the information about the health score, governance issue, and check events about all workspaces that belong to a governance unit. In most cases, workspaces of the same business type are included in one governance unit. A workspace can belong to multiple governance units. Members of a workspace can view the management reports and governance reports of the governance unit to which the workspace belongs, and identify and handle governance issues in the governance unit at the earliest opportunity.

**Limits**

DataWorks allows only governance administrators to create, modify, or delete governance units. Regular users can only view the information about governance units.

**Create a governance unit**

1. Go to the Data Governance Center page.
i. Log on to the DataWorks console.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the governance unit. |
| Description | The description of the governance unit. |
| Workspace | The workspaces to be included in the governance unit. You can select one or more DataWorks workspaces for which you want to collect statistics on health scores, governance issues, and check events. You can add workspaces of the same business type to one governance unit to identify and troubleshoot similar issues. Note Only the workspaces in which you are assigned the Workspace Administrator role are displayed. |
| Owner | The owner of the governance unit. The owner manages the governance unit in a centralized manner. |

ii. In the upper-left corner of the DataStudio page, click the icon and choose **All**
**Products > Data Governance > Data Governance Center**.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configuration**. In the left-side navigation pane, click
**Governance Unit**. The **Governance unit** page is displayed.
3. Create a governance unit.
i. Click **New**. ii. Configure the governance unit. In the **Governance unit** dialog box, configure the parameters as required. iii. Click **OK**. On the **Governance unit** page, you can search for a specific governance unit by configuring the **Name** and **Workspace** parameters. In the search result, you can view the **name**,
**description**, **workspaces**, **owner**, **creator**, and **creation time** of the governance unit. You
can also modify or delete a governance unit.

**Note**

You can enter a keyword in the **Name** field to search for governance units in fuzzy match mode. All governance units whose names contain the keyword are displayed in the search result. DataWorks allows only governance administrators to create, modify, or delete governance units. Regular users can only view the information about governance units.

#### View data governance results

After check events and governance issues are handled, you can view data governance results in the form of governance reports or governance rankings on the Assessment page in Tag Management. You can analyze data governance results to identify the dimensions and types of governance issues that frequently occur. This helps you handle the governance issues and achieve your goal of data governance. This topic describes how to view and analyze governance reports and governance rankings. A governance plan template is enabled. For more information, see View a governance plan template. Governance items are configured. For more information, see Configure governance items. Check items are configured. For more information, see Create and configure check items. Governance issues are handled. For more information, see View and handle governance issues. Check events are handled. For more information, see View and handle check events.

**Background information**

Tag Management uses a built-in health assessment model to perform a quantitative assessment on the data governance results of your account and generates an overall health score and a health score for each governance dimension. A higher health score indicates better governance results. You can view data governance results from different governance dimensions in the form of governance reports or governance rankings on the Assessment page. Governance reports On the right side of the Assessment page, click Report. On the page that appears, you can check the governance results based on an overall health score and an overall assessment of data governance from the **global perspective**, **workspace perspective**, or **personal**
**perspective**. You can also view the health score, health score trend, and governance
issues that need to be handled from the computing, storage, R&D, security, and quality dimensions. This allows you to identify the dimensions and types of governance issues that frequently occur and organize your governance work in an efficient manner. Governance rankings Governance rankings help you manage data governance work. You can view the rankings of **governance units**, **workspaces**, and **user accounts** based on the governance results in handling **governance issues** and **check events**.

**Limits**

Governance reports: Only data governance administrators can view governance reports from the **global**
**perspective**. To view governance reports from the global perspective, you must be
assigned the Data Governance Administrator role. For more information, see Manage members and roles. Only workspace administrators can view governance reports from the **workspace**
**perspective**. To view the governance reports of a specific workspace from the workspace
perspective, you must be assigned the Workspace Administrator role of the workspace. For more information, see Manage members and roles. Regular users can view governance reports only from the **personal perspective**. Tag Management allows you to view only the governance reports of the previous day. Governance rankings: Only data governance administrators can view governance rankings. To view governance rankings, you must be assigned the Data Governance Administrator role.

**Go to the Assessment page**

1. Go to the Tag Management page.
i. Log on to the DataWorks console. ii. In the upper-right corner, click the icon and then choose **All Products > Data**
**Governance > Tag Management**.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Assessment** to go to the **Assessment** page.

**View a governance report**

| 1 | In this area, you can select Report or Rank to check the governance results. Note By default, the Assessment page displays a report for you to check the governance results. |

You can check the overall governance results from different perspectives or check the governance results from each governance dimension. This allows you to identify the dimensions of governance issues that frequently occur and organize your governance work in an efficient manner. **View governance rankings**

Governance rankings are used to perform governance operations and facilitate data governance. On the Rank page, you can view the rankings of governance units, workspaces, and user accounts based on the governance results in handling governance issues and check events. The following figure shows the ranking of **workspaces** based on the governance results in handling governance issues and check events.

By individual: displays the ranking of user accounts based on the governance results in handling governance issues and check events. You can filter governance items and check events by role. Governance item By default, governance units, workspaces, and user accounts are sorted in ascending order of health score on the Governance item tab. Other ranking information includes the deducted points, total number of detected issues, total number of fixed issues, and fixing rate of governance units, workspaces, or user accounts. For lower-ranked governance units, workspaces, and user accounts, you can ask the responsible personnel to handle governance issues at the earliest opportunity to achieve governance goals. Inspector By default, governance units, workspaces, and user accounts are sorted in ascending order of event detection rate on the Inspector tab. Other ranking information includes the total number of checks, total number of blocks, total blocking rate, rate of forced blocking, and estimated risk avoidance of governance units, workspaces, or users. For higher- ranked governance units, workspaces, and user accounts, you can ask the responsible personnel to implement data governance and handle check events. Note The preceding figure shows the layout of the rankings on the Governance item tab. You can click the Inspector tab and view the rankings as needed. |

### Data Assets

#### Overview

The Data Assets module of DataWorks helps enterprises make an inventory of their data assets and clarify the business value of data mid-end. This way, business staff of the enterprises can quickly obtain the required data assets and consume the data assets in a secure environment. This topic describes the components and features of Data Assets.

| Compo nent | Scenario | Applicable role | Feature | Reference s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manage ment Center | The manageme nt staff of enterprises can create directories for enterprise data assets, and perform daily manageme nt operations. For example, they can publish and unpublish data assets, and mount data assets to directories. | Data warehouse administrat ors and data developers | Directory Management: You can manage data from different platforms from the business perspective, create a complete set of asset directories, and mount data assets to directories. This way, you can quickly find the required assets. Asset Management: You can perform multiple asset management operations. For example, you can publish and unpublish data assets, and mount data assets to directories. Publish: You can view and use data assets on the Asset Panoramic and Asset Marketplace pages only after the data assets are published. Unpublish: You cannot use data assets after they are unpublished. Proceed with caution. Mount to Directory: You must select the directory to which a data asset is mounted when you publish the data asset. Then, you can query the data asset based on the directory. Asset Space: You can configure an asset space to manage data assets. This helps data asset administrators adjust the scope of managed data assets. Data assets from different workspaces can be managed in the same asset space. Asset Collection: You can collect the information about file assets to the Data Assets module. Then, you can manage and use these file assets in a centralized manner. | Manage asset directorie s Manage data assets Configur e an asset space Collect informati on about data assets |
| Asset Panora ma | You can learn the asset overview of the data mid-end and view the asset statistics. | Data warehouse administrat ors and business managers | Business Overview: This section displays the overview of your data assets and their relationships in a 3D panorama. This way, the importance of data assets in business development is clearly displayed. Asset Overview: This section displays data assets in different dimensions on a dashboard. | View the asset panorama |

The Data Assets module allows you to make an inventory of the data assets of the current workspace, check the status of data assets, search for data assets, and consume data assets in a centralized manner. The following table describes the components of the Data Assets module.

| Asset Market place | This component helps you query and view data assets. | Asset users, such as business staff and developers | You can find data assets in the directory tree level by level or search for data assets based on keywords. You can also filter data assets based on multiple conditions, such as asset type, asset owner, and asset tag. This way, you can quickly query and view data assets. | Search for data assets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Asset Value | This component helps you make an inventory of and use data assets. | Data warehou se administr ators and business manager s Asset users, such as business staff and develope rs | This component can rate the value of each data asset. This helps you make an inventory of data assets and reasonably use data assets. | View asset values |
| Asset Consu mption | This component helps you query and download data assets. | Asset users, such as business staff and developers | You can query and download data assets on which you have permissions. | Consume data assets |

#### View the asset panorama

The **Data Asset** module of DataWorks provides the asset panorama, which is a convenient data asset inventory tool for enterprise managers. The Business Panorama tab displays the overview of enterprise data assets and their relationships in a 3D panorama. The Asset Overview tab displays the statistics of enterprise data assets from various dimensions to help you learn the status of data assets. This topic describes how to use the asset panorama.

**Limits**

DataWorks collects statistics on all published data assets in the current workspace and other workspaces that are managed in the same asset space. Data assets that are not published are not displayed on the Asset Panorama page. For more information about how to publish data assets, see Manage data assets.

**Go to the Asset Panorama page**

1. Go to the Data Asset page.
2. On the Data Asset page, click the
icon in the left-side navigation pane to go to the **Asset**
**Panorama** page.
On the Asset Panorama page, you can view the following information: Business Panorama: This tab displays the overview of the enterprise data assets and their relationships in a 3D panorama. This allows you to learn the importance of data from the business perspective. Data warehouse administrators and business managers can obtain business-related asset information from this tab. Asset Overview: This tab provides an asset dashboard that displays asset statistics from different dimensions for enterprise managers. Data warehouse administrators, business managers, and data asset administrators can obtain asset statistics from this tab.

**Business Panorama**

The **Business Panorama** tab displays all published data assets in the current workspace and other workspaces that are managed in the same asset space in a 3D panorama. On this tab, you can perform the following operations: View the number of assets, relationships among assets, and asset details. Search for data assets by using keywords to accurately locate the data assets in the 3D panorama. Learn the positions of data assets in the panorama. Adjust the display granularity and layout of the panorama. The smaller the percentage, the more detailed the asset information. Select the types and directories of the data assets to be displayed in the panorama. By default, all types of assets and directories are displayed. The **Asset Overview** tab displays the core metrics of all published data assets in the current workspace and other workspaces that are managed in the same asset space from different dimensions, such as the asset directory and asset type. You can also view the rankings of popular assets, newly published assets, and newly updated assets. On this tab, you can perform the following operations: View the following core metrics for a specific date:

**Note**

The statistics on the published data assets until the specified date are collected. By default, the statistics on the published data assets until the previous day are collected. The statistics on unpublished data assets are not collected. You can query and view a data asset only after the data asset is published. The total number of data assets and the number of data assets of each type. The data assets added in the previous month of different types. The week-on-week and month-on-month trends of data assets of different types. View the following asset trends: The accumulated number of published data assets until now, and the week-on-week and month-on-month trends of data assets. The number of data assets whose status changes from **Unpublished** to **Published** in the current month, and the week-on-week and month-on-month trends of the change. The accumulated data assets of a specific asset type in a specific cycle and the change trend. View the directories to which the data assets of a specific type are mounted and the published and updated data assets of this type. View the view ranking of data assets of a specific type in the previous month. You can unpublish the data assets with low views. For more information about how to unpublish data assets, see Manage data assets. Click **Download** in the upper-right corner to download the asset overview report in PDF format.

#### Search for data assets

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks provides the asset marketplace that allows business staff of enterprises to search for data assets in a more efficient and secure way and consume data assets. This topic describes how to search for data assets on the Asset market page.

**Limits**

DataWorks collects statistics on all published data assets in workspaces that are managed in an asset space. Unpublished data assets are not displayed on the Asset market page. For more information about how to publish data assets, see Manage data assets.

**Go to the Asset market page**

1. Go to the Data Asset page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click the
icon to go to the **Asset market** page. On the Asset market page, you can search for data assets in the directory tree of data assets or by keyword and then consume the data assets. You can search for data assets on the Asset market page by using one of the following methods:

**Method 1**

Find the data assets that you want to use in the directory tree of data assets level by level, and specify filter conditions such as asset type, asset tag, and asset owner to filter data assets.

**Method 2**

Search for data assets by keyword. In the search results, you can filter data assets by specifying filter conditions such as asset type, asset tag, and asset owner.

**Note**

Fuzzy match is supported when you search for data assets by keyword. If you enter a keyword in the search box, data assets whose names contain the keyword are displayed. After you find the required data asset, you can view the asset details and apply for the required permissions to perform operations such as data analysis on the data asset.

**Note**

You can apply for permissions only on MaxCompute physical tables and models that have been published to the production environment. For more information about asset analysis, see Consume data assets.

#### View asset values

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks allows you to evaluate the values of your data assets of different types in different asset directories. This helps asset administrators make an inventory of data assets and business staff use data assets in a reasonable manner. This topic describes the information displayed on the Asset Value page and the operations that you can perform on your data assets on this page.

**Go to the Asset Value page**

1. Go to the Data Assets page.
icon in the left-side navigation pane to go to the
**Asset Value** page.
On the Asset Value page, you can view the overview, rankings, and details of your asset values. You can learn more about the values of your data assets at different granularities. For example, you can view the total value of your data assets or the value of a single data asset. Then, you can perform operations on your data assets. For example, you can unpublish low-value data assets or use high-value data assets. On the Asset Value page, you can view the total asset value of the current workspace, the asset value trend in the specified period, and the rankings of asset values. This helps asset administrators make an inventory of assets and adjust asset structures, and promotes business staff to consume assets in a reasonable manner. On the Asset Value page, you can perform the following operations: View the total asset value and average asset value in the specified period in the current workspace, and compare the asset values with those of the last month or last year. View the rankings of asset values. This helps you find high-value data assets. View the distribution of asset values. This helps you understand the distribution of value scores for data assets of different types in different asset directories. View the detailed asset value for each data asset. You can filter data assets based on conditions such as the statistical period and the directory to which data assets belong. For more information about how to consume data assets, see Consume data assets. For more information about how to unpublish data assets, see Manage data assets.

#### Consume data assets

The **Data Asset** module of DataWorks supports the asset consumption feature. The feature allows data consumers such as business staff in operations, products, and sales departments and data warehouse developers to analyze data on which they have permissions. The asset consumption feature allows you to query and download table data without the need to write any code. This topic describes how to consume data assets.

**Go to the Asset consumption page**

1. Go to the Data Asset page.
2. On the Data Asset page, click the
icon in the left-side navigation pane to go to the **Asset**
**consumption** page.
On the Asset consumption page, you can analyze data assets on which you have permissions, query analysis results, and download the analysis results to your computer.

**Note**

You can analyze only MaxCompute physical tables and models that have been published as MaxCompute physical tables. On the **Asset consumption** page, you can create an analysis file to query and analyze data assets on which you have permissions, and download the analysis results as Excel files to your computer.
1. Create an analysis file.
i. On the Asset consumption page, click **Create Analysis File** in the upper-right corner. ii. Enter a name for the analysis file. Select the source tables and fields that you want to analyze, and specify filter conditions.

**Note**

You can filter only partition fields. iii. Configure the **File Name** and **Remarks** parameters in the Basic information section, and click **Save and Run**. You can save the analysis file or save and run the analysis file based on your business requirements.
2. View and download the analysis results.
You can filter analysis files by file name, source table, or asset directory to view the execution status and execution time of a specific data asset analysis file. You can also download the analysis results as Excel files to your computer.

#### Use the management center

##### Manage asset directories

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks allows you to manage asset directories in
**Management Center**. You can create custom asset directories for your data assets. This
helps you design asset directories and prepare for asset inventorying. This topic describes how to manage asset directories.

**Background information**

Defining asset directories is the first step in using data assets. After asset directories are defined, data assets can be mounted to the corresponding asset directories when the data assets are published. This helps data asset administrators better understand the distribution of data assets and helps data asset consumers find the required data assets.

**Limits**

Only **project administrators** and **project owners** can create, edit, and delete asset directories. Members in a workspace can view all asset directories that are created in the workspace. If you want to manage asset directories, you must contact the administrator to assume the corresponding role. For more information, see Manage workspace members and roles.

**Go to the Directory Management page**

1. Go to the Data Assets page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, move the pointer over the
**Management**.
On the Directory Management page, you can create custom asset directories and manage the asset directories. Only **project administrators** and **project owners** can create, edit, and delete asset directories. Members in a workspace can view all asset directories that are created in the workspace. If you want to manage asset directories, you must contact the administrator to assume the corresponding role. For more information, see Manage workspace members and roles. On the **Directory Management** page, click **Edit** in the upper-right corner. Then, you can customize the structure of asset directories based on your business requirements.

**Create and edit asset directories**

Create asset directories and specify the attributes of the directories. Click the icon to create a subdirectory in the current directory. You can create up to three levels of subdirectories. Click the icon to modify the name of the current directory or delete the directory.

**Note**

If a data asset is mounted to a directory, you must unmount the data asset from the directory before you delete the directory. For more information, see Manage data assets. You must be a member of the current workspace before you can be an asset owner. An asset owner must be a member of the current workspace. For more information about how to add a workspace member, see Manage workspace members and roles. Drag a directory to modify the position of the directory. You can batch delete multiple abandoned directories or modify the responsible persons of multiple directories.

**What to do next**

After asset directories are created, you can go to the Asset Management page to mount data assets to the directories. For more information, see Manage data assets.

##### Manage data assets

| Operation | References |
|---|---|
| Models and metrics are submitted. | - |
| MaxCompute physical tables are published to the production environment. | MaxCompute physical tables can be published in multiple ways. |
| Local files are uploaded to Alibaba Cloud Object Storage Service (OSS) buckets. | Upload files to OSS buckets Configure OSS-related information |
| Asset directories are created. Published data assets must be mounted to directories. | Manage asset directories |

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks allows you to manage your data assets in
**Management Center** based on your business requirements. For example, you can publish
data assets that have been imported. Only published data assets can be viewed on the Asset Overview page and consumed on the Asset Marketplace page. This topic describes how to manage data assets. In this example, data assets of the model type are used. After model or metrics are submitted, or MaxCompute physical tables are published to the production environment, these data assets are automatically imported into DataWorks. After an asset administrator publishes the data assets, you can view or consume the data assets on pages such as the Asset Overview and Asset Marketplace pages. You can manage data assets only after they are imported into DataWorks.

**Note**

If you want to manage MaxCompute physical tables as data assets, the MaxCompute physical tables must have been published to the production environment. Only administrators and developers can publish data assets. Data assets that can be managed include but are not limited to data assets that are created by members of the current workspace in each module of DataWorks. You can manage data assets of multiple types, such as models, metrics, MaxCompute physical tables, and OSS objects.

**Go to the Asset Management page**

1. Go to the Data Assets page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, move the pointer over the
**Management**.
On the Asset Management page, you can manage your data assets, such as publishing and unpublishing data assets. On the **Asset Management** page, you can publish and unpublish data assets, and modify the directories to which the data assets are mounted based on your business requirements.

**Operation types**

DataWorks allows you to **perform operations on a single data asset** or **perform**
**operations on multiple data assets at a time**.
**View asset details**: You can filter data assets by using filter conditions such as the
name or source service. You can click the name of a data asset to go to the details page and view details of the data asset.

**Note**

The filter conditions vary based on the types of data assets. The filter conditions on the actual page prevail. Fuzzy match is supported for data asset names. You can enter a keyword to search for all data assets whose names contain the keyword.
**Publish data assets**: You can view and use data assets on the Asset Overview and
Asset Marketplace pages only after the data assets are published.

**Note**

When you publish data assets, you must mount the asserts to asset directories. Then, you can search for data assets by asset directory. For more information about how to create an asset directory, see Manage asset directories.
**Unpublish data assets**: You cannot use data assets after they are unpublished. Proceed
with caution.
**Modify the directory to which a data asset is mounted** : You can mount a published
data asset to another directory.

##### Configure an asset space

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks allows you to configure an asset space in
**Management Center**. This helps data asset administrators specify the management scope
of data assets. If you want to manage only data assets that are generated in the current workspace, you do not need to use this feature. If you want to manage the data assets that are generated in the current workspace and other workspaces, you can use this feature to modify the scope of data assets. This topic describes how to configure an asset space.

**Background information**

A tenant may have multiple workspaces. DataWorks allows you to manage multiple workspaces within one asset space. Then, you can collect asset data from the managed workspaces to the asset space for use.

**Limits**

Only **project administrators** and **project owners** can modify configurations of an asset space. If you want to modify an asset space, you must be granted the required permissions. For more information, see Manage workspace members and roles.

**Go to the Asset Space page**

1. Go to the Data Assets page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, move the pointer over the
icon and select **Asset Space**. On the Asset Space page, you can modify the workspaces that can be managed in an asset space and view the change records. By default, only the current workspace is managed in an asset space. If you want to manage data assets that are generated in the current workspace and other workspaces, you can add the workspaces to an asset space. You can also view the change records of an asset space. In the **Asset Space Configuration** section, click **Modify**. Then, add workspaces to or delete workspaces from the asset space.

**Note**

Only the workspaces whose **project administrators** or **project owners** belong to the current tenant can be added to an asset space.

**View the change records of an asset space**

Each time you modify the configurations of an asset space, a change record is generated. You can view information about the asset space such as the change operations and the users who perform the operations.

**What to do next**

After an asset space is configured, you can go to the Asset Collection page to collect information about data assets. For more information, see Collect information about data assets.

##### Collect information about data assets

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks allows you to collect information about data assets in
**Management Center**. This helps asset administrators collect information about file assets in
workspaces to an asset space to manage and use the file assets in a centralized manner. This topic describes how to collect information about file assets. An asset space is configured. DataWorks allows you to collect information about data assets only from workspaces that are managed in an asset space. For more information, see Configure an asset space.

**Limits**

To manage file assets, you must configure the account and endpoint used to access the files on the Asset Collection page.

**Go to the Asset Collection page**

1. Go to the Data Assets page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, move the pointer over the
**Collection**.
3. Configure OSS-related information.
If you want to import and publish file assets in DataWorks, you must configure the account and Object Storage Service (OSS) endpoint used to collect information about the file assets. The file assets can be imported and published only after the information about the file assets is collected. i Click**Configure** i. Click **Configure**. ii. Configure OSS-related information.

**What to do next**

After the information about file assets is collected, you can go to the Asset Management page to import and publish the file assets. For more information, see Manage data assets.

### Approval Center

#### Overview

The DataWorks Approval Center feature is used to manage permissions on data and manage high-risk operations. You can use this feature to specify the scope of requests and customize request processing procedures to meet the request processing requirements of your enterprise in different compliance scenarios. When you develop and manage data in DataWorks, you can manage permissions on table data and data service APIs in an efficient manner. You can use the default permission requesting and processing procedure in **Security Center** or customize permission processing procedures in **Approval Center**. When a user submits a request for specific permissions after you create a custom request processing procedure, DataWorks checks whether the permissions in the request hit the custom request processing procedure. If the custom request processing procedure is hit, the request is processed based on the procedure. You can perform the following operations in DataWorks **Approval Center**: Customize a request processing policy: You can specify the scope of requests and customize request processing procedures to manage permissions on key data sources and manage high-risk operations. In addition, you can configure notification methods such as text messages, emails, or DingTalk chatbots. Process requests: The user who submits or processes the request can approve or reject the request in Approval Center. For more information about how to configure request processing policies, see Approval policies for MaxCompute data, Approval policies for data services, and Create a request processing policy for Data Integration nodes. After custom request processing policies are configured, you can process the requests for permissions on tables and APIs, functions, and service orchestration in DataService Studio based on the policies. For more information, see the Requesting and processing procedure for permissions on table fields, Requesting and processing procedure for permissions on data services, and Processing procedure for permissions on Data Integration nodes sections of this topic.

**Requesting and processing procedure for permissions on table**

**fields**

The following figure shows the request processing procedure after a custom request processing policy is configured in **Approval Center** and an applicant submits a request for the permissions on table fields in **Security Center**. In Security Center, when a user submits a request for the permissions on a specific field in a MaxCompute table, DataWorks determines the type of request processing procedure based on the field. If the field on which the user requests permissions belongs to the data range that is specified in a custom request processing procedure, the request is processed based on the custom request processing procedure in Approval Center. If the field on which the user requests permissions is out of the data range that is specified in a custom request processing procedure, the request is processed based on the default request processing procedure in Security Center. If the request hits multiple custom request processing policies in Approval Center, DataWorks selects one custom request processing policy based on the value of the Priority of Policy for Tables parameter. When you configure a custom request processing policy, you can specify the data range to which the custom request processing policy applies based on a project or the sensitivity level and category of the data on which you request permissions. You can also configure information such as the approver and notification method. You can decide whether to determine the data range based on a project or the data sensitivity level and category based on your business requirements. For more information, see Approval policies for MaxCompute data.

**Requesting and processing procedure for permissions on APIs,**

**functions, and service orchestration in DataService Studio**

After a custom request processing procedure is created for DataService Studio, the custom request processing procedure is triggered if a specific operation is performed on an API, function, or service orchestration that is managed by the procedure. The following figure shows the request processing procedure after an applicant submits a request for the required permissions in **Security Center**. When a user performs a specific operation on an API, function, or service orchestration in DataService Studio, DataService Studio determines whether to use a custom request processing procedure to process the request based on whether you configured the custom procedure for the workspace in which the operation is performed. If you configured the custom procedure for the workspace in which the operation is performed, the request is processed based on the custom request processing procedure. If you did not configure the custom procedure for the workspace in which the operation is performed, the user can perform operations on APIs, functions, or service orchestration in DataService Studio without the need to request permissions. After you configure a custom request processing procedure, DataWorks processes a request by using the default or custom request processing procedure based on whether the request hits the custom request processing procedure. When you configure a custom request processing policy, you can specify the data range to which the custom request processing policy applies based on a project. You can also configure information such as the approver and notification method. For more information, see Approval policies for data services.

**Processing procedure for permissions on Data Integration**

Approval Center allows administrators to determine the Data Integration nodes on which the operation permissions must be processed based on a combination of **a source and a**
**destination**. For example, users can request permissions to save a node on the Data
Integration or DataStudio page. In a custom request processing policy that is configured for a Data Integration node, an administrator specifies the **mysql_1** data source as a source and the **odps_1** data source as a destination. When a developer saves the node, the custom request processing procedure is triggered. The developer can proceed to the save operation only after the required permissions are granted to the developer in Security Center. The following figure shows the request processing procedure after an applicant submits a request for the required permissions in **Security Center**. When a user saves a Data Integration node on the DataStudio or Data Integration page, Approval Center determines how to process the request based on whether you configured a custom request processing procedure for the workspace in which the operation is performed. If you configured the custom procedure for the workspace in which the operation is performed, the request is processed based on the custom request processing procedure. If you did not configure the custom procedure for the workspace in which the operation is performed, the user can save the node without the need to request permissions. After a custom request processing procedure is configured, DataWorks determines whether a request is processed by using the default or custom request processing procedure based on whether the request hits the custom request processing procedure. When you configure a custom request processing policy, you can specify a workspace and add a source and a destination as a combination to the workspace to determine the Data Integration nodes on which the operation permissions must be processed based on the custom request processing policy. You can also configure information such as the approver and notification method. For more information, see Create a request processing policy for Data Integration nodes.

#### Create and manage approval policies

##### Request processing policies for compute

**engine data**

You can customize request processing procedures for MaxCompute tables, resources, and functions.

**Background information**

You can specify the data scope to which a request processing procedure applies based on a
**MaxCompute project** or the **category and sensitivity level of data in Data Security**
**Guard**. For more information, see the Specify the data scope section in this topic.

**Limits**

Only workspace administrators and the Resource Access Management (RAM) users to which the **AliyunDataWorksFullAccess** policy is attached can create and manage request processing policies. Only DataWorks Enterprise Edition and Ultimate Edition allow you to configure request processing policies for MaxCompute data.

**Create a request processing policy**

1. Log on to the DataWorks console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > More > Approval**
**Center**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane of the Approval Center page, choose **Policies > Compute**
**Engine**.
On the page that appears, you can view a list of created request processing policies and edit and delete the request processing policies.
4. Click **Create Policy** in the upper-right corner. On the Create Policy page, configure the
parameters as required.

**Enter the basic information**

Configure the **Policy Name** and **Purpose** parameters based on your business scenario to which the request processing policy applies.

**Specify the data scope**

You must specify the data scope to which the request processing policy applies based on your business scenario. After the request processing policy is created, the requests for the permissions on the data in this data scope must be processed based on this request processing policy. For a MaxCompute compute engine, you can specify the data scope of a request processing policy in a workspace based on a MaxCompute project or the category and sensitivity level of data in Data Security Guard. When you specify the data scope, take note of the following items: Specify the data range based on a MaxCompute project You must select an appropriate MaxCompute project from the **MaxCompute Project** drop-down list. This way, when requests for the permissions on the tables in this MaxCompute project are submitted, this request processing policy is used to process the requests. A MaxCompute project can be associated with only one MaxCompute project-based request processing policy. Otherwise, a policy conflict error is reported. You can select a MaxCompute project in which the current account assumes the administrator or super administrator role. If no MaxCompute project is displayed in the drop-down list, the current account may not have the required permissions. In this case, you must use an account that is assigned the Admin or Super_Administrator role.

**Note**

A DataWorks administrator is assigned the role_project_admin role in a DataWorks workspace, but not the Admin or Super_Administrator role in the MaxCompute project that you associate with the DataWorks workspace. To check the role of the current account, run the `whoami` command on the DataStudio page in DataWorks to obtain the account information. Then, run the `show grants for <Your current account>` command to check whether the current account is assigned the Admin or Super_Administrator role in the MaxCompute project. Specify the data scope based on data classification in Data Security Guard You must select the category and sensitivity level of data from the **Select Data**
**Security Level** drop-down list. This way, when requests for the permissions on the
tables of the selected data category and sensitivity level are submitted, this request processing policy is used to process the requests. A data sensitivity level can be associated with only one request processing policy that is based on the data category and sensitivity level. Otherwise, a policy conflict error is reported. You can specify the data scope by using an Apsara Stack account or as a RAM user. If you specify the data scope as a RAM user, the following conditions must be met: The **AdministratorAccess** policy is attached to the RAM user. The RAM user is granted the **AliyunDataWorksFullAccess** permission and assigned the Project Owner or Super_Administrator role of all MaxCompute projects.

**Configure the notification methods**

Three notification methods are supported: text messages, emails, and DingTalk chatbots. After you configure the notification methods, notifications are sent to approvers based on the configured notification methods when a permission request is submitted for processing.

**Note**

In the Configure Processing Links step, you can specify an approver on each request processing node. To ensure that the approvers can receive notifications by using a DingTalk chatbot, select **Custom Keywords** when you configure the **Security Settings** parameter in the Add Robot dialog box. Then, enter **DataWorks** in the Custom Keywords field. Make sure that the other check boxes are **cleared** when you configure the Security Settings parameter. If you do not add DataWorks as a custom keyword or you select other check boxes when you set the Security Settings parameter, the processing personnel cannot receive notifications by using the DingTalk chatbot.

**Configure the request processing nodes**

When you configure the request processing nodes, take note of the following items: The request processing nodes are sequentially connected. After you configure the request processing policy, the processing process specified in the request processing policy sequentially flows from node to node. After an approver on a request processing node approves the request, the approver on the next request processing node receives a notification and then starts request processing. You can specify different roles as approvers on different request processing nodes. If you set the scope type to **MaxCompute Project**, the following roles of approvers are supported: **DataWorks Workspace Role**, **DataWorks Workspace Member**, **Table**
**Owner**, **Alibaba Cloud Account**, and **MaxCompute Role**.
If you set the scope type to **Data Security Level in Data Security Guard**, the following roles of approvers are supported: **DataWorks Workspace Role**, **Table Owner**, and
**Alibaba Cloud Account**.

**Note**

DataWorks sends notifications to each approver based on the configured notification methods when a permission request is submitted for processing. If multiple users who assume the same role are specified as approvers on a request processing node, notifications are sent to all the approvers. In this case, if one of the approvers on the request processing node approves the request, the request is forwarded to the next request processing node.

**Set priorities for request processing policies**

If both a MaxCompute project-based request processing policy and a request processing policy that is based on the category and sensitivity level of data in Data Security Guard are configured, a specific data scope may hit both types of request processing policies. In this case, you can set priorities for the two types of request processing policies.

##### Request processing policies for Data

**Integration nodes**

DataWorks allows users who are assigned the Workspace Administrator role to configure request processing policies for saving Data Integration nodes in workspaces. This topic describes how to create a request processing policy for Data Integration nodes.

**Background information**

Approval Center allows a user who is assigned the Workspace Administrator role to use a combination of **a source and a destination** to specify the Data Integration nodes on which the operation requests must be processed. The operations that trigger request processing include the operation of saving a node on the Data Integration or DataStudio page. For example, in a request processing policy that is configured for Data Integration nodes, a user who is assigned the Workspace Administrator role specifies the **mysql_1** data source as a source and the **odps_1** data source as a destination. When a developer saves a node that matches the specified source and destination, the request processing procedure is triggered. The developer can proceed to the save operation only after the request is approved in Approval Center.

**Limits**

You have permissions to manage all workspaces only if you log on to the DataWorks console by using an Alibaba Cloud account or as a Resource Access Management (RAM) user to which the **AliyunDataWorksFullAccess** policy is attached. The request processing policy that you create takes effect only for workspaces on which you have management permissions. A user who is assigned the **Workspace Administrator** role can manage only workspaces to which the user belongs. The request processing policy that the user creates takes effect only for workspaces to which the user belongs.

**Usage notes**

To use this feature, you must install `v3.18r-SZF-base-hotfeature-SP003 HotFeature` .

**Create a request processing policy**

1. Go to the page on which you can create request processing policies for Data Integration
nodes. i. Log on to the DataWorks console. ii. Click the icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > More > Approval**
**Center**.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane of the Approval Center page, choose **Policies > Data**
**Integration**.
On the Data Integration page, you can view a list of created request processing policies, and perform operations such as modifying or deleting request processing policies.
2. On the Data Integration page, click **Create Policy** in the upper-right corner and configure
the parameters in the Create Policy wizard.

**Enter the basic information**

Configure the **Policy Name** and **Purpose** parameters based on your business scenario to which the request processing policy applies.

**Specify the data range**

You must specify the data range to which the request processing policy applies based on your business scenario. You can determine the Data Integration nodes on which the operation requests must be processed based on a combination of **a source and a destination** . After the request processing policy is configured and takes effect, the request processing procedure is triggered when a developer saves a node that matches the specified source and destination. The developer can proceed to the save operation only after the request is approved in Approval Center. When you specify the data range, take note of the following items: You can select multiple workspaces.

**Note**

You have permissions to manage all workspaces only if you log on to the DataWorks console by using an Alibaba Cloud account or as a RAM user to which the **AliyunDataWorksFullAccess** policy is attached. The request processing policy that you create takes effect only for workspaces on which you have management permissions. A user who is assigned the **Workspace Administrator** role can manage only workspaces to which the user belongs. The request processing policy that the user creates takes effect only for workspaces to which the user belongs. You can click **Add** to add a combination of a source and a destination for a specific workspace. To add multiple combinations of sources and destinations for the workspace, repeat the add operation.

**Configure the notification methods**

The following four notification methods are supported: text message, email, DingTalk chatbot, and webhook. After you configure the notification methods, notifications are sent to approvers based on the configured notification methods when a permission request is submitted for processing.

**Note**

You need to only configure notification methods in this section. You can configure approvers when you configure request processing nodes in the next step. To ensure that the approvers can receive notifications by using a DingTalk chatbot, select
**Custom Keywords** when you configure the **Security Settings** parameter in the Add
Robot dialog box. Then, enter **DataWorks** in the Custom Keywords field. Make sure that the other check boxes are **cleared** when you configure the Security Settings parameter. If you do not add DataWorks as a custom keyword or you select other check boxes when you configure the Security Settings parameter, the approvers cannot receive notifications by using the DingTalk chatbot.

**Configure request processing nodes**

You can specify an approver and a role for the approver on each request processing node in the **Configure Processing Links** step. When you configure the request processing nodes, take note of the following items: Request processing procedure: After a request processing procedure is configured, a permission request is forwarded to the approvers that you specified on the request processing nodes in sequence. The next approver can receive a request processing notification and process the permission request only after the current approver approves the permission request. Approver: You can specify the following types of entities as approvers on the request processing nodes: **DataWorks workspace-level role**, **DataWorks workspace member**,
**table owner**, **Alibaba Cloud account**, and **MaxCompute role**.

**Note**

DataWorks sends notifications to each approver based on the configured notification methods when a permission request is submitted for processing. If multiple users that assume the same role are specified as approvers on a request processing node, notifications are sent to all the approvers. In this case, if one of the approvers on the request processing node approves the request, the request is forwarded to the next request processing node.

**Enable or disable a request processing policy**

After you create a request processing policy, you can click **Apply** or **Stopped** in the Actions column of the policy to enable or disable the policy. After the request processing policy is disabled, the save operation that is performed on a node on the DataStudio or Data Integration page does not trigger the request processing procedure. You can also click View, Edit, or Delete in the Actions column of a request processing policy to view, edit, or delete the policy.

**What to do next**

You can view the requests that are waiting to be processed by your account and process the requests. For more information, see Process and view applications. You can also view historical processing records on the Processing Records page.

#### Process and view applications

You can view all applications submitted by the current account and the applications that are approved and to be approved by the current account in DataWorks Approval Center. On the **Application Records** page, you can view all applications submitted by the current account. You can filter application records based on **Effective Scope** and **Submitted At**. On the **Requests To Be Processed** page, you can view all applications to be approved by the current account. Find an application that you want to process and click **Process** in the upper-right corner. In the dialog box that appears, confirm the information, enter your comments, and then determine whether to approve or reject the application. On the **Processing Records** page, you can view all applications that are approved by the current account. You can filter approval records based on **Effective Scope**, **Submitted**
**At**, and **Initiated By**.

## DataAnalysis

### Overview

DataAnalysis provides the features of building and sharing workbooks, dimension tables, and visual reports. These features help developers and business personnel analyze data.

**Benefits**

Compared with offline data analysis, DataAnalysis has the following benefits: High efficiency: DataAnalysis analyzes data in a database by using online data analysis tools, such as pivot tables. For example, in a user profile table, you can create a pivot table for a partition that belongs to September. When data for October is obtained, you can update the source data and reuse the configuration of the pivot table for September to obtain a pivot table for October. This avoids repeated operations. High capacity: DataAnalysis efficiently analyzes large amounts of data with the help of compute engines. Data sharing: DataAnalysis can analyze data obtained from the databases of different business systems. DataAnalysis allows you to export data to MaxCompute tables. It also allows you to share data with specified members and grant them access permissions. This way, data can be shared between different systems and different users. High security: DataAnalysis allows you to analyze data online without the need to download data. It also allows you to manage the permissions that allow users to analyze and share data. Workbooks are the core feature of DataAnalysis. A workbook is a workspace in which you can obtain, explore, and analyze data. A workbook is in the form of an online table and offers common table features. After you import data from data sources or import local data to workbooks, you can perform data pivoting and profiling. The dimension table feature allows you to create MaxCompute tables without the need to write SQL code. It also allows you to collaboratively edit MaxCompute tables with other users online. The dimension table feature also allows you to import data to MaxCompute tables in a visualized manner. For more information, see Create and manage dimension tables. You can create and design visual reports by dragging and configuring controls without the need to execute SQL statements.

### SQL queries

DataWorks allows you to import data from a data source and perform queries and analysis of data by using the SQL query feature. This topic describes how to use the SQL query feature.

**Create an SQL query task**

1. Go to the DataAnalysis page.
i. Log in to the DataWorks console.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | The type of the data source that you want to query. |
| Workspace | The workspace in which the specified data source resides. |
| Data Source | The data source that you want to query. Note If you set the Type parameter to MaxCompute, this parameter is not displayed. |

ii. In the upper-left corner of the console, click the icon and choose **All Products > Data**
**Analysis > DataAnalysis**.
2. On the **DataAnalysis** page, click **SQL Query** in the top navigation bar to go to the **SQL**
**Query** page.
3. Select the data source that you want to query.
i. On the left side of the **SQL Query** page, click the icon in the **Data source** section. The first time you go to the **SQL Query** page, you must click **Add Now** first. ii. In the **Select Datasource** dialog box, configure the parameters.

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 | This section displays the tables that are contained in the data source in the specified workspace. You can also search for a table by entering keywords in the search box. |
| 2 | This section allows you to execute SQL statements to query data. After you enter SQL statements, click the icon in the toolbar to execute the statements. You can also click Go to DataStudio to copy the SQL statements and go to the DataStudio page. On the DataStudio page, you can develop data and schedule extract, transform, and load (ETL) tasks. |
| 3 | This section allows you to view the details of the saved queries, execution history, and logs of SQL queries. You can also preview, load, rename, and delete historical SQL queries on the Saved query tab. |

iii. Click **OK** to create an SQL query task. On the SQL Query page, you can use SQL statements to query and analyze data for the created SQL query task. On the SQL Query page, you can execute SQL statements to query and analyze data from the specified data source. You can also view saved queries, execution history, and logs of the SQL queries.

**Data Profile**

The data profiling feature allows you to analyze the quality, structure, distribution, and statistics of the data. It also allows you to preview, detect, process, analyze, and visualize data. The data profiling feature analyzes data by column and allows you to view the data types and value distribution of each column. Select the data that you want to analyze and click **Data Profile** in the Data Analysis section in the top toolbar. Then, you can view the data types and value distribution of each column at the top of the workbook in the form of charts and rich text. The simple mode of the data profiling feature has the following features: For a column whose values are of the STRING or DATE data type: displays the values that rank top 2 and their respective percentages, and the percentage of other values in the form of rich text. If the number of unique values exceeds 50% of the total number of values, the number of unique values is displayed. For a column whose values are of the INTEGER or FLOAT data type: displays the value distribution in the form of a histogram. For a column whose values are of the BOOLEAN data type: displays the proportions of different values in the form of pie charts. For a column whose values are of two or more data types: displays the proportions of different data types in the form of pie charts. The system reminds you that the current column contains dirty data. After the dirty data is cleared, the simple mode displays value distribution in one of the preceding forms based on the data type. For a column whose values are null values: displays the percentage of the null values in red. Click **Detailed Mode** in the upper-right corner. In the **Data Profile** dialog box, you can view the profiling result of each column. The profiling result information includes the column name, value distribution information, data type, and data source. The detailed mode of the data profiling feature has the following features: For a column whose values are of the STRING or DATE data type: displays basic information and the values that rank top 5 based on frequency. The basic information includes the number of fields, unique values, valid values, and the percentage of null values. For a column whose values are of the INTEGER or FLOAT data type: displays basic information, the values that rank top 5 based on frequency, statistics, and a histogram. The basic information includes the number of fields, unique values, zeros, and the percentage of null values. For a column whose values are of the BOOLEAN data type: displays basic information, the values that rank top 5 based on frequency, and a pie chart. The basic information includes the number of fields, unique values, zeros, and the percentage of null values.

**Note**

The system considers the **true** and **false** strings and the 0 and 1 integers as values of the BOOLEAN data type.

## Data Service

### Overview

DataWorks DataService Studio aims to build a data service bus to help enterprises centrally manage private and public APIs. DataService Studio allows you to create APIs based on data tables. You can also register existing APIs to DataService Studio for centralized management. DataService Studio and API Gateway are interconnected. This allows you to publish APIs to API Gateway with ease. DataService Studio works together with API Gateway to provide a secure, stable, costeffective, and easy-to-use data sharing service. DataService Studio adopts a serverless architecture. This allows you to focus on the query logic of an API without worrying about the infrastructure, such as computing resources. DataService Studio supports automatic scaling for computing resources, which significantly reduces your O&M costs. DataService Studio allows you to create APIs based on tables in relational databases and NoSQL databases. You can create an API in the codeless user interface (UI) within a few minutes without the need to write code. For more information about how to create an API, see Create an API by using the codeless UI. DataService Studio also allows you to create an API in the code editor. You can write SQL statements to customize the query logic of the API. In the code editor, you can specify multitable join queries, complex query criteria, and aggregate functions. For more information, see Create an API in the code editor. You can register existing RESTful APIs to DataService Studio to manage them together with the APIs that are created in DataService Studio based on tables. Four request methods and three data formats are supported. The four request methods are GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE. The three data formats are tables, JSON, and XML.

**API Gateway**

API Gateway provides API lifecycle management services, including API publishing, management, maintenance, and monetization. It provides a simple, fast, cost-effective, and low-risk service for you to aggregate microservices, separate the frontend from the backend, integrate systems, and provide features and data to partners and developers. Being integrated with API Gateway, DataService Studio allows you to publish APIs to API Gateway conveniently. Both APIs that you create based on data tables and APIs that you register to DataService Studio can be published to API Gateway for management, for example, for authorization, authentication, throttling, and billing.

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Data source | Indicates database links. Data Service accesses data through data sources. Data sources are configured in Data Integration. |
| Create an API | Creates APIs based on data tables. |
| Register an API | Registers existing APIs to Data Service for unified management. |
| Wizard mode | Guides you through the procedure of API creation. This method is suitable for beginners who want to create simple APIs. You do not need to write any code. |
| Script mode | Allows you to create APIs by writing SQL scripts. This method supports associative tables, complex queries, and aggregate functions. This method is suitable for experienced developers who want to create complex APIs. |
| API group | Indicates a set of APIs for a specific scenario or for consuming a specific service. An API group is the smallest group unit in Data Service, and the smallest unit for API Gateway management. API groups are published in Alibaba Cloud API Marketplace as API products. |
| API Gateway | Indicates a hosted service provided by Alibaba Cloud to manage APIs. API Gateway supports API lifecycle management, permission management, access management, and traffic control. |

###### Create an API by using the codeless UI

DataWorks allows you to use the codeless user interface (UI) to create APIs. When you use the codeless UI to create an API, you do not need to write code. You only need to configure the parameters. This topic describes how to use the codeless UI to create an API.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| API Mode | The mode used to create the API. Valid values: Wizard Mode and Script Mode. In this example, Wizard Mode is selected. |
| API Name | The name of the API. The name must be 4 to 50 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). The name must start with a letter. _ |
| API Path | The path of the API, such as /user. |
| Call Mode | The mode used to call the API. Valid values: Synchronous Call and Asynchronous Call. If you set this parameter to Synchronous Call, the API returns results immediately after it is called. The synchronous mode is most commonly used. If you set this parameter to Asynchronous Call, the API returns the request ID immediately after it is called. The API caller can then obtain the call result from a message queue based on the request ID. |
| Protocol | The protocol used by the API. Valid values: HTTP and HTTPS. |
| Request Method | The request method used by the API. Valid values: GET and POST. |

A data source is created on the **All Products > Data Integration > Data Sources** > **Data**
**Sources** page. For more information, see Add a data source.

When you use the code editor to create an API, you can customize SQL statements for the API. The code editor allows you to use features such as table join queries, complex queries, and aggregate functions. For example, if you want to specify a request parameter to query data within a specific value range of a field, you can create an API in the code editor.

Private: The API is visible only to its owner, and permissions on the API cannot be granted to other members. **Configure an API**

1. Double-click the API in the API list. On the tab that appears, configure the **Datasource**
**Type**, **Datasource Name**, **Datasource Environment**, and **Table Name** parameters in
the **Select Table** section. The parameters that you need to configure vary based on the selected data source type. The parameters in the console shall prevail.

**Note**

Before you select a table for an API, you must configure a data source in Data Integration. You can enter a table name in the Table Name field to search for the table that you want to use. For a workspace in standard mode, you can select Production or Environment for the **Datasource Environment** parameter. After you create an API, the API configuration tab appears. Then, you can select a table for the API.
2. In the **Select Parameters** section, configure request and response parameters for the API.
After you select a table in the Select Table section, all fields in the table automatically appear in the **Select Parameters** section. In the **Set as Req Param** column, select the check boxes of the fields that you want to specify as request parameters. In the **Set as**
**Resp Param** column, select the check boxes of the fields that you want to specify as
response parameters. To sort the data that the API returns based on a specific field, find the field and click **Add** in the Add to field sort column. After you click Add, the field is added to the **Sort field** section. The sorting feature allows you to specify the fields based on which the data that the API returns is sorted. A field with a smaller sequence number in the Sort field section has a higher priority in data sorting. You can click **Move up** or **Move down** to adjust the sequence of a field. You can select **Ascending order** or **Descending order** in the Sort column of each field to specify the sorting mode. If you want to display the returned results by page, you can turn on the Pagination for Return Results switch. When you select Pagination option, and take note of the following information: If you do not enable **Pagination for Return Results**, the API returns up to 2,000 records by default. If more than 2,000 records may be returned, we recommend that you enable
**Pagination for Return Results**. If you disable this feature, you can go to the
**Environment Configuration** tab to configure the maximum number of data records
for a single request parameter based on the resource group that you select. The following common parameters are displayed when you enable Pagination for Return Results:
**pageNum**: the page number.
**pageSize**: the number of entries to return on each page.
**pageNum**: the page number.
**pageSize**: the number of entries to return on each page.
**totalNum**: the total number of entries returned.

**Note**

Request parameters are optional for an API. If you do not specify request parameters for an API, you must enable **Pagination for Return Results**.
3. In the right-side navigation pane, click the **Request Param** tab. On the Request Param tab,
configure the parameters based on your business requirements.

**Note**

Before you preview the result, you must configure information such as the example value, default value, and description for each request parameter of the API. To improve the match efficiency, specify an indexed field as a request parameter.

Note If you set the Position parameter to BODY for one or more request parameters, you must configure the Content-Type parameter to define the format of the request parameters in the request body. Valid values of Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8: the JSON format. application/xml; charset=utf-8: the XML format. application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8: the FORM format. |

| Operator | The operator that is used to associate or compare the value of the request parameter with the value that you specify. You can select one of the following operators: Equal: The value of the request parameter is equal to the specified value. LIKE: The value of the request parameter matches the specified pattern. IN: The value of the request parameter is in the specified range. NOT IN: The value of the request parameter is out of the specified range. NOT LIKE: The value of the request parameter does not match the specified pattern. !=: The value of the request parameter is not equal to the specified value. >: The value of the request parameter is greater than the specified value. <: The value of the request parameter is less than the specified value. >=: The value of the request parameter is greater than or equal to the specified value. <=: The value of the request parameter is less than or equal to the specified value. Note If you set the Datasource Type parameter to Table Store in the Select Table section, you can set the Operator parameter only to Equal. |
|---|---|

**Switch from the codeless UI to the code editor**

On the configuration tab of an API, you can switch from the codeless UI to the code editor.
1. Go to the **Service Development** tab and double-click the target API. The configuration tab
of the API appears.
2. Click the
icon in the top toolbar. Select **Switch to Basic SQL** or **Switch to Advanced**
**SQL**.
3. In the message that appears, click **OK**. Then, you can view the SQL statements of the API in
the **Edit Query SQL** section.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| API Mode | The mode that is used to create the API. Valid values: Wizard Mode and Script Mode. In this example, Script Mode is selected. |
| API Name | The name of the API. The name must be 4 to 50 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, and underscores ( ). The name must start with a letter. _ |
| API Path | The path of the API, such as /user. |
| Call Mode | The mode used to call the API. Valid values: Synchronous Call and Asynchronous Call. If you set this parameter to Synchronous Call, the API returns results immediately after it is called. The synchronous mode is most commonly used. If you set this parameter to Asynchronous Call, the API returns the request ID immediately after it is called. The API caller can then obtain the call result from a message queue based on the request ID. |

**Important**

DataService Studio allows you to switch only from the codeless UI to the code editor. After you switch from the codeless UI to the code editor, you cannot switch back to the codeless UI.

To meet the personalized query requirements of advanced users, DataService Studio provides a code editor that you can use to customize the SQL statements of APIs. DataService Studio supports table join queries, complex queries, and aggregate functions. This topic describes how to create an API in the code editor. Data sources are configured on the **Workspace Manage > Data Sources** page. For more information, see Add a data source.

2. In the upper-left corner, click the
**Data Service**.

icon and choose
**Create API > Generate API**.

**API**.

| Protocol | The protocol used by the API. Valid values: HTTP and HTTPS. |
|---|---|
| Request Method | The request method. Valid values: GET and POST. |
| Response Type | The format of the data returned by the API. Set the value toJ SON. |
| Visible Scope | The range of users to whom the API is visible. Valid values: Workspace: The API is visible to all members in the current workspace. Private: The API is visible only to its owner, and permissions on the API cannot be granted to other members. Note If you set this parameter to Private, other members in the workspace cannot view the API in the API list. |
