### FAQ

| Error code | Error message | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | success | The error message returned because the data query has succeeded. |

This topic provides answers to commonly asked questions about DataService Studio. Q: Do I need to activate the API Gateway service? A: API Gateway provides you with high-performance and highly available API hosting services. If you need to make your APIs available to others, activate the API Gateway service first. Q: Where can I add and change connections? A: After you log on to the DataWorks console, click the DataWorks icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > Data Integration** to go to the **Data Integration** page. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Sync Resources > Connections**. On the page that appears, perform the relevant configuration. DataService Studio automatically reads data from the connections that you have configured. Q: What is the role of an API group in DataService Studio? What is the relationship between an API group in DataService Studio and an API group in API Gateway? A: An API group is a set of APIs specific to a feature or scenario. It is the smallest organization unit in DataService Studio, which is similar to an API group in API Gateway. An API group in DataService Studio is equivalent to an API group in API Gateway. After you publish an API from DataService Studio to API Gateway, API Gateway automatically creates an API group with the same name. Q: How can I configure an API group appropriately? A: Typically, an API group includes APIs that provide similar features or resolve a specific issue. For example, a weather API group can include APIs that are used to check the weather by city and by longitude and latitude. Q: How many API groups can I create? A: An Alibaba Cloud account can create up to 100 API groups. Q: When do I need to enable the pagination feature for an API call so that its return results can be displayed on multiple pages? A: By default, an API call returns a maximum of 2,000 records. If an API call may return more than 2,000 records, enable the pagination feature. If you do not specify any request parameters, the API call usually returns a large number of records and the pagination feature is automatically enabled. Q: Do APIs created by DataService Studio support POST requests? A: APIs created by DataService Studio support GET and POST requests. Q: Do APIs created by DataService Studio support the HTTPS protocol? A: APIs created by DataService Studio support both HTTP and HTTPS protocols.

### Appendix: DataService

**Studio error codes**

After DataService Studio receives an API request, it returns a response that contains an error code. You can locate and troubleshoot issues based on the error code. This topic describes common error codes that are returned by DataService Studio.

| 1108110583 | query timeout | The error message returned because the query has timed out. The timeout occurs because the total runtime of the API in DataService Studio and the database exceeds the timeout period that is configured for the API. |
|---|---|---|
| 1108110519 | param miss | The error message returned because specific required request parameters are not specified. |
| 1108110584 | api context failed | The error message returned because the system has failed to obtain context information based on the third party. The information includes the connection information of the data source, AccessKey information of the data source, and tenant information. |
| 1108110622 | datasource query error | The error message returned because the system has failed to query the data source. The failure may occur because the SQL syntax is invalid, the data source does not respond within the configured timeout period (10s), or the number of connections to the data source exceeds the upper limit. |
| 1108110703 | database connection error | The error message returned because the data source has failed to be connected. |
| Other error codes | Other error messages | If the response contains an error code other than the preceding error codes, you can consult technical support personnel. |

## Migration Assistant

### Overview

The Migration Assistant service of DataWorks allows you to migrate data objects across different DataWorks versions, Alibaba Cloud accounts, regions, and workspaces. Migration Assistant allows you to export data objects in your workspace, including auto triggered nodes, manually triggered nodes, resources, functions, data sources, table metadata, ad hoc queries, and components. You can create full export tasks, incremental export tasks, or custom export tasks to export your data objects in DataWorks based on your business requirements.

**Important**

To create export or import tasks, you must use an Alibaba Cloud account or be the workspace administrator. If you use a Resource Access Management (RAM) user that is not assigned the administrator role, you can only view export and import tasks. Back up node code You can use Migration Assistant to periodically back up your node code to prevent data from being deleted by mistake. In this case, we recommend that you create a full export task. Export a common workflow for replication You can use Migration Assistant to export a common workflow that can be replicated in other workspaces. In this case, we recommend that you create a custom export task. Build a test environment You can use Migration Assistant to copy all the node code and replace the production data with test data to build a test environment. In this case, we recommend that you create a full export task or a custom export task. Develop data in a hybrid cloud environment You can use Migration Assistant to migrate node code from Alibaba Cloud public cloud to Alibaba Cloud Apsara Stack to develop data in a hybrid cloud environment. We recommend that you create a custom export task. If the difference between Alibaba Cloud public cloud and Alibaba Cloud Apsara Stack is large, a compatibility problem may occur when data objects are migrated. Migrate data objects between the development environment and production environment If a workspace consists of the production environment and development environment that are completely isolated, you can use Migration Assistant to export nodes from the development environment and import them to the production environment for deployment.

### Cloud tasks

#### Export tasks from scheduling engines

DataWorks allows you to migrate tasks from open source scheduling engines, such as Oozie, Azkaban, Airflow, and DolphinScheduler, to DataWorks. This topic describes how to export tasks from open source scheduling engines.

**Background information**

Before you import a task of an open source scheduling engine to DataWorks, you must export the task to your local device or Object Storage Service (OSS).

**Limits**

For Airflow tasks, you can export only tasks of Airflow 1.10.x. In addition, the export of Airflow tasks depends on Python 3.6 or later.

**Export a task from Oozie**

**Export requirements**

The package must contain XML-formatted definition files and configuration files of a task. The package is exported in the ZIP format.

**Structure of the package**

Oozie task descriptions are stored in a Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) directory. For example, on the Apache Oozie official website, each subdirectory under the **apps** directory in the Examples package is a task of Oozie. Each subdirectory contains XML-formatted definition files and configuration files of a task. The following figure shows the structure of an exported package.

| Azkaban item | DataWorks item | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Flow | Workflow in DataStudio | Jobs in a flow are placed in the workflow that corresponds to the flow and used as nodes in the workflow Nested flows in a flow are converted into separate workflows in DataWorks. After the conversion, the dependencies between the nodes in the workflow are automatically established. |

**Export a job from Azkaban**

**Download a flow**

You can download a specific flow in the Azkaban console.
1. Log in to the Azkaban console and go to the **Projects** page.
2. Select a project whose package you want to download. On the project page, click **Flows** to
show all flows of the project.
3. Click **Download** in the upper-right corner of the page to download the package of the
project.

**Note**

The actual product page prevails. Native Azkaban packages can be exported. No format limit is imposed on the packages of Azkaban. The exported package in the ZIP format contains information about all jobs and relationships of a specific project of Azkaban. You can directly upload the ZIP package exported from the Azkaban console to the Scheduling Engine Import in DataWorks.

**Conversion logic**

The following table describes the mappings between Azkaban items and DataWorks items and the conversion logic.

| Command- type job | Shell node | In DataWorks on EMR mode, a command-type job is converted into an E-MapReduce (EMR) Shell node. You can specify the mapped node type by configuring the related parameter in the Advanced Settings dialog box. If you call other scripts in the CLI of a command-type job, the script file obtained after analysis can be registered as a resource file of DataWorks and the resource file is referenced in the converted Shell code. |
|---|---|---|
| Hive-type job | ODPS SQL node | In DataWorks on MaxCompute mode, a Hive-type job is converted into an ODPS SQL node. You can specify the mapped node type by configuring the related parameter in the Advanced Settings dialog box. |
| Other types of nodes that are not supported by DataWorks | Zero load node or Shell node | You can specify the mapped node type by configuring the related parameter in the Advanced Settings dialog box. |

**Export a task from DataGo**

DataWorks allows you to migrate DataGo tasks to DataWorks. The following section describes how to export a task from DataGo.

**Export a DataGo task**

Go to {Datago domain}/index.htm#/deployPackage/deploy and create an export task. You can export the following items: Projects

**Important**

When you export a task, the task information in the publish domain is exported. Therefore, make sure that a task is published in the specified domain before you export the task. When you export a publish package, the latest versions of the tasks that are published to the specified domain are exported. Therefore, the publish domain ID is required when you export a publish package.

**View the publish domain ID**

To view the publish domain ID of a DataGo node, perform the following operations: Go to the DataGo console and refresh the page. Click the Publish Record tab and go to the DevTools panel. In the DevTools panel, click the Network tab. In the Name section, find the listDeployEnvs.json operation and click its name. On the Preview tab, view the publish domain ID of the task that you want to export.

**View the project ID, tenant ID, and workspace ID**

To view the project ID, tenant ID, and workspace ID of a DataGo node, perform the following operations: Go to the DataGo console and refresh the page. Click the Data Development tab and go to the DevTools panel. In the DevTools panel, click the Network tab. In the Name section, find the list.json operation and click its name. On the Headers tab, view the project ID, tenant ID, and workspace ID of the node that you want to export. In the query result, currentTenantId indicates the ID of the tenant, namespaceId indicates the ID of the workspace, and dataProjectId indicates the ID of the project.

**Note**

If you migrate a node to DataWorks, the mapping of the environment variable is unavailable. You can specify the mapping.

**Limits**

You cannot export tables, resources, functions, or data sources. You cannot export the system variables of projects. When you export a node that has cross-workspace dependencies, you must export its ancestor nodes first. Otherwise, node dependencies may be lost.

**Note**

Sync nodes depend on data sources. After you import a sync node, we recommend that you check the configuration of the node.

**Export a task from Airflow**

**Procedure**

1. Go to the runtime environment of Airflow.
2. Use the Python library of Airflow to load the directed acyclic graph (DAG) folder that is
scheduled on Airflow. The DAG Python file is stored in the DAG folder.
3. Use the export tool to read the task information and dependencies stored in the DAG
Python file based on the Python library of Airflow in memory. Then, write the generated DAG information to a JSON file and export the file. You can download the export tool on the **Schemes of Scheduling Engine Export** page of
**Cloud tasks** in DataWorks **Migrant Assistant**. For more information about how to go to
the **Schemes of Scheduling Engine Export** page, see the Export nodes from open source engines section of this topic.

**Usage notes for the export tool**

Perform the following steps to use the export tool:
1. Run the following command to decompress the airflow-exporter.tgz package:

```
tar zxvf airflow-exporter.tgz
```

2. Run the following command to set the PYTHONPATH parameter to the directory of the
Python library:

```
export PYTHONPATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages
```

3. Run the following commands to export the node from Airflow:

```
cd airflow-exporter python3.6 ./parser -d /path/to/airflow/dag/floder/ -o output.json
```

4. Run the following command to compress the exported output.json file into a ZIP package:

```
zip out.zip output.json
```

After the ZIP package is generated, you can perform the following operations to create an import task to import the ZIP package to DataWorks: Go to the **Migrant Assistant** module in the DataWorks console. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Cloud tasks > Scheduling**
**Engine Import**. For more information, see Import tasks into scheduling engines.

**How it works**

The DataWorks export tool obtains the JSON configurations of a process in DolphinScheduler by calling the API operation that is used to export multiple processes from DolphinScheduler at a time. The export tool generates a ZIP file based on the JSON configurations. In the leftside navigation pane of the **Migrant Assistant** page, you can choose **Cloud tasks** > Scheduling Engine Import. On the Import Tasks page, create an import task of the DolphinScheduler type to import the ZIP file. DataWorks Migration Assistant parses and converts code and dependencies of nodes in a process in the ZIP file into valid file configurations for related DataWorks nodes. For information about how to import a task of an open source scheduling engine, see **Import tasks of open source engines** .

**Limits**

**Limits on the version**: Only DolphinScheduler 1.3.x can be used to export
DolphinScheduler tasks.
**Limits on node type conversion**:
SQL nodes: Only some types of compute engines support the conversion of SQL nodes. During the node type conversion, the syntax of SQL code is not converted and the SQL code is not modified. CRON expressions: In specific scenarios, CRON expressions may be pruned or CRON expressions may not be supported. You must check whether the scheduling time that is configured meets your business requirements. Python nodes: DataWorks does not provide Python nodes. DataWorks can convert a Python node in DolphinScheduler into a Python file resource and a Shell node that references the Python file resource. However, issues may occur when scheduling parameters of the Python node are passed. Therefore, debugging and checks are required. Depend nodes: DataWorks cannot convert Depend nodes for which cross-cycle scheduling dependencies are configured. If cross-cycle scheduling dependencies are configured for a Depend node, DataWorks converts the dependencies into the same-cycle scheduling dependencies of the mapped auto triggered node in DataWorks.

**Conversion logic**

The following table describes the mappings between DolphinScheduler items and DataWorks items and the conversion logic.

| DolphinSche duler item | DataWorks item | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Process | Workflows | Nodes in a DolphinScheduler process are converted into nodes in a DataWorks workflow. In addition, zero load nodes used as the start and end nodes in the DataWorks workflow are automatically added. |
| SubProcess node | Zero load node | When a process to which a SubProcess node belongs is converted into a DataWorks workflow, two zero load nodes are added to the workflow. One is used as the start node and the other is used as the end node. The SubProcess node is converted into a zero load node in the DataWorks workflow. The start node depends on the zero load node, and the descendant nodes of the SubProcess node depend on the end node. |
| Conditions node | Merge node | A dependency item and a conditional relation of a Conditions node are converted into a DataWorks merge node and related logic. The outermost logical dependency configured for the Conditions node uses the mapped merge node and another two merge nodes to determine whether a success or failure path is used. Note DataWorks cannot convert Conditions nodes for which cross- cycle scheduling dependencies are configured. If cross-cycle scheduling dependencies are configured for a Conditions node, DataWorks converts the dependencies into the same-cycle scheduling dependencies of the mapped auto triggered node in DataWorks. |

| Depend node | Zero load node | The dependencies of a Depend node are converted into the input of the mapped zero load node based on the scheduling configurations. Concatenation rule for the input of the mapped zero load node: {current dataworks project name}. _ _ _ {dolphin project name}.{dolphin process name}. _ _ _ _ {dolphin task name} _ _ |
|---|---|---|
| SQL Task | Types of the compute engines that support conversion of SQL nodes in DolphinSched uler: HIVE SPARK CLICKHOUS E POSTGRES QL | You can specify the type of mapped compute engine node by configuring the related parameter in the Advanced Settings dialog box of an import node. Note The syntax of SQL code is not converted and the SQL code is not modified. |
| Python node | A Python file resource and a Shell node that references the Python file resource | Issues may occur when scheduling parameters of the Python node are passed. Therefore, debugging and checks are required. |
| MR | EMR MR node ODPS MR CDH MR node | You can specify the type of mapped compute engine node by configuring the related parameter in the Advanced Settings dialog box of an import node. |
| Spark | EMR Spark CDH Spark | You can specify the type of mapped compute engine node by configuring the related parameter in the Advanced Settings dialog box of an import node. |
| Sqoop | Batch synchronizati on node that is configured in script mode | The data sources used for the batch synchronization node vary based on your business requirements. |

| Other types of nodes that are not supported by DataWorks | Zero load node | None |
|---|---|---|

**Environment preparations**

Obtain the download tool on the DolphinScheduler tab of the Scheduling Engine Export page. Dependency settings: Install Java Development Kit (JDK) 1.8 or later, and Python 2.7 or later.

**Export procedure**

1. Decompress the export tool.
Run the following commands to decompress the export tool package:
2. Generate a token used to call DolphinScheduler APIs.
For information about how to generate a token, see DolphinScheduler documentation.
3. Export a ZIP file.
Run the following command to export the required ZIP file:

```
python ./bin/reader.py -a dolphinscheduler -e http://dolphinschedulerhost:port -t tok en -v 1.3.9 -p project_name -f ds_dump.zip
```

After you export the ZIP file, choose **Cloud tasks** > Scheduling Engine Import in the left-side navigation pane of the **Migrant Assistant** page, and create an import task of the DolphinScheduler type to import the ZIP file. DataWorks Migration Assistant parses and converts code and dependencies of nodes in a process in the ZIP file into valid file configurations for related DataWorks nodes. For information about how to import a task of an open source scheduling engine, see **Import tasks of open source engines** .

### Migrate data objects in

**DataWorks**

#### Create and view export tasks

Migration Assistant allows you to export data objects in your workspace, including auto triggered tasks, manually triggered tasks, resources, functions, table metadata, data sources, script templates, and ad hoc queries. This topic describes how to create and view export tasks. An Apsara Stack tenant account or a Resource Access Management (RAM) user to which the Workspace Administrator role is assigned is used. If you use a RAM user to which the Workspace Administrator role is not assigned, you can only view export and import tasks.

**Background information**

Migration Assistant allows you to export data objects in **full export**, **incremental export**, or
**custom export** mode. You can select an export mode based on your business requirements.
**Full export** tasks are used to export all or selected types of data objects in your
workspace. For example, you can use a full export task to back up the code of all nodes in your workspace or clone your workspace for a test environment. When you run a full export task, data objects of the latest version are exported. Only saved data objects can be exported. If a node is saved in both the development environment and production environment, the node saved in the development environment is exported.
**Incremental export** tasks are used to export data objects that were modified after the
specified date.

**Note**

You cannot configure a blacklist for incremental export tasks.
**Custom export** tasks are used to export data objects that you specify. For example, you
can use a custom export task to extract a common workflow. This way, you can clone this workflow to other workspaces. If a workspace runs in both a production environment and a development environment that are completely isolated from each other, you can run a custom export task to export nodes from the development environment and import them to the production environment for deployment.

**Limits**

Migration Assistant can be used to export up to 5,000 metadata records at a time.

**Go to the Export Tasks page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the export task. The name can contain only letters, digits, underscores ( ), and periods (.). _ |
| Type | The type of the export task. Select Full export for this parameter. A full export task is used to export all the auto triggered tasks, manually triggered nodes, table metadata, and data sources that have been saved or committed in the current workspace. |
| Export Scope | The objects that you want to export. Valid values: All Objects: After you select this value, DataWorks exports all types of objects in your workspace, including auto triggered tasks, manually triggered tasks, resources, functions, DDL statements of tables, data sources, data services, ad hoc queries, and script templates. Selected Objects: If you select this option, you can select the types of data objects that you want to export from the Export Object drop- down list. For example, you can select Periodic tasks, Resources, and DATA SERVICE from the Export Object drop-down list. _ |
| Export Object Status | The state of the data objects that you want to export. Valid values: Save: the data objects that are saved. Submit: the data objects that are committed. |
| Blacklist | Specifies whether to enable the blacklist feature for full export based on your business requirements. If you select Add to Blacklist, you can add the nodes and resources that you do not want to export to a blacklist. |
| Export Version | The version of the exported data. Valid values: Standard and Private Cloud(V3.6.1-V3.11). The DataWorks version determines the format in which data objects are exported. Check the DataWorks version of your workspace before you create an export task. |
| Remarks | The description of the export task. |

If you use a RAM user to which the Workspace Administrator role is not assigned, you can only view export and import tasks.

In the **Engine Instance Mapping** section, select a compute engine instance that is associated with the destination workspace to establish a mapping. The system uses this name to replace the original workspace name in the code, input settings, and output settings of the nodes. iv. **Optional**. In the **Dry-run** section, find the node that you want to configure as a dry-run node and click **Set up empty run** in the Actions column. You can also select multiple nodes and click **Batch Configure** to configure these nodes as dry-run nodes. This configuration is used to configure time properties for auto triggered tasks. The system returns a success response for the auto triggered task that is configured as a dryrun node without running the node. The node does not generate data. v. **Optional**. In the **Data service settings** section, configure a mapping between data service business processes. vi. **Optional**: In the **Configure Policy Settings** section, configure an import policy for the object with the same name. vii. **Optional**. based on your business requirements.

## View the asset panorama

The **Data Assets** module of DataWorks provides the asset panorama, which is a convenient data asset inventory tool for enterprise managers. The Business Overview section displays the overview of enterprise data assets and their relationships in a 3D panorama. The Asset Overview section displays the statistics of enterprise data assets from various dimensions to help you learn the status of data assets. This topic describes how to use the asset panorama.

**Limits**

DataWorks collects statistics on all published data assets in the current workspace and other workspaces that are managed in the same asset space. Data assets that are not published are not displayed on the Asset Panorama page. For more information about how to publish data assets, see Manage data assets.

**Go to the Asset Panorama page**

1. Go to the Data Assets page.
icon in the left-side navigation pane to go to the
**Asset Panorama** page.
On the Asset Panorama page, you can view the following information: Business Overview: This section displays the overview of the enterprise data assets and their relationships in a 3D panorama. This allows you to learn the importance of data from the business perspective. Data warehouse administrators and business managers can obtain business-related asset information from this section. Asset Overview: This section provides an asset dashboard that displays asset statistics from different dimensions for enterprise managers. Data warehouse administrators, business managers, and data asset administrators can obtain asset statistics from this section. The **Asset Panorama** section displays all published data assets in the current workspace and other workspaces that are managed in the same asset space in a 3D panorama. In this section, you can perform the following operations: View the number of assets, relationships among assets, and asset details. Search for data assets by using keywords to accurately locate the data assets in the 3D panorama. Learn the positions of data assets in the panorama. Adjust the display granularity and layout of the panorama. The smaller the percentage, the more detailed the asset information. Select the types and directories of the data assets to be displayed in the panorama. By default, all types of assets and directories are displayed. The **Asset Panoramic** section displays the core metrics of all published data assets in the current workspace and other workspaces that are managed in the same asset space from different dimensions, such as the asset directory and asset type. You can also view the rankings of popular assets, newly published assets, and newly updated assets. In this section, you can perform the following operations: View the following core metrics for a specific date: ama

**Note**

The statistics on the published data assets until the specified date are collected. By default, the statistics on the published data assets until the previous day are collected. The statistics on unpublished data assets are not collected. You can query and view a data asset only after the data asset is published. The total number of data assets and the number of data assets of each type. The data assets added in the previous month of different types. The week-on-week and month-on-month trends of data assets of different types. View the following asset trends: The accumulated number of published data assets until now, and the week-on-week and month-on-month trends of data assets. The number of data assets whose status changes from **Unpublished** to **Published** in the current month, and the week-on-week and month-on-month trends of the change. The accumulated data assets of a specific asset type in a specific cycle and the change trend. View the directories to which the data assets of a specific type are mounted and the published and updated data assets of this type. View the view ranking of data assets of a specific type in the previous month. You can unpublish the data assets with low views. For more information about how to unpublish data assets, see Manage data assets.

### Open platform overview

The DataWorks Open Platform is an open gateway to DataWorks data and capabilities. It offers OpenAPI, OpenEvent, and Extensions to help you quickly integrate your applications with DataWorks, conveniently manage data workflows, data governance, and O&M, and respond to business changes in real time. Only **Open Platform administrators** and **tenant administrators** have read and write permissions for the **Developer Center**. Other tenant-level and workspace-level roles have read-only access to the **Developer Center** page and cannot copy, display, or reset Kafka user passwords.

**Access open platform**

1. Log on to the DataWorks console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **All Products > More > Open**
**Platform** to open the **Developer Center**.

**OpenAPI**

OpenAPI lets your local services interact with DataWorks. This helps you improve big data processing efficiency, reduce manual operations and O&M efforts, and lower both data risks and business costs. For more information about OpenAPI, see the relevant topics in the **Developer Guide** for the corresponding version. ama OpenEvent provides a message subscription service that allows your applications to integrate with DataWorks. You can subscribe to DataWorks events to receive real-time status updates. This helps you respond immediately to changes and enables custom decision-making. For more information about this feature, see OpenEvent. DataWorks provides message push and subscription capabilities through OpenEvent. You can register your services as DataWorks Extensions. These Extensions can intercept and respond to subscribed event messages to implement custom notifications and workflow controls for specific events. For more information about this feature, see Extensions.

### OpenEvent

You can use Kafka to subscribe to change events such as table changes and file changes, and use DataWorks extensions to trigger checks. If a change event is reported, a check is triggered. You can handle the event based on the check results.

**Go to the Developer Backend page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
icon and choose **All Products > More >**
**Openplatform**. The **Developer Backend** page appears.

1. In the left-side navigation pane of the **Developer Backend** page, click **OpenEvent**. The
OpenEvent page appears.
2. Add a Kafka endpoint.

**Note**

DataWorks allows you to add only one Kafka endpoint. i. In the **Kafka Endpoint Information** section, click **Add Kafka Endpoint**. In the Add Kafka Endpoint dialog box, configure the parameters for the endpoint, such as Type and Protocol. ii. After the configuration is complete, click **Test Connectivity** in the **Actions** column to test the connectivity of the endpoint.
3. Add Kafka topics.

**Note**

DataWorks allows you to add up to 50 Kafka topics. i. In the **Kafka Topic Information** section, click **Add Kafka Topic**. ii. In the **Add Kafka Topic** dialog box, enter a topic name and click **OK**.

### Extensions

#### Register an extension

DataWorks allows you to register service programs as extensions and use the extensions to process subscribed events. This topic describes how to register an extension.

**Go to the Developer Backend page**

1. Log in to the DataWorks console.
2. In the upper-left corner, click the
icon and choose **All Products > More >**
**Openplatform**. The **Developer Backend** page appears.
1. In the left-side navigation pane of the **Developer Backend** page, click **Extensions** to go
to the Extensions page.
2. In the **List of Extensions** section, click **Register Extension**.
3. In the Register Extension panel, configure the parameters for the extension.
i. Select a deployment mode. In the Select Deployment Method step of the Register Extension dialog box, select
**Deploy Based on Self-managed Service** and click **Next**.
ii. Register the extension.

**Note**

During the preparation, you need to configure only the required parameters. You can configure the optional parameters after you develop and debug the extension. The required parameters include **Extension Name**, **Processed Extension Points**,
**Owner**, and **Workspace for Testing**. The rest of the parameters can be configured
after the extension is developed and deployed. The following table describes the parameters.

| Extension Name | The name of the custom extension, which is used to identify the extension. |
|---|---|
| Processed Extension Points | The type of the extension point event that you want the extension to check. You can select event types based on your actual requirements. Note After you configure this parameter, the system automatically configures the Event and Applicable Service parameters. |
| Owner | The person in charge of the extension. Users of the extension can contact the extension owner at the earliest opportunity when they encounter issues. |
| Workspace for Testing | The workspace that is used to test the extension. To check whether the extension is effective, you do not need to publish the extension because the test workspace supports an end-to-end test that allows you to check whether the extension works as expected. |
| Extension Details Address | The URL of the extension details page. After you develop and deploy the extension, you can develop a web page to display how the extension works. Set this parameter to the page URL so that users can visit this web page to better understand and use the extension. For example, users can visit the web page to check why a node is blocked by the extension. |
| Extension Documentation Address | The URL of the extension documentation page. After you develop and deploy the extension, you can develop a help documentation page. Set this parameter to the page URL so that users can know the business logic and properties of the extension. |
| Parameters for Extension | The extension parameters. To improve the extension development and application efficiency, you can enter both the built-in parameters for typical scenarios and custom parameters for future reference. You can enter multiple parameters, each occupying a separate line and defined in the format of key=value . |
| Options for Extension | The configuration item for the extension. The extension developer provides this parameter for users to implement custom process management in different workspaces based on their business requirements when the users register the extension. The extension developer must define the configuration item in JSON strings in the Register Extension dialog box. For example, the extension developer allows users to manage the length of an SQL statement based on this parameter. |

ama

| Description | The description of the extension. |
|---|---|

ama
4. Click **OK**.
After the extension is registered, you can click **Publish** in the **Actions** column to publish the extension. After the extension is published, it is available in all workspaces of the tenant. You can also click **Details**, **Modify**, **Disable**, or **Delete** in the Actions column to view the details of, modify, disable, or delete the extension.

#### Enable an extension

After you develop and deploy an extension, you can enable it in DataWorks and manage its permissions. Complete the procedure in Register an extension.

**Access the extension page**

1. Log on to the DataWorks console.
2. On the **data development** page, click the
icon in the upper-right corner.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tenant management > Extension**.
1. On the **Extension** page, configure the **effective scope**.
2. In the extension list, find the target extension and turn on the switch in the **Enable** column.
In the dialog box that appears, grant the required permissions.

**Note**

If the **Actions** column for your extension includes a **Settings** option, you can click the
**Settings** button to configure data authorization for the extension before enabling it.

## View operation logs

You can use the operation log to view and retrieve your activity records in a private cloud. These records detail your access to and use of cloud products and services through the Alibaba Cloud console, OpenAPI, and developer tools. You can export the logs to OSS based on specified query conditions for event monitoring, alerting, auditing, and root cause analysis. This topic describes how to view and export operation logs. You have obtained the service domain name for the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console from the deployment personnel. Use the Google Chrome browser. Only authorized users can access the operation log. To gain access, contact your administrator for the required permissions.

**Access the operation log**

1. In the address bar of your browser, enter the service domain name for the Apsara Uni-
manager Management Console and press Enter.

**Note**

You can click the current language in the upper-right corner to switch to another language.
2. Select **I Have Read And Agree To The Product Service Agreement, Privacy**
**Agreement, And User Agreement**.

**Note**

The link text on the logon page is the title of the agreement document. You can click the link to view the details of the agreement. The **Product Service Agreement**, **Privacy Agreement**, and **User**
**Agreement** are displayed only if they have been published. If none of these
agreements are published, you can skip this step.
3. Click **Account Logon** or **Authorized Logon**.

**Note**

The Authorized Logon button is displayed only if the global IdP setting for third-party authentication is enabled. This display name can be customized. The default name is "Authorized Logon".
4. If multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for your account, follow the steps for one of
the following scenarios:

**Note**

When you log on from the Internet, multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory by default.

**First logon after MFA is enabled**

a. After you log on with your username and password, the Bind Virtual MFA Device page appears. b. On the Bind Virtual MFA Device page, follow the on-screen instructions to bind a virtual MFA device. c. You have logged in to the console.

**MFA is already enabled and a device is bound**

Enter the six-digit MFA code and click **Authenticate**.
5. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**ActionTrail > Advanced Search** to go to the **Advanced Search** page.

**Search for DataWorks audit events**

On the **Advanced Search** page, you can filter events by criteria such as organization, product type, and source IP. To view the details of a specific event, click **View** next to the event. You can then assess potential risks based on the instance details.

**Note**

DataWorks currently supports the following two types of audit events: API-based events: For these events, the **Event Name** corresponds to the name of the API operation. Non-API events: For a list of these events, see Appendix: DataWorks audit events.

**Log storage**

If you have security and compliance requirements, you can export logs. On the **Advanced**
**Search** page, click **Export Events** above the search results. Then, in the left-side navigation
pane, choose **ActionTrail > Export History** to download the logs to your local machine.

## Basic concepts

This article explains the basic concepts in DataWorks. A workspace is the basic unit in DataWorks for managing tasks, members, roles, and permissions. A workspace administrator can add members to a workspace and assign roles such as workspace administrator, developer, O&M, Deployment, security administrator, or visitor to facilitate collaboration. A workflow consists of multiple nodes and their dependencies.

**Task**

A task is an operation performed on data. Examples include: A data synchronization Node Task synchronizes data from RDS to MaxCompute. A MaxCompute SQL Node Task runs MaxCompute SQL to transform data. Each task uses one or more tables (datasets) as input and generates one or more as output. Tasks fall into three types: Node Task, Flow Task, and Inner Node.

| Flow Task | A Flow Task groups a set of Inner Nodes for a specific business scenario. You can configure a dependency between a Flow Task and other Flow Tasks or Node Tasks to form a DAG. A Flow Task should contain fewer than 10 Inner Nodes. Note Other Flow Tasks or Node Tasks cannot depend on Inner Nodes within a Flow Task. Tasks upgraded from DataWorks V1.0 still retain the workflow concept. In DataWorks V2.0 and later, you can no longer create Flow Tasks. Instead, you can create a workflow for subsequent operations. |
|---|---|
| Inner Node | A node within a Flow Task. Its function is almost identical to that of a Node Task. You can establish dependencies between nodes by dragging and dropping them in the UI. The scheduling cycle of an Inner Node is inherited from its parent Flow Task and cannot be configured separately. |

An instance is a snapshot of a task for a specific execution. When a task is triggered, either automatically by the scheduling system or manually by a user, it generates an instance. This instance contains details about the execution, such as its runtime, status, and logs.

**Note**

The **Operation Center > Cycle Task** page shows information about an instance. For example, if Task1 is scheduled to run at 2:00 AM every day, the scheduling system automatically generates a snapshot at 11:30 PM the day before. This snapshot is the instance for the 2:00 AM run. At 2:00 AM, the Task1 instance starts if all its ancestor instances have successfully completed. Resources and functions are MaxCompute concepts. You can manage resources and functions through the DataWorks UI. If you manage them by using other MaxCompute tools, you cannot find or view them in DataWorks. An output name identifies a task's output. It is an identifier used within a single tenant (Alibaba Cloud account) to connect upstream and downstream Node Tasks when you configure a dependency. When you set the upstream and downstream dependencies for a task, you must use its output name, not the node name or node ID. Once configured, this output name also serves as the input name for its downstream nodes.

**Note**

The output name of a node must be unique within a tenant. Metadata is data that describes other data. It can specify a dataset's attributes (such as name, size, and data type), its structure (such as fields, types, and length), or related information (such as its location, owner, generating task, and access permissions). After you develop and publish a scheduled task, it runs according to its schedule. If you need to process data for a historical period, you can use the backfill feature. This action creates backfill instances that run for the specified bizdates.
